{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/backend/app/alerting/builder.py",
  "content": "\"\"\"Assemble a redacted ``RunReport`` from a completed run's persisted rows.\n\nThis is the one place that reads the ORM and applies the seam's PII policy:\n``sample_failures`` is passed through ``run_service.redact_sample_failures``\n(counts-only; raw cell values masked) before it can reach a publisher. Everything\ndownstream of here works on the DTO, never the DB rows.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom typing import Any\n\nfrom sqlalchemy import select\nfrom sqlalchemy.orm import Session\n\nfrom backend.app.alerting.base import FAILING_TIERS, CheckReport, RunReport\nfrom backend.app.db.models import Check, Connection, Result, Run, Suite\nfrom backend.app.services import run_service\n\n# Worst-first lookup so a single pass can keep the highest tier seen.\n_SEVERITY_RANK = {tier: rank for rank, tier in enumerate(FAILING_TIERS, start=1)}\n\n\ndef _worst_severity(statuses: list[str]) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"The highest failing tier among ``statuses`` (``critical`` > ``fail`` >\n    ``warn``), or ``None`` when nothing breached.\"\"\"\n    present = [s for s in statuses if s in _SEVERITY_RANK]\n    return max(present, key=lambda s: _SEVERITY_RANK[s]) if present else None\n\n\ndef _target_label(suite: Suite | None) -> str:\n    \"\"\"A human-readable one-line target for the notification.\n\n    Reads the datasource-shaped ``Suite.target`` (#215) directly rather than\n    ``run_target.resolve_target`` (which can raise on a malformed target — a\n    report must never fail to build). Flat-file targets show their ``path``;\n    SQL targets show the dotted ``catalog.schema.table``.\n    \"\"\"\n    target: dict[str, Any] = dict(suite.target) if suite and suite.target else {}\n    path = target.get(\"path\")\n    if path:\n        return str(path)\n    parts = [target.get(\"catalog\"), target.get(\"schema\"), target.get(\"table\")]\n    dotted = \".\".join(str(p) for p in parts if p)\n    return dotted or \"(no target)\"\n\n\ndef build_run_report(session: Session, run: Run) -> RunReport:\n    \"\"\"Build the redacted, GX-agnostic report for a terminal ``run``.\n\n    Joins each ``Result`` back to its ``Check`` (by id) for the check name +\n    expectation; a result whose check was since deleted degrades to a placeholder\n    name rather than failing the build. ``metric_value`` is widened ``Decimal`` →\n    ``float`` for JSON-friendly transport.\n    \"\"\"\n    suite = session.get(Suite, run.suite_id)\n    connection = session.get(Connection, suite.connection_id) if suite is not None else None\n    checks = {\n        c.id: c\n        for c in session.scalars(select(Check).where(Check.suite_id == run.suite_id))\n    }\n    results: list[Result] = run_service.list_results(session, run.id)\n\n    counts: dict[str, int] = {}\n    check_reports: list[CheckReport] = []\n    for result in results:\n        counts[result.status] = counts.get(result.status, 0) + 1\n        check = checks.get(result.check_id)\n        check_reports.append(\n            CheckReport(\n                check_name=check.name if check is not None else \"(deleted check)\",\n                expectation_type=check.expectation_type if check is not None else \"\",\n                status=result.status,\n                metric_value=(\n                    float(result.metric_value) if result.metric_value is not None else None\n                ),\n                observed_value=result.observed_value,\n                expected_value=result.expected_value,\n                # Redaction policy at the seam: counts only, never raw rows.\n                sample_summary=run_service.redact_sample_failures(result.sample_failures),\n            )\n        )\n\n    worst = _worst_severity([r.status for r in results])\n    return RunReport(\n        run_id=run.id,\n        suite_id=run.suite_id,\n        suite_name=suite.name if suite is not None else \"(deleted suite)\",\n        run_status=run.status,\n        datasource_type=connection.type if connection is not None else \"\",\n        target_label=_target_label(suite),\n        success=run.status == \"succeeded\" and worst is None,\n        worst_severity=worst,\n        counts=counts,\n        checks=check_reports,\n        finished_at=run.finished_at,\n    )\n"
}

  "content": "\"\"\"Resolve the configured ``ResultPublisher`` (cached after first build).\n\nMirrors ``core.secrets.get_secret_store``: a process-wide singleton built from\nsettings, with a test-only reset. v1 has only the no-op; the Teams publisher is\nwired here (gated on a configured webhook) when it lands, so callers never change.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport threading\n\nfrom backend.app.alerting.base import ResultPublisher\nfrom backend.app.alerting.noop import NoopPublisher\nfrom backend.app.core.config import Settings, get_settings\nfrom backend.app.core.logging import get_logger\n\nlog = get_logger(__name__)\n\n_publisher_singleton: ResultPublisher | None = None\n_publisher_lock = threading.Lock()\n\n\ndef _build_publisher(settings: Settings) -> ResultPublisher:\n    \"\"\"Pick the publisher from settings. v1: always the no-op (the Teams branch\n    lands with the Teams publisher, gated on a configured webhook).\"\"\"\n    return NoopPublisher()\n\n\ndef get_result_publisher() -> ResultPublisher:\n    \"\"\"Return the configured publisher (built once, then cached).\"\"\"\n    global _publisher_singleton\n    if _publisher_singleton is not None:\n        return _publisher_singleton\n    with _publisher_lock:\n        if _publisher_singleton is None:\n            _publisher_singleton = _build_publisher(get_settings())\n            log.info(\"result_publisher_initialized\", impl=type(_publisher_singleton).__name__)\n        return _publisher_singleton\n\n\ndef reset_result_publisher_cache() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Test-only: clear the cached publisher so the next call rebuilds it.\"\"\"\n    global _publisher_singleton\n    with _publisher_lock:\n        _publisher_singleton = None\n"

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/backend/app/alerting/dispatch.py",
  "content": "\"\"\"The run-completion hook: build a run's report and hand it to the publisher.\n\nCalled from the worker right after a run reaches a terminal state. It is\n**best-effort and never raises** — the run is already persisted, so a broken /\nslow notification channel must not fail the task or roll anything back. Only\nruns that actually executed (``succeeded``/``failed``) are published; a\n``cancelled`` run is user-initiated and not alert-worthy.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport uuid\n\nfrom sqlalchemy.orm import Session\n\nfrom backend.app.alerting.builder import build_run_report\nfrom backend.app.alerting.registry import get_result_publisher\nfrom backend.app.core.logging import get_logger\nfrom backend.app.db.models import Run\n\nlog = get_logger(__name__)\n\n# Terminal statuses worth notifying on. `cancelled` is excluded (user-initiated);\n# `queued`/`running` are non-terminal so they never reach here.\n_PUBLISHABLE_STATUSES = frozenset({\"succeeded\", \"failed\"})\n\n\ndef publish_run_outcome(session: Session, *, run_id: uuid.UUID) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Publish ``run_id``'s outcome through the configured publisher.\n\n    Returns whether a report was dispatched (``False`` when the run is missing,\n    not in a publishable state, or a failure was swallowed). Any exception —\n    building the report or the publisher itself — is logged and contained.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        run = session.get(Run, run_id)\n        if run is None or run.status not in _PUBLISHABLE_STATUSES:\n            return False\n        report = build_run_report(session, run)\n        get_result_publisher().publish(report)\n        return True\n    except Exception:\n        log.exception(\"result_publish_failed\", run_id=str(run_id))\n        return False\n"
}

"""Tests for the dashboard aggregates service.

Two layers: the pure ADR-0005 health-score math (no DB), and the DB-backed
summary aggregation — scoping (owned-or-shared only), the window cutoff, the
run trend zero-fill, and per-suite performance from the latest run. Skips
without TEST_DATABASE_URL.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
from itertools import pairwise
from typing import Any

import pytest

from backend.app.db.models import Check, Connection, Result, Run, Share, Suite, User
from backend.app.services import dashboard_service as svc

# ── pure health-score / pass-rate / state (ADR 0005) ─────────────────────────


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("counts", "expected"),
    [
        ({"pass": 4}, 100.0),
        ({"fail": 4}, 50.0),
        ({"warn": 4}, 75.0),
        ({"critical": 4}, 0.0),
        ({"fail": 2, "pass": 2}, 75.0),  # the ADR's worked example
        ({"pass": 1, "warn": 1, "fail": 1, "critical": 1}, 56.2),  # (0+.5+1+2)/(4*2)=.4375
        ({}, None),
        ({"skip": 3, "error": 2}, None),  # non-severity statuses excluded → N=0
    ],
)
def test_health_score(counts: dict[str, int], expected: float | None) -> None:
    assert svc.health_score(counts) == expected


def test_health_score_excludes_skip_and_error_from_n() -> None:
    # skip/error don't dilute the score — {pass, fail} alone is 75, with skip/error too.
    assert svc.health_score({"pass": 1, "fail": 1}) == 75.0
    assert svc.health_score({"pass": 1, "fail": 1, "skip": 10, "error": 5}) == 75.0


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("counts", "expected"),
    [
        ({"pass": 4}, 100.0),
        ({"pass": 1, "fail": 3}, 25.0),
        ({}, None),
        ({"skip": 5}, None),
    ],
)
def test_pass_rate(counts: dict[str, int], expected: float | None) -> None:
    assert svc.pass_rate(counts) == expected

No real correctness bugs found. Summary of what I verified:

- **Session lifecycle (the main cross-file concern): safe.** Every return path in `_run_suite` commits before returning — `_terminal_failed` commits, `execute_run` commits on both success and failure (with `rollback()` before the failed-state commit), `skip_run` commits. So when `publish_run_outcome` reuses the same session, the transaction is always clean and the terminal run row is committed. No publish runs on a dirty/rolled-back session.
- **Status gating: correct.** `_PUBLISHABLE_STATUSES = {"succeeded","failed"}` excludes `cancelled` (user-initiated, returns early in `_run_suite`), `not_found` (no run row — `session.get` returns None → False), and `running`/`queued` (non-terminal). A `BatchNotFoundError` skip sets the run to `succeeded` with all checks `skip`ped, which correctly publishes with `success=True`, `worst_severity=None`, `has_failures=False`.
- **Monkeypatch correctness: works.** `dispatch.py` calls `registry.get_result_publisher()` through the imported module object, and `test_dispatch.py` patches `registry.get_result_publisher` — late attribute lookup on the module means the patch takes effect.
- **Redaction: no PII leak.** `builder.py` routes `sample_failures` through `run_service.redact_sample_failures` (value-based allowlist masking, the established seam). `observed_value`/`expected_value` are GX aggregates, JSON-sanitized at write time — passing them through is consistent with documented intent.
- **Derivations: match documented intent.** `failed_checks` = fail+critical (warn excluded), `has_failures` true on warn or run-failed, `worst_severity` ranks critical>fail>warn and is None for clean/`skip`/`error`, `success` = succeeded AND no breach. Tests cover the warn-only, all-pass, run-failed-no-results, and skip/error-not-a-failure cases.
- **Concurrency:** registry singleton + lock mirrors `core/secrets.get_secret_store` (double-checked locking), correct.
- **Decimal→float:** `metric_value` is widened only when not None; falsy-zero is handled (`is not None`).
- **Exception isolation:** `publish_run_outcome` wraps everything in try/except and never raises, so a broken channel cannot fail the task or the persisted run.

  "content": "\"\"\"Render a ``RunReport`` as a Microsoft Teams message (Adaptive Card).\n\nPure: the boundary DTO in, the JSON body a Teams incoming webhook accepts out —\nno I/O, no GX, no ORM. The card carries what an on-call needs to triage a failed\nrun: suite + datasource + target, the pass/fail tally, and per-failing-check\nobserved-vs-expected. Everything here is already redacted upstream\n(``CheckReport.sample_summary`` is counts-only; raw rows never reach the seam),\nso the renderer can format every field without a second PII pass.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom typing import Any\n\nfrom backend.app.alerting.base import FAILING_TIERS, CheckReport, RunReport\n\n# Teams' incoming-webhook (Workflows) body shape: a message wrapping one or more\n# adaptive-card attachments.\n_ADAPTIVE_CARD_VERSION = \"1.4\"\n_ADAPTIVE_CARD_SCHEMA = \"http://adaptivecards.io/schemas/adaptive-card.json\"\n_CARD_CONTENT_TYPE = \"application/vnd.microsoft.card.adaptive\"\n\n# Keep the card a sane size — a suite with hundreds of failing checks shouldn't\n# produce a multi-megabyte card. Overflow is summarised as \"+N more\".\n_MAX_CHECK_ROWS = 10\n\n# Worst-severity → accent colour for the title (Adaptive Card named colours).\n_SEVERITY_COLOR = {\"critical\": \"attention\", \"fail\": \"attention\", \"warn\": \"warning\"}\n\n\ndef render_teams_message(report: RunReport) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    \"\"\"The full Teams webhook payload for ``report`` (message + adaptive card).\"\"\"\n    return {\n        \"type\": \"message\",\n        \"attachments\": [\n            {\"contentType\": _CARD_CONTENT_TYPE, \"content\": _adaptive_card(report)},\n        ],\n    }\n\n\ndef _adaptive_card(report: RunReport) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    body: list[dict[str, Any]] = [_title_block(report), _subtitle_block(report), _facts_block(report)]\n    failing = [c for c in report.checks if c.status in FAILING_TIERS]\n    if failing:\n        body.append(_text(\"Failing checks\", weight=\"Bolder\", spacing=\"Medium\"))\n        body.extend(_check_block(c) for c in failing[:_MAX_CHECK_ROWS])\n        overflow = len(failing) - _MAX_CHECK_ROWS\n        if overflow > 0:\n            body.append(_text(f\"+{overflow} more\", is_subtle=True))\n    return {\n        \"type\": \"AdaptiveCard\",\n        \"$schema\": _ADAPTIVE_CARD_SCHEMA,\n        \"version\": _ADAPTIVE_CARD_VERSION,\n        \"body\": body,\n    }\n\n\ndef _title_block(report: RunReport) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    color = _SEVERITY_COLOR.get(report.worst_severity or \"\", \"attention\")\n    return _text(report.suite_name, size=\"Large\", weight=\"Bolder\", color=color)\n\n\ndef _subtitle_block(report: RunReport) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    # An operational run failure (adapter raised) has no result rows to tally.\n    if report.run_status == \"failed\" and not report.checks:\n        return _text(\"Run failed to execute\", is_subtle=True)\n    return _text(\n        f\"{report.failed_checks} of {report.total_checks} checks failed\", is_subtle=True\n    )\n\n\ndef _facts_block(report: RunReport) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    facts = [\n        {\"title\": \"Datasource\", \"value\": report.datasource_type or \"—\"},\n        {\"title\": \"Target\", \"value\": report.target_label},\n        {\"title\": \"Run\", \"value\": report.run_status},\n        {\"title\": \"Severity\", \"value\": report.worst_severity or \"—\"},\n    ]\n    if report.finished_at is not None:\n        facts.append({\"title\": \"Finished\", \"value\": report.finished_at.isoformat()})\n    return {\"type\": \"FactSet\", \"facts\": facts}\n\n\ndef _check_block(check: CheckReport) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    detail = f\"observed {_compact(check.observed_value)} vs expected {_compact(check.expected_value)}\"\n    sample = check.sample_summary or {}\n    if \"unexpected_count\" in sample:\n        detail += f\" · {sample['unexpected_count']} rows\"\n    return _text(\n        f\"**{check.check_name}** ({check.status}) — {check.expectation_type}\\n\\n{detail}\",\n        wrap=True,\n        spacing=\"Small\",\n    )\n\n\ndef _compact(value: dict[str, Any] | None) -> str:\n    \"\"\"A short ``key=val`` rendering of a small GX observed/expected dict.\"\"\"\n    if not value:\n        return \"—\"\n    return \", \".join(f\"{k}={v}\" for k, v in value.items())\n\n\ndef _text(text: str, **props: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    \"\"\"An Adaptive Card ``TextBlock``. ``is_subtle``/``weight``/``size``/``color``/\n    ``spacing``/``wrap`` map to their camelCase card properties.\"\"\"\n    block: dict[str, Any] = {\"type\": \"TextBlock\", \"text\": text}\n    if props.pop(\"wrap\", False):\n        block[\"wrap\"] = True\n    if props.pop(\"is_subtle\", False):\n        block[\"isSubtle\"] = True\n    for key in (\"weight\", \"size\", \"color\", \"spacing\"):\n        if key in props:\n            block[key] = props[key]\n    return block\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/backend/app/alerting/teams.py",
  "content": "\"\"\"The v1 ``ResultPublisher`` — posts a run's report as a Teams Adaptive Card.\n\nThe webhook URL is resolved **per report** by an injected resolver, not baked\ninto the publisher: v1 resolves a single workspace webhook, and per-suite\nnotification config (a later PR) extends the resolver without touching the\npublisher or the seam. A run with nothing to report, or no webhook for its suite,\nis a quiet no-op — alerts are for failures, not green runs.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\n\nimport httpx\n\nfrom backend.app.alerting.base import RunReport\nfrom backend.app.alerting.card import render_teams_message\nfrom backend.app.core.logging import get_logger\n\nlog = get_logger(__name__)\n\n# Resolve the Teams webhook URL for a given run (None → no channel, skip).\nWebhookResolver = Callable[[RunReport], str | None]\n\n_POST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 10.0\n\n\nclass TeamsPublisher:\n    \"\"\"Posts an Adaptive Card to the webhook the resolver returns for the run.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(\n        self, resolve_webhook: WebhookResolver, *, timeout: float = _POST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS\n    ) -> None:\n        self._resolve_webhook = resolve_webhook\n        self._timeout = timeout\n\n    def publish(self, report: RunReport) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Send the run's card, if it has failures and a webhook is configured.\n\n        Raises on an HTTP error — the dispatch layer isolates that so a flaky\n        webhook can't fail the run. A clean run (nothing breached) or an\n        unresolved webhook is a silent no-op, not a send.\n        \"\"\"\n        if not report.has_failures:\n            return\n        webhook = self._resolve_webhook(report)\n        if not webhook:\n            return\n        message = render_teams_message(report)\n        response = httpx.post(webhook, json=message, timeout=self._timeout)\n        response.raise_for_status()\n        log.info(\n            \"teams_alert_sent\",\n            run_id=str(report.run_id),\n            suite=report.suite_name,\n            worst_severity=report.worst_severity,\n            failed_checks=report.failed_checks,\n        )\n"
}

the redacted sample count\n    # Exactly one failing-check block (the passing check is excluded).\n    assert sum(\"not-null id\" in t for t in texts) == 1\n\n\ndef test_operational_failure_has_no_check_tally() -> None:\n    content = card.render_teams_message(\n        _report(run_status=\"failed\", checks=[], counts={}, worst=None)\n    )[\"attachments\"][0][\"content\"]\n    texts = [b.get(\"text\", \"\") for b in content[\"body\"] if b[\"type\"] == \"TextBlock\"]\n    assert any(\"Run failed to execute\" in t for t in texts)\n\n\ndef test_check_overflow_is_summarised() -> None:\n    content = card.render_teams_message(\n        _report(checks=[_check() for _ in range(13)])\n    )[\"attachments\"][0][\"content\"]\n    texts = [b.get(\"text\", \"\") for b in content[\"body\"] if b[\"type\"] == \"TextBlock\"]\n    # 10 rows rendered + a \"+3 more\".\n    assert sum(\"not-null id\" in t for t in texts) == 10\n    assert any(\"+3 more\" in t for t in texts)\n\n\ndef test_compact_handles_empty() -> None:\n    assert card._compact(None) == \"—\"\n    assert card._compact({}) == \"—\"\n    assert card._compact({\"a\": 1, \"b\": 2}) == \"a=1, b=2\"\n"

None = \"fail\", run_status: str = \"succeeded\") -> RunReport:\n    return RunReport(\n        run_id=uuid.uuid4(),\n        suite_id=uuid.uuid4(),\n        suite_name=\"s\",\n        run_status=run_status,\n        datasource_type=\"snowflake\",\n        target_label=\"T\",\n        worst_severity=worst,\n        counts={\"fail\": 1} if worst else {\"pass\": 1},\n        checks=[\n            CheckReport(\n                check_name=\"c\",\n                expectation_type=\"e\",\n                status=worst or \"pass\",\n                metric_value=None,\n                observed_value=None,\n                expected_value=None,\n                sample_summary=None,\n            )\n        ],\n        finished_at=None,\n    )\n\n\nclass _CapturePost:\n    def __init__(self, *, status_code: int = 200) -> None:\n        self.calls: list[dict[str, Any]] = []\n        self._status_code = status_code\n\n    def __call__(self, url: str, *, json: dict[str, Any], timeout: float) -> httpx.Response:\n        self.calls.append({\"url\": url, \"json\": json, \"timeout\": timeout})\n        return httpx.Response(self._status_code, request=httpx.Request(\"POST\", url))\n\n\ndef test_posts_card_to_resolved_webhook(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:\n    post = _CapturePost()\n    monkeypatch.setattr(teams.httpx, \"post\", post)\n    publisher = TeamsPublisher(lambda _r: \"https://teams.example/hook\")\n\n    publisher.publish(_report(worst=\"fail\"))\n\n    assert len(post.calls) == 1\n    call = post.calls[0]\n    assert call[\"url\"] == \"https://teams.example/hook\"\n    assert call[\"json\"][\"type\"] == \"message\"\n    assert call[\"json\"][\"attachments\"][0][\"content\"][\"type\"] == \"AdaptiveCard\"\n\n\ndef test_clean_run_does_not_send(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:\n    post = _CapturePost()\n    monkeypatch.setattr(teams.httpx, \"post\", post)\n    TeamsPublisher(lambda _r: \"https://teams.example/hook\").publish(_report(worst=None))\n    assert post.calls == []\n\n\ndef test_unresolved_webhook_does_not_send(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:\n    post = _CapturePost()\n    monkeypatch.setattr(teams.httpx, \"post\", post)\n    TeamsPublisher(lambda _r: None).publish(_report(worst=\"fail\"))\n    assert post.calls == []\n\n\ndef test_http_error_propagates_for_dispatch_isolation(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:\n    # A 4xx/5xx must raise so the dispatch layer (not the publisher) decides to\n    # swallow it — the publisher is not allowed to silently eat a delivery failure.\n    monkeypatch.setattr(teams.httpx, \"post\", _CapturePost(status_code=500))\n    with pytest.raises(httpx.HTTPStatusError):\n        TeamsPublisher(lambda _r: \"https://teams.example/hook\").publish(_report(worst=\"critical\"))\n"

  "content": "\"\"\"Severity-aware routing — *whether* and *how loudly* to alert on a run.\n\nThe single policy point between a built ``RunReport`` and the channel: it maps\nthe run's worst severity to a ``Route`` (send-or-not + urgency + whether to\nescalate to the whole channel). The publisher delegates the send decision here,\nand the card renders the urgency, so \"warn is quiet, fail is standard, critical\npings the channel\" lives in one place rather than smeared across the publisher\nand the renderer.\n\nPer-suite policy (alert on fail / warn / always) extends this in a later PR by\nfolding the suite's preference into ``route_for`` — the publisher and card don't\nchange.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\n# Urgency levels, quietest first. The card maps these to colour + escalation.\nQUIET = \"quiet\"\nSTANDARD = \"standard\"\nCRITICAL = \"critical\"\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Route:\n    \"\"\"The routing decision for one run.\n\n    ``should_send`` gates delivery (a clean run is ``False``); ``urgency`` drives\n    the card's prominence; ``mention_channel`` escalates a critical breach to the\n    whole channel.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    should_send: bool\n    urgency: str\n    mention_channel: bool\n\n\n_NO_SEND = Route(should_send=False, urgency=QUIET, mention_channel=False)\n\n\ndef route_for(report: \"RunReport\") -> Route:  # noqa: F821 — forward ref, imported below for typing\n    \"\"\"Decide how to route ``report`` from its worst severity.\n\n    - **critical** → send, critical urgency, escalate to the channel.\n    - **fail** (or an operational run failure with no result rows) → send,\n      standard urgency.\n    - **warn** → send, quiet urgency (no escalation).\n    - otherwise (all clean) → don't send.\n    \"\"\"\n    if report.worst_severity == CRITICAL:\n        return Route(should_send=True, urgency=CRITICAL, mention_channel=True)\n    if report.worst_severity == \"fail\" or report.run_status == \"failed\":\n        return Route(should_send=True, urgency=STANDARD, mention_channel=False)\n    if report.worst_severity == \"warn\":\n        return Route(should_send=True, urgency=QUIET, mention_channel=False)\n    return _NO_SEND\n\n\nfrom backend.app.alerting.base import RunReport  # noqa: E402 — late import avoids a base↔routing cycle\n"
}

Overflow is summarised as \"+N more\".\n_MAX_CHECK_ROWS = 10\n\n# Worst-severity → accent colour for the title (Adaptive Card named colours).\n_SEVERITY_COLOR = {\"critical\": \"attention\", \"fail\": \"attention\", \"warn\": \"warning\"}\n\n\ndef render_teams_message(report: RunReport) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    \"\"\"The full Teams webhook payload for ``report`` (message + adaptive card).\"\"\"\n    return {\n        \"type\": \"message\",\n        \"attachments\": [\n            {\"contentType\": _CARD_CONTENT_TYPE, \"content\": _adaptive_card(report)},\n        ],\n    }\n\n\ndef _adaptive_card(report: RunReport) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    body: list[dict[str, Any]] = [\n        _title_block(report),\n        _subtitle_block(report),\n        _facts_block(report),\n    ]\n    failing = [c for c in report.checks if c.status in FAILING_TIERS]\n    if failing:\n        body.append(_text(\"Failing checks\", weight=\"Bolder\", spacing=\"Medium\"))\n        body.extend(_check_block(c) for c in failing[:_MAX_CHECK_ROWS])\n        overflow = len(failing) - _MAX_CHECK_ROWS\n        if overflow > 0:\n            body.append(_text(f\"+{overflow} more\", is_subtle=True))\n    return {\n        \"type\": \"AdaptiveCard\",\n        \"$schema\": _ADAPTIVE_CARD_SCHEMA,\n        \"version\": _ADAPTIVE_CARD_VERSION,\n        \"body\": body,\n    }\n\n\ndef _title_block(report: RunReport) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    color = _SEVERITY_COLOR.get(report.worst_severity or \"\", \"attention\")\n    return _text(report.suite_name, size=\"Large\", weight=\"Bolder\", color=color)",
  "new_string": "from backend.app.alerting.base import FAILING_TIERS, CheckReport, RunReport\nfrom backend.app.alerting.routing import QUIET, Route\n\n# Teams' incoming-webhook (Workflows) body shape: a message wrapping one or more\n# adaptive-card attachments.\n_ADAPTIVE_CARD_VERSION = \"1.4\"\n_ADAPTIVE_CARD_SCHEMA = \"http://adaptivecards.io/schemas/adaptive-card.json\"\n_CARD_CONTENT_TYPE = \"application/vnd.microsoft.card.adaptive\"\n\n# Keep the card a sane size — a suite with hundreds of failing checks shouldn't\n# produce a multi-megabyte card. Overflow is summarised as \"+N more\".\n_MAX_CHECK_ROWS = 10\n\n# Routing urgency → title accent colour (Adaptive Card named colours). A quiet\n# (warn) alert is amber and calm; standard/critical are red.\n_URGENCY_COLOR = {QUIET: \"warning\"}\n_DEFAULT_COLOR = \"attention\"\n\n\ndef render_teams_message(report: RunReport, route: Route) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    \"\"\"The full Teams webhook payload for ``report`` (message + adaptive card).\n\n    ``route`` (from ``routing.route_for``) sets the prominence: the title colour\n    follows the urgency, and a critical ``mention_channel`` adds a channel-escalation\n    banner at the top.\n    \"\"\"\n    return {\n        \"type\": \"message\",\n        \"attachments\": [\n            {\"contentType\": _CARD_CONTENT_TYPE, \"content\": _adaptive_card(report, route)},\n        ],\n    }\n\n\ndef _adaptive_card(report: RunReport, route: Route) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    body: list[dict[str, Any]] = []\n    if route.mention_channel:\n        body.append(_text(\"@channel · CRITICAL\", weight=\"Bolder\", color=\"attention\"))\n    body += [_title_block(report, route), _subtitle_block(report), _facts_block(report)]\n    failing = [c for c in report.checks if c.status in FAILING_TIERS]\n    if failing:\n        body.append(_text(\"Failing checks\", weight=\"Bolder\", spacing=\"Medium\"))\n        body.extend(_check_block(c) for c in failing[:_MAX_CHECK_ROWS])\n        overflow = len(failing) - _MAX_CHECK_ROWS\n        if overflow > 0:\n            body.append(_text(f\"+{overflow} more\", is_subtle=True))\n    return {\n        \"type\": \"AdaptiveCard\",\n        \"$schema\": _ADAPTIVE_CARD_SCHEMA,\n        \"version\": _ADAPTIVE_CARD_VERSION,\n        \"body\": body,\n    }\n\n\ndef _title_block(report: RunReport, route: Route) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    color = _URGENCY_COLOR.get(route.urgency, _DEFAULT_COLOR)\n    return _text(report.suite_name, size=\"Large\", weight=\"Bolder\", color=color)"
}

A clean run (nothing breached) or an\n        unresolved webhook is a silent no-op, not a send.\n        \"\"\"\n        if not report.has_failures:\n            return\n        webhook = self._resolve_webhook(report)\n        if not webhook:\n            return\n        message = render_teams_message(report)\n        response = httpx.post(webhook, json=message, timeout=self._timeout)\n        response.raise_for_status()\n        log.info(\n            \"teams_alert_sent\",\n            run_id=str(report.run_id),\n            suite=report.suite_name,\n            worst_severity=report.worst_severity,\n            failed_checks=report.failed_checks,\n        )",

Raises on an HTTP error — the dispatch layer isolates\n        that so a flaky webhook can't fail the run; an unresolved webhook is a\n        silent no-op.\n        \"\"\"\n        route = route_for(report)\n        if not route.should_send:\n            return\n        webhook = self._resolve_webhook(report)\n        if not webhook:\n            return\n        message = render_teams_message(report, route)\n        response = httpx.post(webhook, json=message, timeout=self._timeout)\n        response.raise_for_status()\n        log.info(\n            \"teams_alert_sent\",\n            run_id=str(report.run_id),\n            suite=report.suite_name,\n            worst_severity=report.worst_severity,\n            urgency=route.urgency,\n            failed_checks=report.failed_checks,\n        )"

  "content": "\"\"\"Tests for severity-aware routing — the send/urgency/escalation decision.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport uuid\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom backend.app.alerting.base import RunReport\nfrom backend.app.alerting.routing import CRITICAL, QUIET, STANDARD, route_for\n\n\ndef _report(*, worst: str | None, run_status: str = \"succeeded\") -> RunReport:\n    return RunReport(\n        run_id=uuid.uuid4(),\n        suite_id=uuid.uuid4(),\n        suite_name=\"s\",\n        run_status=run_status,\n        datasource_type=\"snowflake\",\n        target_label=\"T\",\n        worst_severity=worst,\n        counts={worst: 1} if worst else {\"pass\": 1},\n        checks=[],\n        finished_at=None,\n    )\n\n\ndef test_critical_sends_and_escalates() -> None:\n    route = route_for(_report(worst=\"critical\"))\n    assert route.should_send is True\n    assert route.urgency == CRITICAL\n    assert route.mention_channel is True\n\n\ndef test_fail_sends_standard_no_escalation() -> None:\n    route = route_for(_report(worst=\"fail\"))\n    assert route.should_send is True\n    assert route.urgency == STANDARD\n    assert route.mention_channel is False\n\n\ndef test_warn_sends_quiet() -> None:\n    route = route_for(_report(worst=\"warn\"))\n    assert route.should_send is True\n    assert route.urgency == QUIET\n    assert route.mention_channel is False\n\n\ndef test_clean_run_does_not_send() -> None:\n    route = route_for(_report(worst=None))\n    assert route.should_send is False\n    assert route.mention_channel is False\n\n\ndef test_operational_failure_routes_standard() -> None:\n    # A run that failed to execute (no result rows, no severity) is a real\n    # failure — it must still alert, at standard urgency.\n    route = route_for(_report(worst=None, run_status=\"failed\"))\n    assert route.should_send is True\n    assert route.urgency == STANDARD\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\n    (\"worst\", \"run_status\", \"sends\"),\n    [\n        (\"critical\", \"succeeded\", True),\n        (\"fail\", \"succeeded\", True),\n        (\"warn\", \"succeeded\", True),\n        (None, \"succeeded\", False),\n        (None, \"failed\", True),\n    ],\n)\ndef test_send_matrix(worst: str | None, run_status: str, sends: bool) -> None:\n    assert route_for(_report(worst=worst, run_status=run_status)).should_send is sends\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/backend/app/alerting/dedup.py",
  "content": "\"\"\"Alert dedup — fire on the *first* failure, not every subsequent run.\n\nA failing check on a scheduled suite would otherwise alert on every run while it\nstays broken. This compares a run's failing checks to the suite's **previous\nterminal run** and suppresses the alert when nothing got worse: a new alert\nfires only when a check starts failing (or escalates severity) relative to last\ntime. Recovery (a clean run) resets the baseline, so the next failure re-fires.\n\nDerived from run history — **no new state / migration**. The unit is per-check\n(by ``check_id``, not name, so a renamed check still dedups), which is why this\nreads ``results`` directly rather than the name-only ``RunReport``.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport uuid\n\nfrom sqlalchemy import select\nfrom sqlalchemy.orm import Session\n\nfrom backend.app.db.models import Result, Run\n\n# Failing severity tiers → rank (higher = worse). `pass`/`skip`/`error` aren't\n# alert-worthy and never appear here.\n_RANK = {\"warn\": 1, \"fail\": 2, \"critical\": 3}\n# An operational run failure (the adapter raised — no per-check result rows) is a\n# single suite-level failure signature, keyed by this sentinel, ranked at fail.\n_OPERATIONAL_KEY = \"__run__\"\n_OPERATIONAL_RANK = 2\n\n\ndef _failing_ranks(session: Session, run: Run) -> dict[str, int]:\n    \"\"\"The failing checks of ``run`` as ``{check_id: rank}`` (escalation-aware).\n\n    An executed run contributes its breaching per-check results; a run that\n    *failed to execute* (no results) contributes one suite-level signature so two\n    consecutive operational failures still dedup.\n    \"\"\"\n    rows = session.execute(\n        select(Result.check_id, Result.status).where(Result.run_id == run.id)\n    ).all()\n    ranks = {str(check_id): _RANK[status] for check_id, status in rows if status in _RANK}\n    if not ranks and run.status == \"failed\":\n        return {_OPERATIONAL_KEY: _OPERATIONAL_RANK}\n    return ranks\n\n\ndef _previous_terminal_run(session: Session, run: Run) -> Run | None:\n    \"\"\"The suite's most recent executed run before ``run`` (succeeded/failed).\"\"\"\n    return session.scalars(\n        select(Run)\n        .where(\n            Run.suite_id == run.suite_id,\n            Run.created_at < run.created_at,\n            Run.status.in_((\"succeeded\", \"failed\")),\n        )\n        .order_by(Run.created_at.desc(), Run.id.desc())\n        .limit(1)\n    ).first()\n\n\ndef is_duplicate_alert(session: Session, run: Run) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"True when ``run``'s alert repeats the suite's previous run (→ suppress).\n\n    Returns ``False`` (i.e. *do alert*) when:\n    - the run has no failures (not an alert at all — the publisher no-ops it),\n    - it's the suite's first terminal run (no baseline), or\n    - any failing check is **new or escalated** vs the previous run.\n\n    Returns ``True`` only when every current failure was already present at the\n    same-or-higher severity last run — an ongoing, unchanged failure.\n    \"\"\"\n    current = _failing_ranks(session, run)\n    if not current:\n        return False  # clean run — nothing to dedup\n    previous_run = _previous_terminal_run(session, run)\n    if previous_run is None:\n        return False  # first-ever run of the suite → always fire\n    previous = _failing_ranks(session, previous_run)\n    # New alert if any failing check is worse than (or absent in) the prior run.\n    return not any(rank > previous.get(key, 0) for key, rank in current.items())\n"
}

1	"""The run-completion hook: build a run's report and hand it to the publisher.
2	
3	Called from the worker right after a run reaches a terminal state. It is
4	**best-effort and never raises** — the run is already persisted, so a broken /
5	slow notification channel must not fail the task or roll anything back. Only
6	runs that actually executed (``succeeded``/``failed``) are published; a
7	``cancelled`` run is user-initiated and not alert-worthy.
8	"""
9	
10	from __future__ import annotations
11	
12	import uuid
13	
14	from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
15	
16	from backend.app.alerting import registry
17	from backend.app.alerting.builder import build_run_report
18	from backend.app.core.logging import get_logger
19	from backend.app.db.models import Run
20	
21	log = get_logger(__name__)
22	
23	# Terminal statuses worth notifying on. `cancelled` is excluded (user-initiated);
24	# `queued`/`running` are non-terminal so they never reach here.
25	_PUBLISHABLE_STATUSES = frozenset({"succeeded", "failed"})
26	
27	
28	def publish_run_outcome(session: Session, *, run_id: uuid.UUID) -> bool:
29	    """Publish ``run_id``'s outcome through the configured publisher.
30	
31	    Returns whether a report was dispatched (``False`` when the run is missing,
32	    not in a publishable state, or a failure was swallowed). Any exception —
33	    building the report or the publisher itself — is logged and contained.
34	    """
35	    try:
36	        run = session.get(Run, run_id)
37	        if run is None or run.status not in _PUBLISHABLE_STATUSES:
38	            return False
39	        report = build_run_report(session, run)
40	        registry.get_result_publisher().publish(report)
41	        return True
42	    except Exception:
43	        log.exception("result_publish_failed", run_id=str(run_id))
44	        return False
45

Skips without TEST_DATABASE_URL.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport uuid\nfrom datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta\nfrom typing import Any\n\nfrom backend.app.alerting import dedup\nfrom backend.app.db.models import Check, Connection, Result, Run, Suite, User\n\n\ndef _suite(db: Any) -> Suite:\n    owner = User(aad_object_id=uuid.uuid4().hex, email=f\"u-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}@x.io\")\n    db.add(owner)\n    db.flush()\n    conn = Connection(\n        name=f\"c-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}\",\n        type=\"snowflake\",\n        env=\"dev\",\n        config={\"account\": \"a\"},\n        secret_ref=\"kv\",\n        created_by=owner.id,\n    )\n    db.add(conn)\n    db.flush()\n    suite = Suite(name=\"s\", connection_id=conn.id, created_by=owner.id, target={\"table\": \"T\"})\n    db.add(suite)\n    db.flush()\n    return suite\n\n\ndef _check(db: Any, suite: Suite) -> Check:\n    check = Check(suite_id=suite.id, name=f\"c-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}\", expectation_type=\"e\", config={})\n    db.add(check)\n    db.flush()\n    return check\n\n\n# Monotonic run timestamps so \"previous run\" is unambiguous.\n_BASE = datetime(2026, 6, 26, 0, 0, tzinfo=UTC)\n\n\ndef _run(db: Any, suite: Suite, *, seq: int, status: str = \"succeeded\") -> Run:\n    run = Run(suite_id=suite.id, status=status, created_at=_BASE + timedelta(minutes=seq))\n    db.add(run)\n    db.flush()\n    return run\n\n\ndef _result(db: Any, run: Run, check: Check, status: str) -> None:\n    db.add(Result(run_id=run.id, check_id=check.id, status=status))\n    db.flush()\n\n\ndef test_first_failure_fires(db_session: Any) -> None:\n    suite = _suite(db_session)\n    chk = _check(db_session, suite)\n    run = _run(db_session, suite, seq=1)\n    _result(db_session, run, chk, \"fail\")\n    db_session.commit()\n    # No previous terminal run → not a duplicate → fire.\n    assert dedup.is_duplicate_alert(db_session, run) is False\n\n\ndef test_unchanged_repeat_is_suppressed(db_session: Any) -> None:\n    suite = _suite(db_session)\n    chk = _check(db_session, suite)\n    r1 = _run(db_session, suite, seq=1)\n    _result(db_session, r1, chk, \"fail\")\n    r2 = _run(db_session, suite, seq=2)\n    _result(db_session, r2, chk, \"fail\")\n    db_session.commit()\n    # Same check still failing at the same severity → duplicate → suppress.\n    assert dedup.is_duplicate_alert(db_session, r2) is True\n\n\ndef test_escalation_fires(db_session: Any) -> None:\n    suite = _suite(db_session)\n    chk = _check(db_session, suite)\n    r1 = _run(db_session, suite, seq=1)\n    _result(db_session, r1, chk, \"fail\")\n    r2 = _run(db_session, suite, seq=2)\n    _result(db_session, r2, chk, \"critical\")\n    db_session.commit()\n    # fail → critical is worse → fire.\n    assert dedup.is_duplicate_alert(db_session, r2) is False\n\n\ndef test_new_failing_check_fires(db_session: Any) -> None:\n    suite = _suite(db_session)\n    a, b = _check(db_session, suite), _check(db_session, suite)\n    r1 = _run(db_session, suite, seq=1)\n    _result(db_session, r1, a, \"fail\")\n    _result(db_session, r1, b, \"pass\")\n    r2 = _run(db_session, suite, seq=2)\n    _result(db_session, r2, a, \"fail\")\n    _result(db_session, r2, b, \"fail\")  # b newly fails at the same overall worst\n    db_session.commit()\n    # b is a *new* failing check even though the worst severity is unchanged.\n    assert dedup.is_duplicate_alert(db_session, r2) is False\n\n\ndef test_recovery_then_failure_refires(db_session: Any) -> None:\n    suite = _suite(db_session)\n    chk = _check(db_session, suite)\n    r1 = _run(db_session, suite, seq=1)\n    _result(db_session, r1, chk, \"fail\")\n    r2 = _run(db_session, suite, seq=2)  # recovered\n    _result(db_session, r2, chk, \"pass\")\n    r3 = _run(db_session, suite, seq=3)  # fails again\n    _result(db_session, r3, chk, \"fail\")\n    db_session.commit()\n    # The previous run (r2) was clean → this failure is new again → fire.\n    assert dedup.is_duplicate_alert(db_session, r3) is False\n\n\ndef test_de_escalation_is_suppressed(db_session: Any) -> None:\n    suite = _suite(db_session)\n    chk = _check(db_session, suite)\n    r1 = _run(db_session, suite, seq=1)\n    _result(db_session, r1, chk, \"critical\")\n    r2 = _run(db_session, suite, seq=2)\n    _result(db_session, r2, chk, \"warn\")\n    db_session.commit()\n    # Improving (critical → warn) is not a new alert → suppress.\n    assert dedup.is_duplicate_alert(db_session, r2) is True\n\n\ndef test_clean_run_is_never_a_duplicate(db_session: Any) -> None:\n    suite = _suite(db_session)\n    chk = _check(db_session, suite)\n    r1 = _run(db_session, suite, seq=1)\n    _result(db_session, r1, chk, \"fail\")\n    r2 = _run(db_session, suite, seq=2)\n    _result(db_session, r2, chk, \"pass\")\n    db_session.commit()\n    # A passing run isn't an alert at all → not a duplicate (publisher no-ops it).\n    assert dedup.is_duplicate_alert(db_session, r2) is False\n\n\ndef test_repeated_operational_failure_is_suppressed(db_session: Any) -> None:\n    suite = _suite(db_session)\n    r1 = _run(db_session, suite, seq=1, status=\"failed\")  # no result rows\n    r2 = _run(db_session, suite, seq=2, status=\"failed\")\n    db_session.commit()\n    assert dedup.is_duplicate_alert(db_session, r1) is False  # first\n    assert dedup.is_duplicate_alert(db_session, r2) is True  # repeat\n"
}

## Summary

I reviewed the dedup logic in depth, tracing the actual run/result data shapes (`execute_run`, `skip_run`, `_terminal_failed`, `_build_result`) to ground each scenario, not just the dedup code in isolation.

**The core dedup decision (`return not any(rank > previous.get(key, 0) ...)`) is logically correct** for "fire on first failure / new check / escalation; suppress unchanged or improving." The per-check-id keying, the recovery-resets-baseline behavior, and the operational-failure sentinel all hold up under the test matrix.

**Key finding that clears a worry in the prompt:** the "operational failure with data rows present" ambiguity is moot in practice — runs that go `failed` via `execute_run` call `session.rollback()` and discard their partial result rows, and `_terminal_failed` writes no rows, so a `failed` run always reaches the operational branch with zero rows. The `_OPERATIONAL_KEY = "__run__"` can never collide with a `str(check_id)` UUID. So the `if not ranks` branch is correctly reached for genuine operational failures.

**The three real defects** (all relatively low-to-medium severity, none a confirmed routine silent-drop in the common path):
1. All-`error`/`skip` `succeeded` runs have no dedup signature — benign now, latent if routing ever alerts on them.
2. `created_at` ties under burst scheduling can pick the wrong baseline (strict `<` excludes same-timestamp prior runs; `created_at` is queue-time `func.now()`, not completion-time).
3. fail/critical→warn de-escalation permanently suppresses a still-failing warn state because dedup compares to the previous *run* rather than the last *alerted* state — documented as intended, but worth an explicit decision since routing does send on warn.

Relevant files: `/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/backend/app/alerting/dedup.py`, `/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/backend/app/alerting/dispatch.py`, `/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/backend/app/alerting/routing.py`, `/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/backend/app/services/run_service.py`.

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/backend/app/alerting/suppression.py",
  "content": "\"\"\"Alert suppression — honour per-check snoozes when deciding to alert.\n\nA check can be snoozed (``checks.alert_snoozed_until``) to mute its alerts for a\nwindow. This answers the one question the dispatch layer needs: *are all of this\nrun's failing checks currently snoozed?* If so, the alert is suppressed; if even\none failing check is live, the alert still fires (the operator silenced specific\nchecks, not the suite).\n\nOperational run failures (no per-check result rows) aren't per-check snoozable,\nso they're never suppressed here — they alert subject only to dedup.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom datetime import UTC, datetime\n\nfrom sqlalchemy import select\nfrom sqlalchemy.orm import Session\n\nfrom backend.app.db.models import Check, Result, Run\n\n_FAILING = frozenset({\"warn\", \"fail\", \"critical\"})\n\n\ndef all_failures_snoozed(session: Session, run: Run, *, now: datetime | None = None) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"True when every failing check on ``run`` is currently snoozed (→ suppress).\n\n    Returns ``False`` (don't suppress) when the run has no per-check failures\n    (clean or operational) or when at least one failing check is live.\n    \"\"\"\n    moment = now or datetime.now(UTC)\n    rows = session.execute(\n        select(Result.check_id, Result.status).where(Result.run_id == run.id)\n    ).all()\n    failing = {check_id for check_id, status in rows if status in _FAILING}\n    if not failing:\n        return False\n    snoozed = set(\n        session.scalars(\n            select(Check.id).where(\n                Check.id.in_(failing),\n                Check.alert_snoozed_until.is_not(None),\n                Check.alert_snoozed_until > moment,\n            )\n        )\n    )\n    return failing <= snoozed\n"
}

176	    config: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
177	    warn_threshold: Decimal | None = None,
178	    fail_threshold: Decimal | None = None,
179	    critical_threshold: Decimal | None = None,
180	    actor_id: uuid.UUID | None = None,
181	) -> Check:
182	    """Partial update, snapshotting the post-update state as a new version (#280).
183	
184	    Follows the codebase PATCH convention (connections / suites): a `None`
185	    argument means "not provided", so an omitted field is left unchanged. v1 has
186	    no clear-to-NULL path for thresholds; recreate the check to drop one.
187	    """
188	    check = get_check(session, suite_id, check_id)
189	    if name is not None:
190	        check.name = name
191	    if expectation_type is not None:
192	        check.expectation_type = expectation_type
193	    if config is not None:
194	        check.config = config
195	    if warn_threshold is not None:
196	        check.warn_threshold = warn_threshold
197	    if fail_threshold is not None:
198	        check.fail_threshold = fail_threshold
199	    if critical_threshold is not None:
200	        check.critical_threshold = critical_threshold
201	    # Re-validate against the post-patch state: a PATCH may change only the query
202	    # (config) or only the type, so guard the effective custom-SQL check before
203	    # commit (a rejected update persists nothing).
204	    if is_custom_sql(check.expectation_type):
205	        suite = get_suite(session, suite_id)
206	        validate_custom_sql_check(
207	            expectation_type=check.expectation_type,
208	            config=check.config,
209	            connection_type=_connection_type(session, suite),
210	        )
211	    # Only snapshot a real change: a no-op PATCH (empty body, or fields set to
212	    # their current values) must not mint a duplicate version — that would fill
213	    # the history drawer with noise and defeat "see previous config". SQLAlchemy
214	    # reports net changes, so setting a field to its existing value isn't dirty.
215	    if session.is_modified(check):
216	        record_check_version(session, check, actor_id=actor_id)
217	    session.commit()
218	    session.refresh(check)
219	    log.info("check_updated", check_id=str(check.id))
220	    return check
221	
222	
223	def delete_check(session: Session, suite_id: uuid.UUID, check_id: uuid.UUID) -> None:
224	    check = get_check(session, suite_id, check_id)
225	    session.delete(check)
226	    session.commit()
227	    log.info("check_deleted", check_id=str(check_id))
228

DB-backed.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport uuid\nfrom datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta\nfrom typing import Any\n\nfrom backend.app.alerting import suppression\nfrom backend.app.db.models import Check, Connection, Result, Run, Suite, User\n\n_NOW = datetime(2026, 6, 26, 12, 0, tzinfo=UTC)\n\n\ndef _suite(db: Any) -> Suite:\n    owner = User(aad_object_id=uuid.uuid4().hex, email=f\"u-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}@x.io\")\n    db.add(owner)\n    db.flush()\n    conn = Connection(\n        name=f\"c-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}\",\n        type=\"snowflake\",\n        env=\"dev\",\n        config={\"account\": \"a\"},\n        secret_ref=\"kv\",\n        created_by=owner.id,\n    )\n    db.add(conn)\n    db.flush()\n    suite = Suite(name=\"s\", connection_id=conn.id, created_by=owner.id, target={\"table\": \"T\"})\n    db.add(suite)\n    db.flush()\n    return suite\n\n\ndef _check(db: Any, suite: Suite, *, snoozed_until: datetime | None = None) -> Check:\n    check = Check(\n        suite_id=suite.id,\n        name=f\"c-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}\",\n        expectation_type=\"e\",\n        config={},\n        alert_snoozed_until=snoozed_until,\n    )\n    db.add(check)\n    db.flush()\n    return check\n\n\ndef _run_with(db: Any, suite: Suite, results: list[tuple[Check, str]], *, status: str = \"succeeded\") -> Run:\n    run = Run(suite_id=suite.id, status=status)\n    db.add(run)\n    db.flush()\n    for check, st in results:\n        db.add(Result(run_id=run.id, check_id=check.id, status=st))\n    db.commit()\n    return run\n\n\ndef test_no_failures_not_suppressed(db_session: Any) -> None:\n    suite = _suite(db_session)\n    chk = _check(db_session, suite)\n    run = _run_with(db_session, suite, [(chk, \"pass\")])\n    assert suppression.all_failures_snoozed(db_session, run, now=_NOW) is False\n\n\ndef test_live_failure_not_suppressed(db_session: Any) -> None:\n    suite = _suite(db_session)\n    chk = _check(db_session, suite)  # not snoozed\n    run = _run_with(db_session, suite, [(chk, \"fail\")])\n    assert suppression.all_failures_snoozed(db_session, run, now=_NOW) is False\n\n\ndef test_all_failures_snoozed_is_suppressed(db_session: Any) -> None:\n    suite = _suite(db_session)\n    chk = _check(db_session, suite, snoozed_until=_NOW + timedelta(hours=2))\n    run = _run_with(db_session, suite, [(chk, \"fail\")])\n    assert suppression.all_failures_snoozed(db_session, run, now=_NOW) is True\n\n\ndef test_partial_snooze_still_alerts(db_session: Any) -> None:\n    suite = _suite(db_session)\n    snoozed = _check(db_session, suite, snoozed_until=_NOW + timedelta(hours=2))\n    live = _check(db_session, suite)  # not snoozed\n    run = _run_with(db_session, suite, [(snoozed, \"fail\"), (live, \"critical\")])\n    # One failing check is live → don't suppress.\n    assert suppression.all_failures_snoozed(db_session, run, now=_NOW) is False\n\n\ndef test_expired_snooze_is_active_again(db_session: Any) -> None:\n    suite = _suite(db_session)\n    chk = _check(db_session, suite, snoozed_until=_NOW - timedelta(hours=1))  # in the past\n    run = _run_with(db_session, suite, [(chk, \"fail\")])\n    assert suppression.all_failures_snoozed(db_session, run, now=_NOW) is False\n\n\ndef test_snoozed_but_passing_is_not_suppressed(db_session: Any) -> None:\n    # A snooze only matters for *failing* checks; a passing snoozed check leaves\n    # the run with no failures, so there's nothing to suppress.\n    suite = _suite(db_session)\n    chk = _check(db_session, suite, snoozed_until=_NOW + timedelta(hours=2))\n    run = _run_with(db_session, suite, [(chk, \"pass\")])\n    assert suppression.all_failures_snoozed(db_session, run, now=_NOW) is False\n\n\ndef test_operational_failure_not_suppressed(db_session: Any) -> None:\n    # An operational run failure has no per-check results → snooze can't apply.\n    suite = _suite(db_session)\n    run = _run_with(db_session, suite, [], status=\"failed\")\n    assert suppression.all_failures_snoozed(db_session, run, now=_NOW) is False\n"
}

434	class Schedule(Base):
435	    """A cron schedule that fires a suite run automatically (A7).
436	
437	    The beat dispatcher (`worker.tasks.dispatch_due_schedules`) ticks every
438	    minute and queries `enabled AND next_run_at <= now()` — an indexed scan, so
439	    the cron is parsed only when a schedule actually fires, never per tick.
440	
441	    `next_run_at` is precomputed (`services.cron.next_fire`) on create and after
442	    each fire / cron change. **No-backfill semantics**: a fire advances it to the
443	    next *future* occurrence, so a downtime gap fires at most once on recovery
444	    rather than backfilling every missed slot (correct for monitoring). `cron` is
445	    a standard 5-field expression evaluated in `timezone` (IANA, DST-aware,
446	    default UTC). Cascade-deleted with the suite.
447	    """
448

454	    )

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/backend/app/services/notification_service.py",
  "content": "\"\"\"Per-suite alert notification config (``suite_notifications``).\n\nStores whether / where / at-what-threshold a suite's run outcomes are delivered.\nThe Teams webhook URL is token-bearing, so it's written through the SecretStore\nand referenced by ``webhook_secret_ref`` (mirrors connection credentials) — never\nplaintext in the DB. The Teams publisher reads this config when delivering.\n\nFastAPI-free like the sibling services: takes a ``Session`` (+ a ``SecretStore``\nwhere credentials are involved), returns ORM models, raises ``DataQError``.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport uuid\n\nfrom sqlalchemy import select\nfrom sqlalchemy.orm import Session\n\nfrom backend.app.core.errors import DataQError\nfrom backend.app.core.logging import get_logger\nfrom backend.app.core.secrets import SecretNotFoundError, SecretStore\nfrom backend.app.db.models import ALERT_ON_POLICIES, SuiteNotification\n\nlog = get_logger(__name__)\n\n# Threshold used for a suite with no config row — preserves the pre-config\n# behaviour (alert on warn+). A suite opts into a stricter/looser policy by\n# saving a config.\nDEFAULT_ALERT_ON = \"warn\"\n\n\nclass InvalidAlertPolicyError(DataQError):\n    \"\"\"Raised when ``alert_on`` isn't one of the allowed policies.\"\"\"\n\n    status_code = 422\n    code = \"alert_policy_invalid\"\n\n\ndef get_config(session: Session, suite_id: uuid.UUID) -> SuiteNotification | None:\n    \"\"\"The suite's notification config, or None if it has never been saved.\"\"\"\n    return session.scalars(\n        select(SuiteNotification).where(SuiteNotification.suite_id == suite_id)\n    ).first()\n\n\ndef upsert_config(\n    session: Session,\n    *,\n    suite_id: uuid.UUID,\n    enabled: bool,\n    alert_on: str,\n    webhook: str | None,\n    secret_store: SecretStore,\n) -> SuiteNotification:\n    \"\"\"Create or update a suite's notification config.\n\n    ``webhook`` is tri-state: ``None`` leaves the stored webhook unchanged, ``\"\"``\n    clears it (fall back to the workspace webhook), and a non-empty value is\n    written through the SecretStore (the ref is derived from the row id, like a\n    connection credential).\n    \"\"\"\n    if alert_on not in ALERT_ON_POLICIES:\n        raise InvalidAlertPolicyError(\n            \"invalid alert policy\",\n            detail={\"alert_on\": alert_on, \"allowed\": list(ALERT_ON_POLICIES)},\n        )\n    config = get_config(session, suite_id)\n    if config is None:\n        config = SuiteNotification(suite_id=suite_id, enabled=enabled, alert_on=alert_on)\n        session.add(config)\n        session.flush()  # assign id for the secret_ref below\n    else:\n        config.enabled = enabled\n        config.alert_on = alert_on\n\n    if webhook is not None:\n        if webhook == \"\":\n            config.webhook_secret_ref = None\n        else:\n            secret_ref = config.webhook_secret_ref or f\"suite-notif-{config.id}\"\n            secret_store.set(secret_ref, webhook)\n            config.webhook_secret_ref = secret_ref\n\n    session.commit()\n    session.refresh(config)\n    log.info(\"suite_notification_saved\", suite_id=str(suite_id), enabled=enabled, alert_on=alert_on)\n    return config\n\n\ndef delete_config(session: Session, suite_id: uuid.UUID) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Delete a suite's config (revert to defaults). Returns whether a row existed.\"\"\"\n    config = get_config(session, suite_id)\n    if config is None:\n        return False\n    session.delete(config)\n    session.commit()\n    log.info(\"suite_notification_deleted\", suite_id=str(suite_id))\n    return True\n\n\ndef resolve_webhook(\n    session: Session,\n    config: SuiteNotification | None,\n    *,\n    secret_store: SecretStore,\n    workspace_secret_name: str | None,\n) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"The webhook URL to deliver to: the per-suite one, else the workspace one.\n\n    Returns ``None`` when neither resolves (delivery is then skipped). A missing\n    secret is logged (by ref/name, never the value) and falls through.\n    \"\"\"\n    ref = config.webhook_secret_ref if config is not None else None\n    if ref:\n        try:\n            return secret_store.get(ref)\n        except SecretNotFoundError:\n            log.warning(\"suite_webhook_unresolved\", secret_ref=ref)\n    if workspace_secret_name:\n        try:\n            return secret_store.get(workspace_secret_name)\n        except SecretNotFoundError:\n            log.warning(\"teams_webhook_unresolved\", secret_name=workspace_secret_name)\n    return None\n"
}

  "old_string": "from dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom backend.app.alerting.base import RunReport\n\n# Urgency levels, quietest first. The card maps these to colour + escalation.\nQUIET = \"quiet\"\nSTANDARD = \"standard\"\nCRITICAL = \"critical\"\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Route:\n    \"\"\"The routing decision for one run.\n\n    ``should_send`` gates delivery (a clean run is ``False``); ``urgency`` drives\n    the card's prominence; ``mention_channel`` escalates a critical breach to the\n    whole channel.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    should_send: bool\n    urgency: str\n    mention_channel: bool\n\n\n_NO_SEND = Route(should_send=False, urgency=QUIET, mention_channel=False)\n\n\ndef route_for(report: RunReport) -> Route:\n    \"\"\"Decide how to route ``report`` from its worst severity.\n\n    - **critical** → send, critical urgency, escalate to the channel.\n    - **fail** (or an operational run failure with no result rows) → send,\n      standard urgency.\n    - **warn** → send, quiet urgency (no escalation).\n    - otherwise (all clean) → don't send.\n    \"\"\"\n    if report.worst_severity == CRITICAL:\n        return Route(should_send=True, urgency=CRITICAL, mention_channel=True)\n    if report.worst_severity == \"fail\" or report.run_status == \"failed\":\n        return Route(should_send=True, urgency=STANDARD, mention_channel=False)\n    if report.worst_severity == \"warn\":\n        return Route(should_send=True, urgency=QUIET, mention_channel=False)\n    return _NO_SEND",
  "new_string": "from dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom backend.app.alerting.base import RunReport\n\n# Urgency levels, quietest first. The card maps these to colour + escalation.\nQUIET = \"quiet\"\nSTANDARD = \"standard\"\nCRITICAL = \"critical\"\n\n# Per-suite delivery policies (mirror db.models.ALERT_ON_POLICIES). The default\n# preserves the pre-config behaviour: alert on warn+ but not on clean runs.\nFAIL_ONLY = \"fail\"\nWARN_PLUS = \"warn\"\nALWAYS = \"always\"\nDEFAULT_POLICY = WARN_PLUS\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Route:\n    \"\"\"The routing decision for one run.\n\n    ``should_send`` gates delivery; ``urgency`` drives the card's prominence;\n    ``mention_channel`` escalates a critical breach to the whole channel.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    should_send: bool\n    urgency: str\n    mention_channel: bool\n\n\ndef _urgency(report: RunReport) -> tuple[str, bool]:\n    \"\"\"(urgency, mention_channel) from the run's worst severity.\"\"\"\n    if report.worst_severity == CRITICAL:\n        return CRITICAL, True\n    if report.worst_severity == \"fail\" or report.run_status == \"failed\":\n        return STANDARD, False\n    return QUIET, False  # warn or clean\n\n\ndef _should_send(report: RunReport, policy: str) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Apply the per-suite delivery threshold.\n\n    ``always`` sends every terminal run (a heartbeat). Otherwise an operational\n    run failure always alerts; a clean run never does; and the severity threshold\n    decides the rest (``fail`` = fail/critical only, ``warn`` = warn+).\n    \"\"\"\n    if policy == ALWAYS:\n        return True\n    if report.run_status == \"failed\" and report.worst_severity is None:\n        return True  # operational failure — alert regardless of threshold\n    worst = report.worst_severity\n    if worst is None:\n        return False  # clean run\n    if policy == FAIL_ONLY:\n        return worst in (\"fail\", CRITICAL)\n    return worst in (\"warn\", \"fail\", CRITICAL)  # WARN_PLUS\n\n\ndef route_for(report: RunReport, policy: str = DEFAULT_POLICY) -> Route:\n    \"\"\"Decide whether + how loudly to alert on ``report`` under ``policy``.\n\n    Urgency/escalation come from the worst severity (``critical`` pings the\n    channel, ``fail``/operational is standard, ``warn`` is quiet); the per-suite\n    ``policy`` gates *whether* to send (see ``_should_send``).\n    \"\"\"\n    urgency, mention = _urgency(report)\n    return Route(\n        should_send=_should_send(report, policy), urgency=urgency, mention_channel=mention\n    )"

  "new_string": "def _title_block(report: RunReport, route: Route) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    # A clean run delivered under the 'always' (heartbeat) policy reads positive;\n    # otherwise the title colour follows the alert urgency.\n    color = \"good\" if report.success else _URGENCY_COLOR.get(route.urgency, _DEFAULT_COLOR)\n    return _text(report.suite_name, size=\"Large\", weight=\"Bolder\", color=color)\n\n\ndef _subtitle_block(report: RunReport) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    if report.success:\n        return _text(f\"All {report.total_checks} checks passed\", is_subtle=True)\n    # An operational run failure (adapter raised) has no result rows to tally."
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/backend/app/alerting/teams.py",
  "content": "\"\"\"The v1 ``ResultPublisher`` — posts a run's report as a Teams Adaptive Card.\n\nDelivery is driven by the run's **per-suite** notification config (read from the\ndispatch session): whether the suite has alerting enabled, its threshold\n(``alert_on`` → routing policy), and which webhook to post to (the per-suite one,\nfalling back to the workspace webhook). A suite with notifications disabled, a\nrun below its threshold, or no resolvable webhook is a quiet no-op — alerts are\nfor what the suite asked to be told about.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport httpx\nfrom sqlalchemy.orm import Session\n\nfrom backend.app.alerting.base import RunReport\nfrom backend.app.alerting.card import render_teams_message\nfrom backend.app.alerting.routing import route_for\nfrom backend.app.core.logging import get_logger\nfrom backend.app.core.secrets import SecretStore\nfrom backend.app.services import notification_service\n\nlog = get_logger(__name__)\n\n_POST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 10.0\n\n\nclass TeamsPublisher:\n    \"\"\"Posts an Adaptive Card to the webhook resolved for the run's suite.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(\n        self,\n        *,\n        secret_store: SecretStore,\n        workspace_secret_name: str | None,\n        timeout: float = _POST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,\n    ) -> None:\n        self._secret_store = secret_store\n        self._workspace_secret_name = workspace_secret_name\n        self._timeout = timeout\n\n    def publish(self, session: Session, report: RunReport) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Deliver the run's card per its suite's notification config.\n\n        Skips silently when the suite disabled alerting, the run is below the\n        suite's threshold, or no webhook resolves. Raises on an HTTP error — the\n        dispatch layer isolates that so a flaky webhook can't fail the run.\n        \"\"\"\n        config = notification_service.get_config(session, report.suite_id)\n        if config is not None and not config.enabled:\n            return\n        policy = config.alert_on if config is not None else notification_service.DEFAULT_ALERT_ON\n        route = route_for(report, policy)\n        if not route.should_send:\n            return\n        webhook = notification_service.resolve_webhook(\n            config,\n            secret_store=self._secret_store,\n            workspace_secret_name=self._workspace_secret_name,\n        )\n        if not webhook:\n            return\n        response = httpx.post(webhook, json=render_teams_message(report, route), timeout=self._timeout)\n        response.raise_for_status()\n        log.info(\n            \"teams_alert_sent\",\n            run_id=str(report.run_id),\n            suite=report.suite_name,\n            worst_severity=report.worst_severity,\n            urgency=route.urgency,\n            failed_checks=report.failed_checks,\n        )\n"
}

  "content": "\"\"\"Per-suite alert notification config — nested under a suite.\n\n`GET`/`PUT`/`DELETE /suites/{suite_id}/notifications`. View to read, edit to\nchange (the capability ladder). The webhook URL is write-only (a secret): it's\naccepted on `PUT` and written through the SecretStore, but never returned — the\nread surface exposes only ``has_webhook``.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport uuid\nfrom typing import Annotated, Literal\n\nfrom fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, status\nfrom pydantic import BaseModel, Field, field_validator\nfrom sqlalchemy.orm import Session\n\nfrom backend.app.core.auth import get_current_user\nfrom backend.app.core.secrets import SecretStore, get_secret_store\nfrom backend.app.db.models import SuiteNotification, User\nfrom backend.app.db.session import get_db\nfrom backend.app.services import notification_service as svc\nfrom backend.app.services.suite_authz import require_permission\n\nrouter = APIRouter(tags=[\"notifications\"])\n\n\nclass SuiteNotificationRead(BaseModel):\n    \"\"\"A suite's effective notification config. ``configured`` distinguishes a\n    saved row from the defaults a suite falls back to. The webhook URL is never\n    returned — only whether one is set (``has_webhook``).\"\"\"\n\n    configured: bool\n    enabled: bool\n    alert_on: str\n    has_webhook: bool\n\n\nclass SuiteNotificationUpdate(BaseModel):\n    enabled: bool = True\n    alert_on: Literal[\"fail\", \"warn\", \"always\"] = \"fail\"\n    # Tri-state: omit/null = leave the stored webhook unchanged; \"\" = clear (use\n    # the workspace webhook); a URL = set the per-suite webhook (write-only).\n    webhook: str | None = None\n\n    @field_validator(\"webhook\")\n    @classmethod\n    def ValueError(\"webhook must be an https URL\")\n        return value\n\n\ndef _read(config: SuiteNotification | None) -> SuiteNotificationRead:\n    if config is None:\n        return SuiteNotificationRead(\n            configured=False,\n            enabled=True,\n            alert_on=svc.DEFAULT_ALERT_ON,\n            has_webhook=False,\n        )\n    return SuiteNotificationRead(\n        configured=True,\n        enabled=config.enabled,\n        alert_on=config.alert_on,\n        has_webhook=config.webhook_secret_ref is not None,\n    )\n\n\n@router.get(\n    \"/suites/{suite_id}/notifications\",\n    response_model=SuiteNotificationRead,\n    summary=\"Get a suite's notification config\",\n)\ndef get_notifications(\n    suite_id:   "content": "\"\"\"Tests for the publisher registry — type, caching, reset.\n\nDelivery behaviour (per-suite config, webhook resolution, policy) is exercised\nin the DB-backed `test_teams.py`; here we only assert what the registry returns.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom backend.app.alerting import registry\nfrom backend.app.alerting.base import ResultPublisher\nfrom backend.app.alerting.noop import NoopPublisher\nfrom backend.app.alerting.teams import TeamsPublisher\n\n\ndef test_returns_teams_publisher() -> None:\n    # v1 always returns the Teams publisher; it self-no-ops per run when nothing\n    # is configured (no webhook / disabled / below threshold).\n    assert isinstance(registry.get_result_publisher(), TeamsPublisher)\n\n\ndef test_publishers_satisfy_the_protocol() -> None:\n    # runtime_checkable Protocol — both impls are structural ResultPublishers.\n    assert isinstance(registry.get_result_publisher(), ResultPublisher)\n    assert isinstance(NoopPublisher(), ResultPublisher)\n\n\ndef test_publisher_is_cached() -> None:\n    assert registry.get_result_publisher() is registry.get_result_publisher()\n\n\ndef test_reset_rebuilds() -> None:\n    first = registry.get_result_publisher()\n    registry.reset_result_publisher_cache()\n    assert registry.get_result_publisher() is not first\n\n\ndef test_noop_publish_is_a_silent_drop() -> None:\n    from backend.app.alerting.base import RunReport\n\n    report = RunReport(\n        run_id=__import__(\"uuid\").uuid4(),\n        suite_id=__import__(\"uuid\").uuid4(),\n        suite_name=\"s\",\n        run_status=\"failed\",\n        datasource_type=\"snowflake\",\n        target_label=\"T\",\n        worst_severity=\"fail\",\n        counts={\"fail\": 1},\n        checks=[],\n        finished_at=None,\n    )\n    # No channel → publishing must not raise; the session arg is ignored.\n    assert NoopPublisher().publish(None, report) is None  # type: ignore[arg-type]\n"

SecretNotFoundError\nfrom backend.app.db.models import Connection, Suite, User\nfrom backend.app.services import notification_service as svc\nfrom backend.app.services.notification_service import InvalidAlertPolicyError\n\n\nclass _FakeStore:\n    def __init__(self) -> None:\n        self.secrets: dict[str, str] = {}\n\n    def get(self, name: str) -> str:\n        try:\n            return self.secrets[name]\n        except KeyError as exc:\n            raise SecretNotFoundError(name) from exc\n\n    def set(self, name: str, value: str) -> None:\n        self.secrets[name] = value\n\n\ndef _suite(db: Any) -> Suite:\n    owner = User(aad_object_id=uuid.uuid4().hex, email=f\"u-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}@x.io\")\n    db.add(owner)\n    db.flush()\n    conn = Connection(\n        name=f\"c-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}\",\n        type=\"snowflake\",\n        env=\"dev\",\n        config={\"account\": \"a\"},\n        secret_ref=\"kv\",\n        created_by=owner.id,\n    )\n    db.add(conn)\n    db.flush()\n    suite = Suite(name=\"s\", connection_id=conn.id, created_by=owner.id, target={\"table\": \"T\"})\n    db.add(suite)\n    db.commit()\n    return suite\n\n\ndef test_get_config_none_until_saved(db_session: Any) -> None:\n    suite = _suite(db_session)\n    assert svc.get_config(db_session, suite.id) is None\n\n\ndef test_upsert_creates_then_updates(db_session: Any) -> None:\n    suite = _suite(db_session)\n    store = _FakeStore()\n    created = svc.upsert_config(\n        db_session, suite_id=suite.id, enabled=True, alert_on=\"fail\", webhook=None, secret_store=store\n    )\n    assert created.alert_on == \"fail\"\n    assert created.webhook_secret_ref is None\n\n    updated = svc.upsert_config(\n        db_session, suite_id=suite.id, enabled=False, alert_on=\"always\", webhook=None, secret_store=store\n    )\n    assert updated.id == created.id  # same row (upsert)\n    assert updated.enabled is False\n    assert updated.alert_on == \"always\"\n\n\ndef test_upsert_writes_webhook_through_secret_store(db_session: Any) -> None:\n    suite = _suite(db_session)\n    store = _FakeStore()\n    config = svc.upsert_config(\n        db_session,\n        suite_id=suite.id,\n        enabled=True,\n        alert_on=\"fail\",\n        webhook=\"https://teams.example/hook\",\n        secret_store=store,\n    )\n    assert config.webhook_secret_ref == f\"suite-notif-{config.id}\"\n    # The URL lives in the store, not the DB row.\n    assert store.secrets[config.webhook_secret_ref] == \"https://teams.example/hook\"\n\n\ndef test_upsert_blank_webhook_clears_ref(db_session: Any) -> None:\n    suite = _suite(db_session)\n    store = _FakeStore()\n    svc.upsert_config(\n        db_session, suite_id=suite.id, enabled=True, alert_on=\"fail\", webhook=\"https://x/h\", secret_store=store\n    )\n    cleared = svc.upsert_config(\n        db_session, suite_id=suite.id, enabled=True, alert_on=\"fail\", webhook=\"\", secret_store=store\n    )\n    assert cleared.webhook_secret_ref is None\n\n\ndef test_upsert_rejects_bad_policy(db_session: Any) -> None:\n    suite = _suite(db_session)\n    with pytest.raises(InvalidAlertPolicyError):\n        svc.upsert_config(\n            db_session, suite_id=suite.id, enabled=True, alert_on=\"nope\", webhook=None, secret_store=_FakeStore()\n        )\n\n\ndef test_delete_config(db_session: Any) -> None:\n    suite = _suite(db_session)\n    svc.upsert_config(\n        db_session, suite_id=suite.id, enabled=True, alert_on=\"fail\", webhook=None, secret_store=_FakeStore()\n    )\n    assert svc.delete_config(db_session, suite.id) is True\n    assert svc.get_config(db_session, suite.id) is None\n    assert svc.delete_config(db_session, suite.id) is False  # idempotent\n\n\ndef test_resolve_webhook_prefers_suite_then_workspace(db_session: Any) -> None:\n    suite = _suite(db_session)\n    store = _FakeStore()\n    store.secrets[\"ws\"] = \"https://workspace\"\n    # No config → workspace fallback.\n    assert svc.resolve_webhook(None, secret_store=store, workspace_secret_name=\"ws\") == \"https://workspace\"\n\n    config = svc.upsert_config(\n        db_session, suite_id=suite.id, enabled=True, alert_on=\"fail\", webhook=\"https://suite\", secret_store=store\n    )\n    assert (\n        svc.resolve_webhook(config, secret_store=store, workspace_secret_name=\"ws\") == \"https://suite\"\n    )\n\n\ndef test_resolve_webhook_none_when_nothing_set(db_session: Any) -> None:\n    assert svc.resolve_webhook(None, secret_store=_FakeStore(), workspace_secret_name=None) is None\n"

The shared validation-error handler (`errors.py:73`) json-encodes `exc.errors()`, which includes the raw `ValueError` in `ctx` for custom Pydantic validators — not serializable. That's a latent handler bug, but the localized, consistent fix is to validate the webhook in the service layer (raising a `DataQError`, like `alert_on` does) rather than a Pydantic validator. Summary: the seam change `publish(report)` → `publish(session, report)` is fully and correctly propagated — dispatch passes the session, noop/teams updated, and both the dispatch spy and registry test doubles use the new signature (verified by grep, no stragglers). The `routing.route_for(report, policy)` matrix is correct and well-tested across all policy × severity combinations (`fail` skips warn, operational failures send under every policy, `always` sends clean runs). `TeamsPublisher.publish` ordering (disabled → policy/should_send → webhook resolve) is correct, the no-config default is `'warn'` (preserves prior behavior), and a fully unconfigured deployment safely no-ops. `card.py` success rendering is correct and doesn't break the failing-run or operational-failure paths; `content["body"][0]` is the title when no mention banner. The API correctly keeps the webhook write-only (`_read` exposes only `has_webhook`), and the secret_ref derivation correctly flushes before reading `config.id`.

The three findings above are: (1) a real `always`-policy interaction defect where dedup upstream of the publisher suppresses ongoing-failure heartbeats; (2) a default-threshold inconsistency (`warn` unconfigured vs `fail` on save) that silently tightens alerting; and (3) orphaned-secret cleanup gaps on webhook clear/delete. None are blocking crashes, but #1 and #2 are behavioral correctness issues worth addressing before merge.
