1	"""The run-completion hook: build a run's report and hand it to the publisher.
2	
3	Called from the worker right after a run reaches a terminal state. It is
4	**best-effort and never raises** — the run is already persisted, so a broken /
5	slow notification channel must not fail the task or roll anything back. Only
6	runs that actually executed (``succeeded``/``failed``) are published; a
7	``cancelled`` run is user-initiated and not alert-worthy.
8	"""
9	
10	from __future__ import annotations
11	
12	import uuid
13	
14	from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
15	
16	from backend.app.alerting import dedup, registry, suppression
17	from backend.app.alerting.builder import build_run_report
18	from backend.app.core.logging import get_logger
19	from backend.app.db.models import Run
20	
21	log = get_logger(__name__)
22	
23	# Terminal statuses worth notifying on. `cancelled` is excluded (user-initiated);
24	# `queued`/`running` are non-terminal so they never reach here.
25	_PUBLISHABLE_STATUSES = frozenset({"succeeded", "failed"})
26	
27	
28	def publish_run_outcome(session: Session, *, run_id: uuid.UUID) -> bool:
29	    """Publish ``run_id``'s outcome through the configured publisher.
30	
31	    Returns whether a report was dispatched (``False`` when the run is missing,
32	    not in a publishable state, or a failure was swallowed). Any exception —
33	    building the report or the publisher itself — is logged and contained.
34	    """
35	    try:
36	        run = session.get(Run, run_id)
37	        if run is None or run.status not in _PUBLISHABLE_STATUSES:
38	            return False
39	        # Suppress when every failing check is snoozed (the operator silenced
40	        # them); a partial snooze still alerts on the live checks.
41	        if suppression.all_failures_snoozed(session, run):
42	            log.info("alert_suppressed_snoozed", run_id=str(run_id), suite_id=str(run.suite_id))
43	            return False
44	        # Dedup before building/publishing: an ongoing, unchanged failure on a
45	        # scheduled suite shouldn't re-alert every run (a clean run is never a
46	        # "duplicate", so this is a no-op for the passing path).
47	        if dedup.is_duplicate_alert(session, run):
48	            log.info("alert_deduped", run_id=str(run_id), suite_id=str(run.suite_id))
49	            return False
50	        report = build_run_report(session, run)
51	        registry.get_result_publisher().publish(session, report)
52	        return True
53	    except Exception:
54	        log.exception("result_publish_failed", run_id=str(run_id))
55	        return False
56

  "new_string": "    assert dispatch.publish_run_outcome(db_session, run_id=run.id) is False\n    assert spy.reports == []\n\n\ndef test_always_policy_bypasses_dedup(db_session: Any, spy: _SpyPublisher) -> None:\n    # An 'always' (heartbeat) suite alerts on every run, even an unchanged repeat\n    # failure that would otherwise be deduped.\n    owner = User(aad_object_id=uuid.uuid4().hex, email=f\"u-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}@x.io\")\n    db_session.add(owner)\n    db_session.flush()\n    conn = Connection(\n        name=f\"c-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}\",\n        type=\"snowflake\",\n        env=\"dev\",\n        config={\"account\": \"a\"},\n        secret_ref=\"kv\",\n        created_by=owner.id,\n    )\n    db_session.add(conn)\n    db_session.flush()\n    suite = Suite(name=\"s\", connection_id=conn.id, created_by=owner.id, target={\"table\": \"T\"})\n    db_session.add(suite)\n    db_session.flush()\n    db_session.add(SuiteNotification(suite_id=suite.id, enabled=True, alert_on=\"always\"))\n    check = Check(suite_id=suite.id, name=\"c\", expectation_type=\"e\", config={})\n    db_session.add(check)\n    db_session.flush()\n    base = datetime(2026, 6, 26, tzinfo=UTC)\n    r1 = Run(suite_id=suite.id, status=\"succeeded\", created_at=base)\n    r2 = Run(suite_id=suite.id, status=\"succeeded\", created_at=base + timedelta(minutes=5))\n    db_session.add_all([r1, r2])\n    db_session.flush()\n    db_session.add(Result(run_id=r1.id, check_id=check.id, status=\"fail\"))\n    db_session.add(Result(run_id=r2.id, check_id=check.id, status=\"fail\"))\n    db_session.commit()\n\n    # Both runs publish — the repeat isn't deduped under 'always'.\n    assert dispatch.publish_run_outcome(db_session, run_id=r1.id) is True\n    assert dispatch.publish_run_outcome(db_session, run_id=r2.id) is True\n    assert [r.run_id for r in spy.reports] == [r1.id, r2.id]"

For a custom Pydantic `field_validator` that raises a raw `ValueError`, `exc.errors()` includes a `ctx` dict holding the original `ValueError` object, which isn't JSON-serializable → the 422 becomes a 500 `TypeError: Object of type ValueError is not JSON serializable`.\n\nNo code triggered it until W6 (the notification webhook validator), which was moved to the service layer to dodge it. The handler should stringify/strip non-serializable `ctx` values so any future `field_validator` raising `ValueError` returns a clean 422.\n\n**Fix:** sanitize `exc.errors()` (e.g. `exc.errors(include_url=False)` + coerce `ctx` values to `str`) before encoding.\n\nFound during W6 PR #371 (per-suite notification config).\nEOF\n)\" 2>&1 | tail -1)\necho \"issue1: $ISSUE1\"\nISSUE2=$(gh issue create --title \"SecretStore has no delete: webhook/connection secrets orphan on clear/delete\" --milestone \"Backlog (post-v1 / testing)\" --body \"$(cat <<'EOF'\nThe `SecretStore` Protocol (`backend/app/core/secrets.py`) exposes only `get`/`set` — no `delete`. So when an entity that owns a secret is deleted or its secret cleared, the secret stays in the backing store (Key Vault / Redis / env):\n\n- **Connections:** `connection_service` never removes `conn-<id>` on delete.\n- **Suite notifications (W6):** clearing a per-suite webhook (`webhook=\"\"`) or `delete_config` drops the `webhook_secret_ref` / row but leaves `suite-notif-<id>` in the store.\n\nLow-risk hygiene (orphaned, unreferenced secrets; tokens not revoked from the store). **Fix:** add `SecretStore.delete` across all impls (Env/Redis/AzureKeyVault) + call it on entity delete / secret clear for connections + notifications.\n\nFound during W6 PR #371; consistent with existing connection behaviour (not a regression).\nEOF\n)\" 2>&1 | tail -1)\necho \"issue2: $ISSUE2\"",

{
  "command": "gh pr create --base feature/w6-alert-suppression --title \"feat(alerting): per-suite notification config (enabled + policy + webhook)\" --milestone \"Week 6 — Results dashboard + alerting\" --body \"$(cat <<'EOF'\n## What\nThe backend for **\"Teams webhook per suite; alert on fail/warn/always\"** (task 7.2) — the last alerting-backend piece.\n\n- **migration `b2c3d4e5f6a7`** — additive `suite_notifications` table (one row per suite, cascade-deleted): `enabled`, `alert_on` (fail/warn/always CHECK, default **warn**), optional per-suite webhook via `webhook_secret_ref` (token-bearing URL → SecretStore, never the DB). Tested up + down; `alembic check` clean.\n- **`notification_service`** — get / upsert (secret write-through, https-only) / delete + `resolve_webhook` (per-suite ref → workspace fallback → None).\n- **`routing.route_for(report, policy)`** — the per-suite threshold gates delivery: `fail` = fail/critical, `warn` = warn+, `always` = every run (heartbeat); operational failures always alert. Urgency/escalation still from severity.\n- **`card`** — a clean run under `always` renders as a success card.\n- **Seam → `publish(session, report)`** so a publisher reads its own per-suite config from the dispatch session. `TeamsPublisher` reads the suite config: skips if disabled / below threshold / no webhook; resolves per-suite-then-workspace webhook; renders + posts. Registry returns the Teams publisher (self-no-ops per run); `NoopPublisher` stays the test double.\n- **API** — `GET/PUT/DELETE /suites/{id}/notifications` (view to read, edit to write; webhook **write-only** — only `has_webhook` returned).\n\n## Tests\n100% alerting-package + `notification_service` coverage; service + API + DB-backed publisher tests (workspace fallback, per-suite override, disabled, each policy, no-webhook no-op, https reject, `always`-bypasses-dedup). import { Alert, Card, Descriptions, Spin, Typography } from 'antd';

import { useMe } from '../auth/useMe';

export function Home() {
  // Reuse the shared /me fetch (MeProvider) rather than fetching again — it's
  // already resolved by the time the Profile page renders.
  const state = useMe();

  if (state.status === 'loading') {
    return <Spin tip="Loading /api/v1/me…" size="large" style={{ marginTop: 80 }} />;
  }
  if (state.status === 'error') {
    return (
      <Alert
        type="error"
        showIcon
        title="Failed to load /api/v1/me"
        description={state.error}
        style={{ margin: 24 }}
      />
    );
  }
  return (
    <Card title="Authenticated as">
      <Descriptions column={1} bordered size="small">
        <Descriptions.Item label="Display name">{state.data.display_name ?? '—'}</Descriptions.Item>
        <Descriptions.Item label="Email">{state.data.email}</Descriptions.Item>
        <Descriptions.Item label="AAD object id">
          <Typography.Text code copyable>
            {state.data.aad_object_id}
          </Typography.Text>
        </Descriptions.Item>
        <Descriptions.Item label="Last seen">{state.data.last_seen_at ?? '—'}</Descriptions.Item>
      </Descriptions>
    </Card>
  );
}

=== Page component ===
import { Flex } from 'antd';
import type { ReactNode } from 'react';

/**
 * Per-screen content-column widths, mirroring the prototype (ADR 0022): list /
 * dashboard screens fill a wide column, authoring forms sit in a narrow column,
 * and the connection source picker is in between.
 */
const WIDTHS = { wide: 1200, picker: 880, form: 720 } as const;
type PageWidthName = keyof typeof WIDTHS;

/**
 * Centered page content column. The prototype wraps every screen in
 * `maxWidth + margin: 0 auto`, so content is centred in the canvas instead of
 * hugging the sider on wide displays. This component is the one place that
 * contract lives — pages use it as their root rather than each re-deriving the
 * `marginInline: 'auto'` dance. `width` takes a named preset (`wide` default,
 * `form`, `picker`) or a raw pixel number for one-off columns.
 */
export function Page({
  width = 'wide',
  gap = 24,
  children,
}: {
  width?: PageWidthName | number;
  /** Vertical gap between the page's stacked sections (header, body, …). */
  gap?: number;
  children: ReactNode;
}) {
  const maxWidth = typeof width === 'number' ? width : WIDTHS[width];
  return (
    <Flex vertical gap={gap} style={{ width: '100%', maxWidth, marginInline: 'auto' }}>
      {children}
    </Flex>
  );
}

import type { ThemeConfig } from 'antd';

/**
 * App-wide Ant Design theme. Kept in one module so the brand palette and the
 * shell (App.tsx) read from the same tokens rather than hard-coding hexes.
 *
 * Design intent: move off the stock antd "navy-header admin template" look.
 * An indigo primary + a soft gray layout canvas (`colorBgLayout`) give the
 * white surfaces (header, sider, cards) depth and definition — so the page no
 * longer reads as a flat sea of white, and the empty space frames content
 * instead of just being blank.
 */

export const BRAND = {
  /** Indigo-600 — the primary accent (buttons, active nav, links). */
  primary: '#4f46e5',
  /** Indigo-200 — the logo's light lobe + the watermark tint. */
  primarySoft: '#c7d2fe',
  /** Pale indigo — the "selected" row/nav background (one tint everywhere). */
  selectedBg: '#eef0fe',
  /** The soft canvas behind white surfaces. */
  canvas: '#f4f5f7',
  /** Hairline border for header / sider / cards. */
  border: '#e6e8eb',
  /** Primary text. */
  ink: '#1f2430',
} as const;

/** Shared shell metrics so App.tsx and the theme agree. */
export const SHELL = {
  headerHeight: 56,
  siderWidth: 220,
} as const;

export const appTheme: ThemeConfig = {
  token: {
    colorPrimary: BRAND.primary,
    colorInfo: BRAND.primary,
    colorLink: BRAND.primary,
    colorTextHeading: BRAND.ink,
```

src/components/dashboard/MetricCard.tsx
import { Card, Flex, Progress, Skeleton, Typography } from 'antd';
import type { ReactNode } from 'react';

import { BRAND } from '../../theme';

/**
 * A single KPI tile on the dashboard (prototype `MetricCard`): a label, a large
 * value, an optional unit suffix, an optional progress bar, and an optional
 * footnote — fronted by a tinted icon chip.
 *
 * The prototype also shows a period-over-period delta ("+0.4%", trend arrow);
 * we omit it deliberately — the summary endpoint has no historical comparison
 * to back it, and a fabricated delta would violate KPI honesty (ADR 0022 /
 * 0018). Add it only once a query backs it.
 *
 * `value === null` renders an em dash (no data for the window) rather than 0,
 * so an empty workspace reads as "nothing yet", not "scored zero".
 */
interface MetricCardProps {
  label: string;
  /** Pre-formatted display value, or `null` for the no-data em dash. */
  value: ReactNode | null;
  icon: ReactNode;
  /** Trailing unit shown next to the value (e.g. "%", "operational"). */
  unit?: string;
  /** 0–100 progress bar under the value; omit for plain count metrics. */
  progress?: number | null;
  footnote?: string;
  loading?: boolean;
}

export function MetricCard({
  label,
  value,
  icon,
  unit,
  progress,
  footnote,
  loading = false,
}: MetricCardProps) {
  return (
    <Card size="small" style={{ height: '100%' }}>
      <Flex vertical gap={12}>
        <Flex justify="space-between" align="flex-start" gap={8}>
          <Typography.Text type="secondary" style={{ fontSize: 13 }}>
            {label}
          </Typography.Text>
          <span
            aria-hidden
            style={{
              display: 'inline-flex',
              alignItems: 'center',
              justifyContent: 'center',
              width: 32,
              height: 32,
              borderRadius: 8,
              background: BRAND.selectedBg,
              color: BRAND.primary,
              flexShrink: 0,
            }}

  "content": "import { AppstoreOutlined, KeyOutlined, TeamOutlined } from '@ant-design/icons';\nimport { Alert, Card, Col, Flex, Row, Spin, Table, Tag, Typography } from 'antd';\nimport type { ColumnsType } from 'antd/es/table';\n\nimport {\n  type AdminAccess,\n  type AdminSuite,\n  type AdminUser,\n  listAdminAccess,\n  listAdminSuites,\n  listAdminUsers,\n} from '../api/admin';\nimport { useMe } from '../auth/useMe';\nimport { MetricCard } from '../components/dashboard/MetricCard';\nimport { Forbidden } from '../components/Forbidden';\nimport { Page } from '../components/layout/Page';\nimport { formatTimestamp } from '../components/results/resultsFormat';\nimport { type AsyncState, useAsyncData } from '../hooks/useAsyncData';\n\n/**\n * Workspace-admin control centre (#173): all suites / members / access overview.\n *\n * Layout reconciled to the prototype (ADR 0022 AdminScreen): KPI MetricCards over\n * stacked tables, **no tabs**. Presentation only — same `/admin/{suites,users,\n * access}` endpoints. Access is server-driven (gated on `/me`'s\n * `is_workspace_admin`; the endpoints re-enforce with 403); a non-admin deep-link\n * sees the Forbidden page and no data is fetched.\n */\nexport function Admin() {\n  const me = useMe();\n\n  if (me.status === 'loading') {\n    return <Spin size=\"large\" style={{ marginTop: 80 }} />;\n  }\n  if (me.status === 'error') {\n    return (\n      <Alert type=\"error\" showIcon message=\"Couldn't verify your access\" description={me.error} />\n    );\n  }\n  if (!me.data.is_workspace_admin) {\n    return <Forbidden message=\"The admin overview is restricted to workspace admins.\" />;\n  }\n\n  return <AdminOverview />;\n}\n\n/** Hooks live here so they only run for an admin (Admin renders this after the gate). */\nfunction AdminOverview() {\n  const suites = useAsyncData(listAdminSuites);\n  const users = useAsyncData(listAdminUsers);\n  const access = useAsyncData(listAdminAccess);\n\n  return (\n    <Page>\n      <Typography.Title level={3} style={{ margin: 0 }}>\n        Admin\n      </Typography.Title>\n\n      <Row gutter={[16, 16]}>\n        <Col xs={24} sm={8}>\n          <MetricCard\n            label=\"Suites\"\n            value={count(suites.state)}\n            loading={suites.state.status === 'loading'}\n            icon={<AppstoreOutlined />}\n          />\n        </Col>\n        <Col xs={24} sm={8}>\n          <MetricCard\n            label=\"Members\"\n            value={count(users.state)}\n            loading={users.state.status === 'loading'}\n            icon={<TeamOutlined />}\n          />\n        </Col>\n        <Col xs={24} sm={8}>\n          <MetricCard\n            label=\"Access grants\"\n            value={count(access.state)}\n            loading={access.state.status === 'loading'}\n            icon={<KeyOutlined />}\n          />\n        </Col>\n      </Row>\n\n      <Section title=\"All suites\">\n        <DataTable\n          state={suites.state}\n          columns={SUITE_COLUMNS}\n          rowKey={(s) => s.id}\n          errorMessage=\"Failed to load suites\"\n        />\n      </Section>\n\n      <Section title=\"Members & access\">\n        <DataTable\n          state={users.state}\n          columns={USER_COLUMNS}\n          rowKey={(u) => u.id}\n          errorMessage=\"Failed to load members\"\n        />\n        <DataTable\n          state={access.state}\n          columns={ACCESS_COLUMNS}\n          // A user appears once per suite (owner or a single share row).\n          rowKey={(a) => `${a.suite_id}:${a.user_id}`}\n          errorMessage=\"Failed to load access overview\"\n        />\n      </Section>\n    </Page>\n  );\n}\n\nfunction count<T>(state: AsyncState<T[]>): number | null {\n  return state.status === 'ok' ? state.data.length : null;\n}\n\nfunction Section({ title, children }: { title: string; children: React.ReactNode }) {\n  return (\n    <Card title={title} size=\"small\">\n      <Flex vertical gap={16}>\n        {children}\n      </Flex>\n    </Card>\n  );\n}\n\n/** Load/error/table boilerplate for an already-fetched admin dataset. */\nfunction DataTable<T extends object>({\n  state,\n  columns,\n  rowKey,\n  errorMessage,\n}: {\n  state: AsyncState<T[]>;\n  columns: ColumnsType<T>;\n  rowKey: (row: T) => string;\n  errorMessage: string;\n}) {\n  if (state.status === 'loading') return <Spin size=\"large\" />;\n  if (state.status === 'error') {\n    return <Alert type=\"error\" showIcon message={errorMessage} description={state.error} />;\n  }\n  return (\n    <Table\n      dataSource={state.data}\n      columns={columns}\n      rowKey={rowKey}\n      size=\"small\"\n      pagination={{ pageSize: 20, hideOnSinglePage: true }}\n    />\n  );\n}\n\n/** Name over email, falling back to the email alone when no display name. */\nfunction Identity({ name, email }: { name: string | null; email: string }) {\n  if (!name) return <Typography.Text>{email}</Typography.Text>;\n  return (\n    <Flex vertical>\n      <Typography.Text>{name}</Typography.Text>\n      <Typography.Text type=\"secondary\" style={{ fontSize: 12 }}>\n        {email}\n      </Typography.Text>\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}\n\nconst PERMISSION_COLORS: Record<string, string> = {\n  owner: 'gold',\n  admin: 'volcano',\n  edit: 'blue',\n  view: 'default',\n};\n\nconst SUITE_COLUMNS: ColumnsType<AdminSuite> = [\n  { title: 'Suite', dataIndex: 'name' },\n  {\n    title: 'Owner',\n    key: 'owner',\n    render: (_, s) => <Identity name={s.owner_name} email={s.owner_email} />,\n  },\n  {\n    title: 'Datasource',\n    key: 'datasource',\n    render: (_, s) => (\n      <Flex align=\"center\" gap={6}>\n        <Typography.Text>{s.connection_name}</Typography.Text>\n        <Tag>{s.connection_type}</Tag>\n      </Flex>\n    ),\n  },\n  { title: 'Env', dataIndex: 'env', render: (env: string) => <Tag>{env}</Tag> },\n  { title: 'Checks', dataIndex: 'check_count', align: 'right' },\n  { title: 'Shared with', dataIndex: 'share_count', align: 'right' },\n  { title: 'Created', dataIndex: 'created_at', render: (v: string) => formatTimestamp(v) },\n];\n\nconst USER_COLUMNS: ColumnsType<AdminUser> = [\n  {\n    title: 'Member',\n    key: 'user',\n    render: (_, u) => <Identity name={u.display_name} email={u.email} />,\n  },\n  { title: 'Suites owned', dataIndex: 'owned_suite_count', align: 'right' },\n  { title: 'Shared with them', dataIndex: 'shared_suite_count', align: 'right' },\n  {\n    title: 'Last seen',\n    dataIndex: 'last_seen_at',\n    render: (v: string | null) => formatTimestamp(v),\n  },\n];\n\nconst ACCESS_COLUMNS: ColumnsType<AdminAccess> = [\n  { title: 'Suite', dataIndex: 'suite_name' },\n  {\n    title: 'User',\n    key: 'user',\n    render: (_, a) => <Identity name={a.user_name} email={a.user_email} />,\n  },\n  {\n    title: 'Permission',\n    dataIndex: 'permission',\n    render: (p: string) => <Tag color={PERMISSION_COLORS[p] ?? 'default'}>{p}</Tag>,\n  },\n];\n"
}

=== Forbidden ===
import { Button, Result } from 'antd';
import { Link } from 'react-router-dom';

/**
 * The 403 page. Rendered by a page when the server's own determination denies
 * access — e.g. the Admin page shows it when `/me`'s `is_workspace_admin` is
 * false (a server-computed flag, not a client-side role guess), so a non-admin
 * who deep-links to /admin lands here rather than seeing admin UI.
 */
export function Forbidden({
  message = "You don't have access to this page.",
}: {
  message?: string;
}) {
  return (
    <Result
      status="403"
      title="403 — Forbidden"
      subTitle={message}
      extra={
        <Link to="/">
          <Button type="primary">Back to app</Button>
        </Link>
      }
    />
  );
}
=== ErrorBoundary ===
import { Button, Result } from 'antd';
import { Component, type ErrorInfo, type ReactNode } from 'react';

interface Props {
  children: ReactNode;
}

interface State {
  error: Error | null;
}

/**
 * Catches render-time errors anywhere in the app subtree and shows an antd
 * fallback instead of React's blank screen. (main.tsx's bootstrap `.catch`
 * only covers the pre-render MSAL bootstrap; this covers everything after the
 * first paint.) Error boundaries must be class components — there is no hook
 * equivalent for `getDerivedStateFromError`.
 */
export class ErrorBoundary extends Component<Props, State> {
  state: State = { error: null };

  static getDerivedStateFromError(error: Error): State {
    return { error };
  }

  componentDidCatch(error: Error, info: ErrorInfo): void {
    // Surfaced to the console (and, once wired, App Insights) — fail loud.
    console.error('Unhandled render error', error, info.componentStack);
  }

  render(): ReactNode {
    if (this.state.error) {
      return (
        <Result
          status="error"
          title="Something went wrong"
          subTitle={this.state.error.message}
          extra={
            <Button type="primary" onClick={() => window.location.reload()}>
              Reload
            </Button>
          }
        />
      );
    }
    return this.props.children;
  }
}
```

Codes antd doesn't draw a\n// dedicated illustration for fall back to info/warning/error.\nconst CATALOG: Record<ErrorCode, CatalogEntry> = {\n  400: { status: 'error', title: '400 — Bad request', subTitle: 'The request was malformed.' },\n  401: {\n    status: 'warning',\n    title: '401 — Sign in required',\n    subTitle: 'Your session has expired. Sign in again to continue.',\n  },\n  403: {\n    status: '403',\n    title: '403 — Forbidden',\n    subTitle: \"You don't have access to this page.\",\n  },\n  404: {\n    status: '404',\n    title: '404 — Not found',\n    subTitle: \"This page doesn't exist or has moved.\",\n  },\n  429: {\n    status: 'warning',\n    title: '429 — Too many requests',\n    subTitle: 'Slow down for a moment, then try again.',\n  },\n  500: {\n    status: '500',\n    title: '500 — Something went wrong',\n    subTitle: 'An unexpected error occurred on our side.',\n  },\n  502: {\n    status: 'error',\n    title: '502 — Bad gateway',\n    subTitle: 'The server received an invalid upstream response.',\n  },\n  503: {\n    status: 'error',\n    title: '503 — Service unavailable',\n    subTitle: 'The service is temporarily unavailable. Try again shortly.',\n  },\n  504: {\n    status: 'error',\n    title: '504 — Gateway timeout',\n    subTitle: 'The server took too long to respond.',\n  },\n};\n\ninterface ErrorStateProps {\n  code: ErrorCode;\n  /** Override the catalog subtitle (e.g. a specific reason). */\n  message?: string;\n  /** Server-error correlation id — shown only for 5xx so support can trace it. */\n  requestId?: string;\n  /** A retry handler; when present, the primary action calls it. */\n  onRetry?: () => void;\n}\n\n/**\n * The one in-brand error page (ADR 0022 ErrorState), switchable across the 4xx /\n * 5xx the app surfaces. Used by the router catch-all (404), the ErrorBoundary\n * fallback (500), and access denials (403). Recovery action follows the tone:\n * a retry handler wins; otherwise server errors offer Reload, client errors a\n * link home. Server errors show the request id when one is supplied.\n */\nexport function ErrorState({ code, message, requestId, onRetry }: ErrorStateProps) {\n  const entry = CATALOG[code];\n  const isServer = code >= 500;\n  return (\n    <Result\n      status={entry.status}\n      title={entry.title}\n      subTitle={message ?? entry.subTitle}\n      extra={\n        <>\n          {onRetry ? (\n            <Button type=\"primary\" onClick={onRetry}>\n              Try again\n            </Button>\n          ) : isServer ? (\n            <Button type=\"primary\" onClick={() => window.location.reload()}>\n              Reload\n            </Button>\n          ) : (\n            <Link to=\"/\">\n              <Button type=\"primary\">Back to app</Button>\n            </Link>\n          )}\n          {isServer && requestId ? (\n            <div style={{ marginTop: 12 }}>\n              <Typography.Text type=\"secondary\">Request id: </Typography.Text>\n              <Typography.Text code copyable>\n                {requestId}\n              </Typography.Text>\n            </div>\n          ) : null}\n        </>\n      }\n    />\n  );\n}\n"
}

> AGENT

**Resolved.** Here's what that was:

**Root cause:** the running backend (my Week-6 branch) has the new `Check.alert_snoozed_until` field in the model (PR 5), but your **dev** `dataq` database was still at migration `f7a8b9c0d1e2` — so every `GET /suites/{id}/checks` SELECTed a column Postgres didn't have → 500 → the frontend's "Failed to load checks." I'd applied the PR-5/PR-6 migrations only to the *test* DB (`dataq_test`), not your dev DB.

**Fix:** ran `alembic upgrade head` against `dataq` → now at `b2c3d4e5f6a7` (column + `suite_notifications` table present). The checks endpoint returns **200** again — reload the app and it'll work.

Why it happened: the api container hot-reloaded my branch code, but the compose `migrate` step didn't re-run for the migrations I added mid-branch, so the dev DB lagged the model. The migrations are additive/backward-compatible, so applying them is safe.

3	/**
4	 * Schedules — cron-driven suite runs (A7). A schedule fires a run of its suite
5	 * on a 5-field cron cadence in a given IANA timezone; the backend precomputes
6	 * `next_run_at` and a Celery-beat tick dispatches due schedules. Managing a
7	 * schedule needs `edit` on the suite (backend-gated); listing needs `view`.
8	 * This is the only place a suite acquires an unattended run cadence — distinct
9	 * from trigger bindings (run-on-pipeline-success, CLAUDE.md §4).

39	  const { data } = await api.get<Schedule[]>('/schedules', { params: { suite_id: suiteId } });
40	  return data;
41	}

44	  const { data } = await api.post<Schedule>('/schedules', payload);
45	  return data;
46	}

49	  const { data } = await api.patch<Schedule>(`/schedules/${id}`, payload);
50	  return data;
51	}
52	
53	export async function deleteSchedule(id: string): Promise<void> {
54	  await api.delete(`/schedules/${id}`);
55	}

57	/**
58	 * IANA timezones for the schedule editor. `Intl.supportedValuesOf` is the
59	 * runtime's own list (no hardcoded table to drift); falls back to UTC on the
60	 * rare engine that lacks it. UTC is hoisted to the front as the default.
61	 */
62	export function timezoneOptions(): string[] {
63	  const supported =
64	    typeof Intl.supportedValuesOf === 'function' ? Intl.supportedValuesOf('timeZone') : [];

38	export function SchedulesPanel({ suiteId, canManage }: { suiteId: string; canManage: boolean }) {
39	  const { state, reload } = useAsyncData(() => listSchedules(suiteId));
40	
41	  return (
42	    <Card
43	      size="small"
44	      title={
45	        <Flex vertical gap={2}>
46	          <Typography.Text strong>Schedules</Typography.Text>
47	          <Typography.Text type="secondary" style={{ fontSize: 12, fontWeight: 400 }}>
48	            Run this suite automatically on a cron cadence.
49	          </Typography.Text>
50	        </Flex>
51	      }
52	    >
53	      <SchedulesBody state={state} suiteId={suiteId} canManage={canManage} onChanged={reload} />
54	    </Card>
55	  );
56	}
57	
58	function SchedulesBody({
59	  state,
60	  suiteId,
61	  canManage,
62	  onChanged,
63	}: {
64	  state: ReturnType<typeof useAsyncData<Schedule[]>>['state'];
65	  suiteId: string;
66	  canManage: boolean;
67	  onChanged: () => void;
68	}) {
69	  if (state.status === 'loading') {
70	    return <Spin tip="Loading schedules…" />;
71	  }
72	  if (state.status === 'error') {
73	    return (
74	      <Alert type="error" showIcon message="Failed to load schedules" description={state.error} />
75	    );
76	  }
77	  const schedules = state.data;
78	
79	  return (
80	    <Flex vertical gap={16}>
81	      {canManage && <AddSchedule suiteId={suiteId} onAdded={onChanged} />}
82	      {schedules.length === 0 ? (
83	        <Empty
84	          image={Empty.PRESENTED_IMAGE_SIMPLE}
85	          description="No schedules — this suite runs only on manual / triggered runs."
86	        />
87	      ) : (
88	        <ScheduleTable schedules={schedules} canManage={canManage} onChanged={onChanged} />
89	      )}
90	    </Flex>
91	  );
92	}
93	
94	function ScheduleTable({
95	  schedules,
96	  canManage,
97	  onChanged,
98	}: {
99	  schedules: Schedule[];
100	  canManage: boolean;
101	  onChanged: () => void;
102	}) {
103	  const { message, modal } = App.useApp();
104	  const [busyId, setBusyId] = useState<string | null>(null);
105	
106	  // cron is not unique per row (the same cron can run in two timezones), so
107	  // identify a schedule by cron + timezone in labels/toasts/confirms.
108	  const label = (s: Schedule) => `${s.cron} (${s.timezone})`;
109	
110	  const onToggle = async (s: Schedule, enabled: boolean) => {
111	    setBusyId(s.id);
112	    try {
113	      await updateSchedule(s.id, { enabled });
114	      message.success(`${label(s)}: ${enabled ? 'resumed' : 'paused'}`);
115	      onChanged();
116	    } catch (err) {
117	      message.error(`Update failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown error'}`);
118	    } finally {
119	      setBusyId(null);
120	    }
121	  };
122	
123	  const onRemove = (s: Schedule) => {
124	    modal.confirm({
125	      title: `Delete schedule ${label(s)}?`,
126	      content: 'This suite will no longer run on this cadence.',
127	      okText: 'Delete',
128	      okType: 'danger',
129	      onOk: async () => {
130	        setBusyId(s.id);
131	        try {
132	          await deleteSchedule(s.id);
133	          message.success(`${label(s)}: removed`);
134	          onChanged();
135	        } catch (err) {
136	          message.error(`Remove failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown error'}`);
137	          throw err; // keep the confirm modal open on failure
138	        } finally {
139	          setBusyId(null);
140	        }
141	      },
142	    });
143	  };
144	
145	  const columns: ColumnsType<Schedule> = [
146	    {
147	      title: 'Cron',
148	      dataIndex: 'cron',
149	      render: (cron: string) => <Typography.Text code>{cron}</Typography.Text>,
150	    },
151	    { title: 'Timezone', dataIndex: 'timezone', width: 160 },
152	    {
153	      title: 'Next run',
154	      dataIndex: 'next_run_at',
155	      render: (t: string) => formatTimestamp(t),
156	    },
157	    {
158	      title: 'Last run',
159	      dataIndex: 'last_run_at',
160	      render: (t: string | null) => formatTimestamp(t),
161	    },
162	    {
163	      title: 'Status',
164	      dataIndex: 'enabled',
165	      width: 100,
166	      render: (enabled: boolean, s) =>
167	        canManage ? (
168	          <Switch
169	            size="small"
170	            checked={enabled}
171	            loading={busyId === s.id}
172	            onChange={(next) => onToggle(s, next)}
173	            aria-label={`${enabled ? 'Pause' : 'Resume'} ${label(s)}`}
174	          />
175	        ) : (
176	          <Tag color={enabled ? 'success' : 'default'}>{enabled ? 'enabled' : 'paused'}</Tag>
177	        ),
178	    },
179	    ...(canManage
180	      ? [
181	          {
182	            title: '',
183	            key: 'actions',
184	            width: 48,
185	            render: (_: unknown, s: Schedule) => (
186	              <Button
187	                size="small"
188	                type="text"
189	                danger
190	                icon={<DeleteOutlined />}
191	                loading={busyId === s.id}
192	                onClick={() => onRemove(s)}
193	                aria-label={`Remove ${label(s)}`}
194	              />
195	            ),
196	          },
197	        ]
198	      : []),
199	  ];
200	
201	  return (
202	    <Table<Schedule>
203	      rowKey="id"
204	      size="small"
205	      columns={columns}
206	      dataSource={schedules}
207	      pagination={false}
208	    />
209	  );
210	}
211	
212	function AddSchedule({ suiteId, onAdded }: { suiteId: string; onAdded: () => void }) {
213	  const { message } = App.useApp();
214	  const [cron, setCron] = useState('');
215	  const [timezone, setTimezone] = useState('UTC');
216	  const [adding, setAdding] = useState(false);
217	  const zones = useMemo(() => timezoneOptions(), []);
218	
219	  const onAdd = async () => {
220	    const expr = cron.trim();
221	    if (!expr) return;
222	    setAdding(true);
223	    try {
224	      await createSchedule({ suite_id: suiteId, cron: expr, timezone });
225	      message.success(`${expr}: scheduled`);
226	      setCron('');
227	      onAdded();
228	    } catch (err) {
229	      message.error(`Add failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown error'}`);
230	    } finally {
231	      setAdding(false);
232	    }
233	  };
234	
235	  return (
236	    <Flex gap={8} align="center" wrap>
237	      <Input
238	        value={cron}
239	        onChange={(e) => setCron(e.target.value)}
240	        placeholder="Cron e.g. 0 9 * * 1-5 (min hour dom mon dow)"
241	        style={{ flex: 1, minWidth: 220 }}
242	        onPressEnter={onAdd}
243	        aria-label="Cron expression"
244	      />
245	      <Select
246	        showSearch
247	        value={timezone}
248	        onChange={setTimezone}
249	        style={{ width: 220 }}
250	        options={zones.map((z) => ({ value: z, label: z }))}
251	        aria-label="Timezone"
252	      />
253	      <Button type="primary" loading={adding} disabled={!cron.trim()} onClick={onAdd}>
254	        Add
255	      </Button>
256	    </Flex>
257	  );
258	}
259	
```

  "content": "import { api } from './client';\n\n/**\n * Per-suite alert notification config (W6). Decides whether a suite's run\n * outcomes are delivered, at what threshold (`alert_on`), and to which Teams\n * webhook. The webhook URL is **write-only** — sent on save, never returned\n * (it's a secret); the read surface exposes only `has_webhook`. Managing needs\n * `edit` on the suite (backend-gated); reading needs `view`.\n */\n\nexport type AlertOn = 'fail' | 'warn' | 'always';\n\n/** Mirrors the backend `SuiteNotificationRead`. */\nexport interface SuiteNotification {\n  /** False when the suite has no saved row (the values are the defaults). */\n  configured: boolean;\n  enabled: boolean;\n  alert_on: AlertOn;\n  has_webhook: boolean;\n}\n\n/** Mirrors `SuiteNotificationUpdate`. `webhook`: omit = unchanged, \"\" = clear. */\nexport interface SuiteNotificationUpdate {\n  enabled: boolean;\n  alert_on: AlertOn;\n  webhook?: string;\n}\n\nexport async function getNotifications(suiteId: string): Promise<SuiteNotification> {\n  const { data } = await api.get<SuiteNotification>(`/suites/${suiteId}/notifications`);\n  return data;\n}\n\nexport async function putNotifications(\n  suiteId: string,\n  payload: SuiteNotificationUpdate,\n): Promise<SuiteNotification> {\n  const { data } = await api.put<SuiteNotification>(`/suites/${suiteId}/notifications`, payload);\n  return data;\n}\n\nexport async function deleteNotifications(suiteId: string): Promise<void> {\n  await api.delete(`/suites/${suiteId}/notifications`);\n}\n"
}

  "content": "import { App, Alert, Button, Card, Flex, Input, Select, Spin, Switch, Tag, Typography } from 'antd';\nimport { useEffect, useState } from 'react';\n\nimport {\n  type AlertOn,\n  deleteNotifications,\n  getNotifications,\n  putNotifications,\n} from '../../api/notifications';\nimport { useAsyncData } from '../../hooks/useAsyncData';\n\nconst ALERT_ON_OPTIONS: { value: AlertOn; label: string }[] = [\n  { value: 'fail', label: 'On fail / critical' },\n  { value: 'warn', label: 'On warn and worse' },\n  { value: 'always', label: 'Always (every run)' },\n];\n\n/**\n * Suite-detail panel for per-suite Teams alerting (W6, fronts `notification_service`).\n * Controls whether outcomes are delivered, the threshold (`alert_on`), and the\n * Teams webhook. The webhook is **write-only** — the API never returns it, so the\n * field shows whether one is set and only writes when you type a new one (blank\n * = unchanged; \"Clear webhook\" removes it). `view` reads; `edit`+ (`canManage`)\n * mutates, matching the backend gate.\n */\nexport function NotificationsPanel({ suiteId, canManage }: { suiteId: string; canManage: boolean }) {\n  const { state, reload } = useAsyncData(() => getNotifications(suiteId));\n\n  return (\n    <Card\n      size=\"small\"\n      title={\n        <Flex vertical gap={2}>\n          <Typography.Text strong>Notifications</Typography.Text>\n          <Typography.Text type=\"secondary\" style={{ fontSize: 12, fontWeight: 400 }}>\n            Send this suite's run outcomes to Microsoft Teams.\n          </Typography.Text>\n        </Flex>\n      }\n    >\n      {state.status === 'loading' ? (\n        <Spin tip=\"Loading notifications…\" />\n      ) : state.status === 'error' ? (\n        <Alert\n          type=\"error\"\n          showIcon\n          message=\"Failed to load notifications\"\n          description={state.error}\n        />\n      ) : (\n        <NotificationsForm\n          suiteId={suiteId}\n          canManage={canManage}\n          initialEnabled={state.data.enabled}\n          initialAlertOn={state.data.alert_on}\n          hasWebhook={state.data.has_webhook}\n          onChanged={reload}\n        />\n      )}\n    </Card>\n  );\n}\n\nfunction NotificationsForm({\n  suiteId,\n  canManage,\n  initialEnabled,\n  initialAlertOn,\n  hasWebhook,\n  onChanged,\n}: {\n  suiteId: string;\n  canManage: boolean;\n  initialEnabled: boolean;\n  initialAlertOn: AlertOn;\n  hasWebhook: boolean;\n  onChanged: () => void;\n}) {\n  const { message } = App.useApp();\n  const [enabled, setEnabled] = useState(initialEnabled);\n  const [alertOn, setAlertOn] = useState<AlertOn>(initialAlertOn);\n  const [webhook, setWebhook] = useState('');\n  const [saving, setSaving] = useState(false);\n\n  // Re-sync when the loaded config changes (e.g. after a reload).\n  useEffect(() => {\n    setEnabled(initialEnabled);\n    setAlertOn(initialAlertOn);\n  }, [initialEnabled, initialAlertOn]);\n\n  const onSave = async () => {\n    setSaving(true);\n    try {\n      // Only send `webhook` when the user typed one (blank = leave it unchanged).\n      const trimmed = webhook.trim();\n      await putNotifications(suiteId, {\n        enabled,\n        alert_on: alertOn,\n        ...(trimmed ? { webhook: trimmed } : {}),\n      });\n      message.success('Notifications saved');\n      setWebhook('');\n      onChanged();\n    } catch (err) {\n      message.error(`Save failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown error'}`);\n    } finally {\n      setSaving(false);\n    }\n  };\n\n  const onClearWebhook = async () => {\n    setSaving(true);\n    try {\n      await putNotifications(suiteId, { enabled, alert_on: alertOn, webhook: '' });\n      message.success('Webhook cleared (falls back to the workspace webhook)');\n      onChanged();\n    } catch (err) {\n      message.error(`Clear failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown error'}`);\n    } finally {\n      setSaving(false);\n    }\n  };\n\n  return (\n    <Flex vertical gap={16}>\n      <Flex align=\"center\" gap={12}>\n        <Switch\n          checked={enabled}\n          disabled={!canManage}\n          onChange={setEnabled}\n          aria-label=\"Enable notifications\"\n        />\n        <Typography.Text>Send alerts for this suite</Typography.Text>\n      </Flex>\n\n      <Flex vertical gap={4}>\n        <Typography.Text type=\"secondary\">Alert threshold</Typography.Text>\n        <Select<AlertOn>\n          value={alertOn}\n          onChange={setAlertOn}\n          disabled={!canManage || !enabled}\n          options={ALERT_ON_OPTIONS}\n          style={{ maxWidth: 280 }}\n          aria-label=\"Alert threshold\"\n        />\n      </Flex>\n\n      <Flex vertical gap={4}>\n        <Flex align=\"center\" gap={8}>\n          <Typography.Text type=\"secondary\">Teams webhook</Typography.Text>\n          <Tag color={hasWebhook ? 'success' : 'default'}>{hasWebhook ? 'set' : 'not set'}</Tag>\n        </Flex>\n        <Input.Password\n          value={webhook}\n          disabled={!canManage}\n          onChange={(e) => setWebhook(e.target.value)}\n          placeholder={\n            hasWebhook ? 'Enter a new https URL to replace it' : 'https://… (falls back to workspace)'\n          }\n          aria-label=\"Teams webhook URL\"\n          style={{ maxWidth: 480 }}\n        />\n        <Typography.Text type=\"secondary\" style={{ fontSize: 12 }}>\n          The URL is stored as a secret and never shown again. Leave blank to keep the current one.\n        </Typography.Text>\n      </Flex>\n\n      {canManage && (\n        <Flex gap={8}>\n          <Button type=\"primary\" loading={saving} onClick={onSave}>\n            Save\n          </Button>\n          {hasWebhook && (\n            <Button loading={saving} onClick={onClearWebhook}>\n              Clear webhook\n            </Button>\n          )}\n        </Flex>\n      )}\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/frontend/tests/components/NotificationsPanel.test.tsx",
  "content": "import { App as AntApp } from 'antd';\nimport { render, screen, waitFor } from '@testing-library/react';\nimport userEvent from '@testing-library/user-event';\nimport { afterEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';\n\nimport {\n  deleteNotifications,\n  getNotifications,\n  putNotifications,\n  type SuiteNotification,\n} from '../../src/api/notifications';\nimport { NotificationsPanel } from '../../src/components/suites/NotificationsPanel';\n\nvi.mock('../../src/api/notifications', () => ({\n  getNotifications: vi.fn(),\n  putNotifications: vi.fn(),\n  deleteNotifications: vi.fn(),\n}));\n\nconst mockGet = vi.mocked(getNotifications);\nconst mockPut = vi.mocked(putNotifications);\nconst mockDelete = vi.mocked(deleteNotifications);\n\nconst CONFIG: SuiteNotification = {\n  configured: true,\n  enabled: true,\n  alert_on: 'fail',\n  has_webhook: false,\n};\n\nfunction renderPanel(props: Partial<Parameters<typeof NotificationsPanel>[0]> = {}) {\n  return render(\n    <AntApp>\n      <NotificationsPanel suiteId=\"s1\" canManage {...props} />\n    </AntApp>,\n  );\n}\n\nafterEach(() => vi.clearAllMocks());\n\ndescribe('NotificationsPanel', () => {\n  it('loads and shows the current config', async () => {\n    mockGet.mockResolvedValue(CONFIG);\n    renderPanel();\n    expect(await screen.findByText('Send alerts for this suite')).toBeInTheDocument();\n    expect(screen.getByText('not set')).toBeInTheDocument(); // webhook status\n  });\n\n  it('saves the threshold without resending an unchanged webhook', async () => {\n    mockGet.mockResolvedValue(CONFIG);\n    mockPut.mockResolvedValue({ ...CONFIG, alert_on: 'always' });\n    renderPanel();\n    await screen.findByText('Send alerts for this suite');\n\n    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Save' }));\n\n    await waitFor(() => expect(mockPut).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1));\n    // No webhook typed → the payload omits `webhook` (leaves the stored one).\n    expect(mockPut).toHaveBeenCalledWith('s1', { enabled: true, alert_on: 'fail' });\n  });\n\n  it('sends a typed webhook on save', async () => {\n    mockGet.mockResolvedValue(CONFIG);\n    mockPut.mockResolvedValue({ ...CONFIG, has_webhook: true });\n    renderPanel();\n    await screen.findByText('Send alerts for this suite');\n\n    await userEvent.type(\n      screen.getByLabelText('Teams webhook URL'),\n      'https://teams.example/hook',\n    );\n    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Save' }));\n\n    await waitFor(() =>\n      expect(mockPut).toHaveBeenCalledWith('s1', {\n        enabled: true,\n        alert_on: 'fail',\n        webhook: 'https://teams.example/hook',\n      }),\n    );\n  });\n\n  it('clears the webhook when one is set', async () => {\n    mockGet.mockResolvedValue({ ...CONFIG, has_webhook: true });\n    mockPut.mockResolvedValue({ ...CONFIG, has_webhook: false });\n    renderPanel();\n    await screen.findByText('set'); // webhook status tag\n\n    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Clear webhook' }));\n\n    await waitFor(() =>\n      expect(mockPut).toHaveBeenCalledWith('s1', { enabled: true, alert_on: 'fail', webhook: '' }),\n    );\n  });\n\n  it('hides the controls for a viewer', async () => {\n    mockGet.mockResolvedValue(CONFIG);\n    renderPanel({ canManage: false });\n    await screen.findByText('Send alerts for this suite');\n    expect(screen.queryByRole('button', { name: 'Save' })).not.toBeInTheDocument();\n  });\n\n  it('surfaces a load error', async () => {\n    mockGet.mockRejectedValue(new Error('boom'));\n    renderPanel();\n    expect(await screen.findByText('Failed to load notifications')).toBeInTheDocument();\n  });\n});\n\n// referenced to keep the import used even though delete is via Clear (put \"\")\nvoid mockDelete;\nvoid deleteNotifications;\n"
}

=== backend Dockerfile ===
# DataQ backend image — serves both the FastAPI API and the Celery worker.
# Build context is the repo ROOT (not backend/) because the app imports as the
# top-level `backend.app.*` package and environment.yml lives at the root:
#   docker build -f backend/Dockerfile .
#
# Conda-only per CLAUDE.md (no venv/poetry). The dataq env is created from the
# pinned environment.yml and its bin dir is put first on PATH so `uvicorn`,
# `celery`, `alembic`, and `python` resolve to it without a `conda run` wrapper
# (which would interfere with signal forwarding to uvicorn/celery).
FROM continuumio/miniconda3:24.11.1-0

WORKDIR /workspace

# Create the conda env first and cache the layer. environment.yml's pip section
# does `-r backend/requirements-dev.txt` (which -r's requirements.txt /
# -typecheck / -tooling), so those must exist before `conda env create`. Copy
# just the requirements files (not all of backend/) so the env-create layer cache
# busts only on a pin change, not on every code edit.
COPY environment.yml ./
COPY backend/requirements*.txt ./backend/
RUN conda env create -f environment.yml && conda clean -afy

ENV PATH=/opt/conda/envs/dataq/bin:$PATH \
    PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1

# Application code + tooling config (pyproject is needed to run pytest/mypy in-container).
COPY pyproject.toml ./
COPY backend ./backend

EXPOSE 8000

# Default to the API; the worker service overrides `command` in compose.
CMD ["uvicorn", "backend.app.main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"]

Added\n# only when origins are configured (empty in dev — the Vite proxy keeps it\n# same-origin), so the allowlist is explicit and never `*`. credentials=True so\n# the bearer/auth flow works from the SPA origin.\n_cors_origins = get_settings().cors_allow_origin_list\nif _cors_origins:\n    app.add_middleware(\n        CORSMiddleware,\n        allow_origins=_cors_origins,\n        allow_credentials=True,\n        allow_methods=[\"*\"],\n        allow_headers=[\"*\"],\n        expose_headers=[REQUEST_ID_HEADER],\n    )\n\n\n@app.middleware(\"http\")"
}

 * Request interceptor attaches an Azure AD bearer token in real auth mode.
 * In dev_bypass / unconfigured modes the interceptor is a no-op (backend
 * dev-bypass resolves the user without a token).
 *
 * Response interceptor surfaces the DataQ error envelope's human message
 * (`{ error: { code, message, detail } }`) as `error.message`, so callers'
 * `err.message` shows the actionable backend reason instead of axios's generic
 * "Request failed with status code 4xx".
 */
export const api = axios.create({
  baseURL: '/api/v1',
});

api.interceptors.request.use(attachBearerToken);

api.interceptors.response.use(
  (response) => response,
  (error: AxiosError<{ error?: { message?: string } }>) => {
    const apiMessage = error.response?.data?.error?.message;
    if (apiMessage) error.message = apiMessage;
    return Promise.reject(error);
  },
);

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/frontend/Dockerfile",
  "content": "# DataQ frontend image — build the Vite SPA, serve the static dist via nginx.\n# Build context = frontend/ :  docker build -f frontend/Dockerfile frontend/\n#\n# NOTE: Azure Static Web App serves dist/ directly and does NOT need this image\n# (the deploy workflow builds + uploads dist to SWA). This Dockerfile is the\n# container option — e.g. running the UI on Container Apps behind the same\n# ingress as the API — and keeps the UI deployable without Azure-specific glue.\n#\n# VITE_* values are inlined at build time (Vite bakes them into the bundle), so\n# they're build args, not runtime env. Pass them with --build-arg.\n\nFROM node:22-alpine AS build\nWORKDIR /app\nRUN corepack enable\n\nCOPY package.json pnpm-lock.yaml ./\nRUN pnpm install --frozen-lockfile\n\nCOPY . .\nARG VITE_AZURE_TENANT_ID=\"\"\nARG VITE_AZURE_SPA_CLIENT_ID=\"\"\nARG VITE_AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID=\"\"\nARG VITE_AZURE_API_SCOPE=\"user_impersonation\"\nARG VITE_AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=\"false\"\nENV VITE_AZURE_TENANT_ID=$VITE_AZURE_TENANT_ID \\\n    VITE_AZURE_SPA_CLIENT_ID=$VITE_AZURE_SPA_CLIENT_ID \\\n    VITE_AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID=$VITE_AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID \\\n    VITE_AZURE_API_SCOPE=$VITE_AZURE_API_SCOPE \\\n    VITE_AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=$VITE_AUTH_DEV_BYPASS\nRUN pnpm build\n\nFROM nginx:1.27-alpine AS serve\nCOPY --from=build /app/dist /usr/share/nginx/html\nCOPY nginx.conf /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf\nEXPOSE 8080\n"

SPA fallback: any non-file path returns index.html so\n# client-side routes (deep links like /results/:runId) resolve to the app, while\n# real assets are served directly.   "content": "name: Deploy\n\n# Manual-only for now (workflow_dispatch): apply-ready scaffolding that never\n# fires on its own until the Azure resources exist + secrets/vars are set. Once\n# the infra is provisioned (see deploy/README.md), flip on the push trigger:\n#   push:\n#     branches: [main]\non:\n  workflow_dispatch:\n    inputs:\n      image_tag:\n        description: \"Image tag to build + deploy\"\n        default: \"latest\"\n\nconcurrency:\n  group: deploy-production\n  cancel-in-progress: false\n\n# OIDC federated login to Azure (no stored client secret). The federated cred +\n# the listed vars/secrets must be configured first — see deploy/README.md.\npermissions:\n  id-token: write\n  contents: read\n\nenv:\n  IMAGE: ${{ vars.ACR_LOGIN_SERVER }}/dataq-backend:${{ inputs.image_tag }}\n\njobs:\n  backend:\n    name: Backend — build, migrate, deploy (API + worker)\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    environment: production\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@v4\n\n      - name: Azure login (OIDC)\n        uses: azure/login@v2\n        with:\n          client-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}\n          tenant-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_TENANT_ID }}\n          subscription-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}\n\n      - name: Build + push backend image to ACR\n        run: |\n          az acr login --name \"${{ vars.ACR_NAME }}\"\n          docker build -f backend/Dockerfile -t \"$IMAGE\" .\n          docker push \"$IMAGE\"\n\n      # Migrate BEFORE rolling the app: migrations are additive/backward-compatible\n      # (CLAUDE.md), so the running old code tolerates the new schema. Runs the\n      # one-off migrate Container Apps Job (provisioned per deploy/README.md).\n      - name: Run DB migrations (alembic upgrade head)\n        run: |\n          az containerapp job start \\\n            --name \"${{ vars.MIGRATE_JOB_NAME }}\" \\\n            --resource-group \"${{ vars.AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP }}\" \\\n            --image \"$IMAGE\"\n\n      - name: Deploy API\n        run: |\n          az containerapp update \\\n            --name \"${{ vars.API_APP_NAME }}\" \\\n            --resource-group \"${{ vars.AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP }}\" \\\n            --image \"$IMAGE\"\n\n      - name: Deploy worker\n        run: |\n          az containerapp update \\\n            --name \"${{ vars.WORKER_APP_NAME }}\" \\\n            --resource-group \"${{ vars.AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP }}\" \\\n            --image \"$IMAGE\"\n\n  frontend:\n    name: Frontend — build + deploy to Static Web App\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    environment: production\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@v4\n      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4\n      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4\n        with:\n          node-version: \"22\"\n          cache: pnpm\n          cache-dependency-path: frontend/pnpm-lock.yaml\n\n      - name: Build\n        working-directory: frontend\n        # VITE_* are inlined at build time. Non-secret azure client/tenant ids\n        # come from repo vars; never the SPA secret (there is none — MSAL is public).\n        env:\n          VITE_AZURE_TENANT_ID: ${{ vars.VITE_AZURE_TENANT_ID }}\n          VITE_AZURE_SPA_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.VITE_AZURE_SPA_CLIENT_ID }}\n          VITE_AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.VITE_AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID }}\n          VITE_AZURE_API_SCOPE: ${{ vars.VITE_AZURE_API_SCOPE }}\n          VITE_AUTH_DEV_BYPASS: \"false\"\n        run: |\n          pnpm install --frozen-lockfile\n          pnpm build\n\n      - name: Deploy to Azure Static Web Apps\n        uses: Azure/static-web-apps-deploy@v1\n        with:\n          azure_static_web_apps_api_token: ${{ secrets.AZURE_STATIC_WEB_APPS_API_TOKEN }}\n          action: upload\n          app_location: frontend/dist\n          skip_app_build: true\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/deploy/README.md",
  "content": "# DataQ — deployment scaffolding\n\nApply-ready Azure deploy scaffolding (Week 7). **Nothing here deploys on its own**\n— the workflow ([.github/workflows/deploy.yml](../.github/workflows/deploy.yml)) is\n`workflow_dispatch`-only until the Azure resources exist and the secrets/vars\nbelow are set. This documents what to provision and how the pieces fit.\n\nAzure is **one** deploy target behind the app's seams (ADR 0010/0013) — the\nmanifests here are infra config, not business logic. No Azure resource names are\nhardcoded in app code; they live only as workflow `vars`/`secrets`.\n\n## Topology\n\n```\nBrowser ─► Azure Static Web App (frontend/dist)\n              │  /api/* proxied to the linked backend (same-origin → no CORS)\n              ▼\n        Azure Container Apps\n          • dataq-api     (FastAPI image, external ingress :8000)\n          • dataq-worker  (same image, `celery -A ... worker` + beat)\n          • dataq-migrate (Container Apps Job: `alembic upgrade head`)\n              │\n              ├─► Azure Database for PostgreSQL (DATABASE_URL)\n              ├─► Azure Cache for Redis        (REDIS_URL)\n              ├─► Azure Key Vault              (SECRET_STORE=azure_key_vault, managed identity)\n              └─► Application Insights         (APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING)\n        Azure Container Registry (ACR) — holds the backend image\n```\n\nBoth api + worker run the **same** image ([backend/Dockerfile](../backend/Dockerfile),\nbuild context = repo root). The frontend is built and uploaded to SWA by the\nworkflow (the [frontend/Dockerfile](../frontend/Dockerfile) is the container\nalternative — only needed if you run the UI on Container Apps instead of SWA).\n\n## One-time provisioning\n\nThe datasource + compute infra is stood up by the external Terraform harness\n(ADR 0021) — see `HARNESS_TODO.md`. Beyond that, this app needs:\n\n1. **ACR** + an **ACA environment** + the three apps/job above. The api/worker run\n   `uvicorn …` / `celery …`; the migrate **job** runs `alembic upgrade head`.\n2. **Managed identity** on the api + worker apps with **Key Vault Secrets User**\n   on the vault (so `DefaultAzureCredential` resolves `SECRET_STORE=azure_key_vault`).\n3. **App env**: set the keys in [deploy/.env.app.prod.example](.env.app.prod.example)\n   on the api + worker apps. Secret values (DB/Redis URL, App Insights) are Key\n   Vault-backed Container Apps secrets — never literals.\n4. **SWA linked backend**: link the `dataq-api` Container App as the SWA backend so\n   `/api/*` is proxied same-origin (then `CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS` can stay empty). If\n   instead the SPA calls the API cross-origin, set `CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS` to the SWA\n   origin (the FastAPI CORS middleware turns on only when it's non-empty).\n5. **Azure Monitor → ADF webhook** alert rule (Week-7 task) — needs the deployed\n   API URL; configure after the first deploy.\n\n## GitHub config the workflow reads\n\nSet under repo **Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions**, and add a\nfederated credential for OIDC login (subject = this repo's `production`\nenvironment).\n\n**Secrets:** `AZURE_CLIENT_ID`, `AZURE_TENANT_ID`, `AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID`\n(OIDC app registration), `AZURE_STATIC_WEB_APPS_API_TOKEN`.\n\n**Variables:** `ACR_NAME`, `ACR_LOGIN_SERVER`, `AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP`,\n`API_APP_NAME`, `WORKER_APP_NAME`, `MIGRATE_JOB_NAME`, and the non-secret\n`VITE_AZURE_*` build values.\n\n## Going live\n\n1. Provision the resources + set the secrets/vars above.\n2. Run the **Deploy** workflow manually (`workflow_dispatch`) to validate end-to-end.\n3. To deploy on every merge, uncomment the `push: branches: [main]` trigger in\n   the workflow.\n\nMigrations are additive/backward-compatible (CLAUDE.md), so the workflow runs\n`alembic upgrade head` **before** rolling the apps — the running old code\ntolerates the new schema. (This is exactly the dev-DB step that, when skipped,\n500s the checks endpoint after a schema-adding deploy.)\n"
}

2	
3	Per 2026-05-28 security audit + observability work (#50, #51).
4	"""
5	
6	import logging
7	from collections.abc import Iterator
8	
9	import pytest
10	from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
11	
12	from backend.app.main import REQUEST_ID_HEADER, app
13	
14	
15	@pytest.fixture
16	def client() -> Iterator[TestClient]:
17	    # FastAPI lifespan runs configure_logging(); avoid re-running it for tests
18	    # by entering the context manually under TestClient.
19	    with TestClient(app) as c:
20	        yield c

23	# ───────────────────────── X-Request-ID validation ─────────────────────────
24	
25	
26	def test_request_id_generated_when_caller_omits(client: TestClient) -> None:
27	    response = client.get("/healthz")
28	    rid = response.headers.get(REQUEST_ID_HEADER)
29	    assert rid is not None
30	    # uuid4().hex is 32 lowercase hex chars
31	    assert len(rid) == 32
32	    assert all(c in "0123456789abcdef" for c in rid)
33	
34	
35	def test_request_id_echoed_when_valid(client: TestClient) -> None:
36	    response = client.get("/healthz", headers={REQUEST_ID_HEADER: "trace-abc.123_XYZ"})
37	    assert response.headers[REQUEST_ID_HEADER] == "trace-abc.123_XYZ"
38	
39	
40	def test_request_id_replaced_when_too_long(client: TestClient) -> None:
41	    """Caller-supplied IDs over 64 chars are rejected (security audit #2)."""
42	    too_long = "a" * 65
43	    response = client.get("/healthz", headers={REQUEST_ID_HEADER: too_long})
44	    echoed = response.headers[REQUEST_ID_HEADER]
45	    assert echoed != too_long
46	    assert len(echoed) == 32  # fresh uuid
47	
48	
49	def test_request_id_replaced_on_bad_chars(client: TestClient) -> None:
50	    """Caller-supplied IDs containing whitespace or JSON-control chars are rejected."""
51	    for bad in ['inject"quote', "with space", "tab\there", "semi;colon"]:
52	        response = client.get("/healthz", headers={REQUEST_ID_HEADER: bad})
53	        echoed = response.headers[REQUEST_ID_HEADER]
54	        assert echoed != bad
55	        assert len(echoed) == 32
56	
57	
58	def test_request_id_replaced_on_empty(client: TestClient) -> None:
59	    response = client.get("/healthz", headers={REQUEST_ID_HEADER: ""})
60	    echoed = response.headers[REQUEST_ID_HEADER]
61	    assert len(echoed) == 32
62	
63	
64	# ───────────────────────── per-request structured log ─────────────────────────
65	
66	
67	def _request_events_from_caplog(records: list[logging.LogRecord]) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
68	    """Pick request-event records that structlog routed through stdlib logging.
69	
70	    structlog's stdlib bridge emits records whose `msg` is the rendered dict
71	    (post-processors) — args slot carries the original event_dict.
72	    """
73	    out: list[dict[str, object]] = []
74	    for rec in records:
75	        # The structlog ProcessorFormatter wraps the original event_dict on rec.msg
76	        # (after processors run). We pull from rec.__dict__ to get the structured fields.
77	        evt = getattr(rec, "_record", None) or rec.__dict__.get("event_dict")
78	        if evt is None and isinstance(rec.msg, dict):
79	            evt = rec.msg
80	        if not isinstance(evt, dict):
81	            continue
82	        if evt.get("event") == "request":
83	            out.append(evt)
84	    return out
85	
86	
87	def test_per_request_log_emitted_on_success(
88	    client: TestClient, caplog: pytest.LogCaptureFixture
89	) -> None:
90	    """#51: every successful request emits one event=request structlog entry."""
91	    caplog.set_level(logging.INFO, logger="backend.app.main")
92	    client.get("/healthz", headers={REQUEST_ID_HEADER: "trace-1"})
93	    events = _request_events_from_caplog(caplog.records)
94	    assert len(events) == 1
95	    evt = events[0]
96	    assert evt["method"] == "GET"
97	    assert evt["path"] == "/healthz"
98	    assert evt["status"] == 200
99	    assert isinstance(evt["duration_ms"], int | float)
100	    assert evt["duration_ms"] >= 0
101	    assert evt["request_id"] == "trace-1"
102	
103	
104	def test_per_request_log_uses_generated_request_id_when_invalid(
105	    client: TestClient, caplog: pytest.LogCaptureFixture
106	) -> None:
107	    """Invalid X-Request-ID → generated UUID propagates into the request log."""
108	    caplog.set_level(logging.INFO, logger="backend.app.main")
109	    client.get("/healthz", headers={REQUEST_ID_HEADER: "with space"})
110	    events = _request_events_from_caplog(caplog.records)
111	    assert len(events) == 1
112	    rid = events[0]["request_id"]
113	    assert isinstance(rid, str)
114	    assert len(rid) == 32  # uuid4().hex, not the rejected "with space"

277	> Adopt the **DataQ Design System** prototype (claude.ai/design project *"DataQ Design System"*, reverse-engineered from the shipped indigo/antd app — its `readme.md` is the spec) — **the full 13-screen set this week**, not a subset (ADR [0022](adr/0022-week6-prototype-adoption-and-chart-library.md); the earlier 6-task scope under-counted it — Profile content, **Settings** (pulled in from Week 7), the Admin layout-reconcile, and the New-Connection source-select split were missing). The **foundation already matches** the product (`theme.ts` palette, `resultsFormat.ts` status model, the 56px-header/220px-sider shell), so this is **not a re-skin** — it adopts the prototype's **structure**: every create/edit flow becomes a dedicated, deep-linkable **page** (the **Share** drawer stays the *only* drawer), login lands on an **Enhanced Monitoring Dashboard**, and standard **error pages** ship. **Where the prototype differs from the shipped app (drawer-vs-page, layout), the prototype wins.** Components are reproduced with **real antd** — the prototype's framework-free recreations + `_ds_bundle.js` are reference only (per the design README). Post-v1 items (marketing, dark mode) + the polish passes (KPI honesty, visual-fidelity) stay in Week 7 / Post-v1 below. The intentionally-dropped prototype bits (the **"View as" role switch**, the **component bundle**, the **teal palette**) are recorded in Post-v1 as *not adopted*.

Read it with the **`/design-sync`** skill / **`DesignSync`** tool over the claude.ai login: `DesignSync method=list_files projectId=…`, then `method=get_file path=<…>`. Key paths: **`readme.md`** = the canonical spec (voice · color · type · spacing · status model · component/template manifest); **`guidelines/*.card.html`** = foundation specimen cards; **`templates/app/*.jsx`** = framework-free recreations of each screen; **`components/<group>/*.jsx`** = the component recreations; **`tokens/*.css`** = raw token values; **`uploads/DESIGN.md`** = the *superseded teal* brief (ignore for palette). ⚠️ The hosted share link `https://api.anthropic.com/v1/design/h/SVkQJqee7xsc2FNWVOsnIQ` returns **404** — reach the prototype via DesignSync, not the link. The `.jsx` / `_ds_bundle.js` are **reference only** — build in real antd reading `theme.ts`.

107	## 2a. Recurring cadence — incremental loads (the "source keeps producing" clock)
108	
109	> The §2 generator is **one-shot** (backfills N snapshots in a single run). Freshness/
110	> volume/anomaly monitors only mean something if data keeps *arriving* on a cadence.
111	> **Three clocks — do not conflate:** (1) **data-arrival** (source produces new data —
112	> NEW, this section); (2) **load+trigger** (ADF/Airflow picks up the file → triggers
113	> DataQ — §3); (3) **check-run** (DataQ's W5 `schedules` cron, or driven by clock 2).
114	>
115	> **Decisions (2026-06-26) — two layers, don't collapse them:**
116	> - **File creation (clock 1, source-system simulator) = Container Apps Job on a cron schedule.**
117	>   Runs the `mockdata` image (`tick → write files to ADLS landing zone`). Chosen over a
118	>   Function App (pandas/pyarrow is a heavy *batch*, not lightweight event glue — Functions
119	>   add packaging/cold-start friction) and over OS cron; reuses DataQ's Container Apps platform
120	>   + image, cron built in, pay-per-run. **This is *upstream* of the orchestrator** (source drops
121	>   files), which is cleaner/more realistic than the orchestrator also producing.
122	> - **Load + trigger (clock 2) = ADF/Airflow** load to Snowflake/UC → on-success trigger DataQ
123	>   (the path under test). **Deliberately mix two trigger modalities — not all event-driven:**
124	>     - **Event / file-landing** (ADF Storage-Event trigger / Airflow file-sensor or dataset DAG) —
125	>       fires when the Job drops a file. Use for high-frequency/latency-sensitive feeds (e.g. orders).
126	>     - **Schedule / time** (ADF Schedule or tumbling-window trigger / Airflow cron `schedule`) —
127	>       fires on a clock, processes whatever landed in the window. Use for daily/batch feeds
128	>       (e.g. inventory, feedback). **Set the load schedule to fire *after* the file-creation Job**
129	>       (e.g. Job drops inventory 01:00 → scheduled load 01:15) so there's data to pick up.
130	>     - _Why both:_ exercises both ADF/Airflow trigger types **and** DataQ's pipeline-run monitoring +
131	>       10-min polling / gap-recovery fallback (the poll only meaningfully bites on scheduled pipelines).
132	>   Flow C (flat-file in place) has no load step — the Job's file drop *is* the arrival; DataQ reads
133	>   in place (its own W5 schedule or arrival event).
134	>   Proposed split (adjustable): **orders → event**, **tracking → event**, **inventory → schedule**,
135	>   **feedback → schedule** — one event + one schedule per warehouse target (Snowflake & UC) for parity.
136	> - **Required by the Job runtime:** Container Apps Jobs are **ephemeral** → the generator's
137	>   state must move off local disk to **blob** (ADLS). `state.py` needs a pluggable backend
138	>   (local FS today; ADLS blob for the Job). See work items below.
139

(`mockdata/increment.py` + `state.py`)
141	- [x] **Persisted state** (`state/state.json` + `state/masters/*.parquet`): master pools + climbing id counters (`order_number` never collides) + open-shipment registry (a `tracking_number` from an orders tick gets `ready→in_transit→delivered` on successive tracking ticks). **Verified:** 2 order ticks → ranges 1–40 / 41–80, 0 collisions; tracking# identical across the 3 lifecycle batches; cross-feed FK integrity holds; ruff+black clean

217	## 6. Performance / scale testing (post-v1 / backlog)
218	
219	> Rides §2's parameterizable volume (`--seed` + a `--volume` knob): generate **S / M / L / XL** of the same
220	> datasets, run, measure, record. **Baseline-first** — establish numbers + a regression budget; no hard SLAs
221	> yet (set them once we know where the knees are). Standalone harness script; the **QA/QE agent (§4)** can
222	> invoke it later as a perf-smoke. Needs §2 (generators) + §3 (the run paths) green first.
223	
224	**Lead axes (do these first):**
225	- [ ] **Run scaling** *(headline)* — GX run wall-clock vs **rows × #checks-per-suite**, per datasource (Snowflake · UC · flat-file CSV+Parquet). Capture throughput (rows/sec) + **worker memory peak** (GX pulls the batch in-memory) — and note whether time is in the warehouse query or GX itself.
226	- [ ] **Profiler latency** — profile a **wide** table (many columns) to quantify the known **N+1 per-column top-values** cost ([#327](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/327)) and the payoff once it's batched.

=== terraform/README.md (head) ===
# DataQ harness — Terraform (§1 of HARNESS_TODO.md)

Provisions the **datasources** for the live test/demo-data environment (ADR 0021):
ADLS Gen2 landing zone, Snowflake DB/warehouse/reader-role, Unity Catalog
catalog+schemas, the ADF factory — **and the compute platform**: a shared Container
Apps Environment hosting Airflow (scheduler+webserver + Postgres metadata) and the
mockdata cron Jobs (§2a), behind a container registry. (ADF Managed Airflow was retired
for new instances 2026-01-01, so Airflow runs on Container Apps.)

**Secret-free by design:** every provider reads its credentials from the environment
exported by `secrets.sh`. No passwords/keys/tokens live in `.tf` files or outputs.

## Usage

```bash
cd ~/Coding/Python/DataQ-harness
source secrets.sh                 # exports ARM_* / SNOWFLAKE_* / DATABRICKS_* 
cd terraform
terraform init
terraform validate
terraform plan                    # review — creates nothing
terraform apply                   # provisions real, billable resources
```

### Apply-time prerequisite — subscription resource providers

The Terraform SP is Contributor on `dataq-rg` only, so it **cannot register
subscription resource providers** (`resource_provider_registrations = "none"`).
Before the first `apply`, a subscription **Owner** must register the RPs the
harness uses:

```bash
az provider register --namespace Microsoft.Storage
az provider register --namespace Microsoft.DataFactory
az provider register --namespace Microsoft.App                # Container Apps
az provider register --namespace Microsoft.OperationalInsights # Log Analytics
az provider register --namespace Microsoft.ContainerRegistry
az provider register --namespace Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL
az provider register --namespace Microsoft.EventGrid          # ADF blob-event trigger
```

`terraform plan`/`validate` pass without this (they only read the RG); `apply` will
403 on the matching resources if the RPs aren't registered.

### Sensitive vars for the ADF pipeline (§3a)

The ADF Snowflake linked service + the DataQ webhook URL need values not in the `.tf`
files — pass them as `TF_VAR_*` from the environment (never committed):

```bash
export TF_VAR_snowflake_password="$SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD"      # from secrets.sh
export TF_VAR_dataq_adf_webhook_secret="<DataQ ADF shared secret>"
export TF_VAR_dataq_webhook_base_url="https://<deployed-dataq>"
```

### Post-apply

```bash
terraform output                  # connection coordinates + airflow_url + acr_login_server
terraform output -raw airflow_admin_password   # Airflow web login (user = airflow_admin_user)

# Flow A — ADF event-driven load (the event half of the §2a trigger mix). §3a.
# A new orders file landing in ADLS fires a Storage-Event trigger → Copy ADLS→Snowflake
# → Web activity POSTs DataQ's ADF webhook (ADR 0006, shared secret in the URL) → DataQ
# records the pipeline_run + fires the bound suite.
#
# Auth is key-based: ADLS via account key, Snowflake via password in the connection
# string, DataQ via the shared-secret token. NOTE: the Copy activity's Snowflake
# staging + the Storage-Event trigger (needs Microsoft.EventGrid registered + the ADF
# managed identity granted on the storage account) are verified only at apply.

locals {
  snowflake_host = "${var.snowflake_organization_name}-${var.snowflake_account_name}.snowflakecomputing.com"

  adf_activities = jsonencode([
    {
      name    = "LoadOrdersToSnowflake"
      type    = "Copy"
      inputs  = [{ referenceName = azurerm_data_factory_dataset_delimited_text.orders_src.name, type = "DatasetReference" }]
      outputs = [{ referenceName = azurerm_data_factory_dataset_snowflake.orders_sink.name, type = "DatasetReference" }]

        source        = { type = "DelimitedTextSource" }
        sink          = { type = "SnowflakeSink", importSettings = { type = "SnowflakeImportCopyCommand" } }

        stagingSettings = {
          linkedServiceName = { referenceName = azurerm_data_factory_linked_service_azure_blob_storage.staging.name, type = "LinkedServiceReference" }
          path              = "staging"
        }
      }

1	# Flow A — ADF event-driven load (the event half of the §2a trigger mix). §3a.
2	# A new orders file landing in ADLS fires a Storage-Event trigger → Copy ADLS→Snowflake
3	# → Web activity POSTs DataQ's ADF webhook (ADR 0006, shared secret in the URL) → DataQ
4	# records the pipeline_run + fires the bound suite.
5	#
6	# Auth is key-based: ADLS via account key, Snowflake via password in the connection
7	# string, DataQ via the shared-secret token. NOTE: the Copy activity's Snowflake
8	# staging + the Storage-Event trigger (needs Microsoft.EventGrid registered + the ADF
9	# managed identity granted on the storage account) are verified only at apply.
10	
11	locals {
12	  snowflake_host = "${var.snowflake_organization_name}-${var.snowflake_account_name}.snowflakecomputing.com"
13	
14	  adf_activities = jsonencode([
15	    {
16	      name    = "LoadOrdersToSnowflake"
17	      type    = "Copy"
18	      inputs  = [{ referenceName = azurerm_data_factory_dataset_delimited_text.orders_src.name, type = "DatasetReference" }]
19	      outputs = [{ referenceName = azurerm_data_factory_dataset_snowflake.orders_sink.name, type = "DatasetReference" }]
20	      typeProperties = {
21	        source        = { type = "DelimitedTextSource" }
22	        sink          = { type = "SnowflakeSink", importSettings = { type = "SnowflakeImportCopyCommand" } }
23	        enableStaging = true
24	        stagingSettings = {
25	          linkedServiceName = { referenceName = azurerm_data_factory_linked_service_azure_blob_storage.staging.name, type = "LinkedServiceReference" }
26	          path              = "staging"
27	        }
28	      }
29	    },
30	    {
31	      name      = "NotifyDataQ"
32	      type      = "WebActivity"
33	      dependsOn = [{ activity = "LoadOrdersToSnowflake", dependencyConditions = ["Succeeded"] }]
34	      typeProperties = {
35	        url     = "${var.dataq_webhook_base_url}/api/v1/orchestration/events/adf?token=${var.dataq_adf_webhook_secret}"
36	        method  = "POST"
37	        headers = { "Content-Type" = "application/json" }
38	        body = {
39	          factoryName  = var.adf_factory_name
40	          pipelineName = "@{pipeline().Pipeline}"
41	          runId        = "@{pipeline().RunId}"
42	          status       = "Succeeded"
43	          start        = "@{pipeline().TriggerTime}"
44	          end          = "@{utcnow()}"
45	        }
46	      }
47	    },
48	  ])
49	}
50	
51	resource "azurerm_data_factory_linked_service_data_lake_storage_gen2" "adls" {
52	  name                = "ls_adls"
53	  data_factory_id     = azurerm_data_factory.dataq.id
54	  url                 = azurerm_storage_account.landing.primary_dfs_endpoint
55	  storage_account_key = azurerm_storage_account.landing.primary_access_key
56	}
57	
58	# Snowflake staging for the Copy (the Snowflake connector stages via blob).
59	resource "azurerm_data_factory_linked_service_azure_blob_storage" "staging" {
60	  name              = "ls_blob_staging"
61	  data_factory_id   = azurerm_data_factory.dataq.id
62	  connection_string = azurerm_storage_account.landing.primary_connection_string
63	}
64	
65	resource "azurerm_data_factory_linked_service_snowflake" "snowflake" {
66	  name            = "ls_snowflake"
67	  data_factory_id = azurerm_data_factory.dataq.id
68	  connection_string = join("", [
69	    "jdbc:snowflake://", local.snowflake_host, "/?user=", var.snowflake_reader_user,
70	    "&password=", var.snowflake_password, "&db=", var.snowflake_database,
71	    "&warehouse=", var.snowflake_warehouse, "&role=", var.snowflake_loader_role,
72	    "&schema=", var.snowflake_schemas[0],
73	  ])
74	}
75	
76	resource "azurerm_data_factory_dataset_delimited_text" "orders_src" {
77	  name                = "ds_orders_src"
78	  data_factory_id     = azurerm_data_factory.dataq.id
79	  linked_service_name = azurerm_data_factory_linked_service_data_lake_storage_gen2.adls.name
80	
81	  azure_blob_storage_location {
82	    container = var.adls_filesystems[0]
83	    path      = "snowflake/orders_header"
84	  }
85	  column_delimiter    = ","
86	  first_row_as_header = true
87	}
88	
89	resource "azurerm_data_factory_dataset_snowflake" "orders_sink" {
90	  name                = "ds_orders_sink"
91	  data_factory_id     = azurerm_data_factory.dataq.id
92	  linked_service_name = azurerm_data_factory_linked_service_snowflake.snowflake.name
93	  schema_name         = var.snowflake_schemas[0]
94	  table_name          = "ORDERS_HEADER"
95	}

100	  activities_json = local.adf_activities
101	}

103	# Storage-Event trigger: a new orders file → run the pipeline (the "event" modality).
104	resource "azurerm_data_factory_trigger_blob_event" "orders_landed" {
