119	    state = load_state(store)
120	    masters = load_masters(store)
121	    datasets, issues = tick(
122	        config,
123	        state,
124	        masters,
125	        args.feed,
126	        args.count,
127	        inject_issues=args.issues,
128	        volume_drop=args.volume_drop,
129	        stale=args.stale,
130	        schema_drift=args.schema_drift,
131	    )
132	    batch_id = f"b{state.batch_counter:06d}"
133	    entry = write_batch(datasets, config, batch_id, args.feed, issues)
134	    save_state(store, state)
135	
136	    rows = sum(d["rows"] for d in entry["datasets"].values())
137	    print(
138	        f"tick #{state.batch_counter} feed={args.feed} batch={batch_id}: {rows:,} rows"
139	    )
140	    for name, d in entry["datasets"].items():
141	        print(f"    {name:<20} {d['rows']:>6,} rows -> {d['file']}")
```

## 2. ADF error — `FormatBasedDatasetMissingFileName`

The Copy source points at the **folder** `snowflake/orders_header/` with no filename or wildcard, so ADF doesn't know which file(s) to read. The mockdata jobs write `orders_header_b000001.csv`, `…_b000002.csv`, etc. — so it needs a `*.csv` wildcard. Let me fix the source's `storeSettings`:

> TOOL

id: toolu_01NJPNULAM6GL8KxkbGvEv11
```json
{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ-harness/terraform/adf_pipeline.tf",
  "old_string": "        source        = { type = \"DelimitedTextSource\" }\n        sink          = { type = \"SnowflakeV2Sink\", importSettings = { type = \"SnowflakeImportCopyCommand\" } }",
  "new_string": "        source = {\n          type = \"DelimitedTextSource\"\n          # The dataset points at a folder; tell the Copy to glob the batch files\n          # (mockdata writes orders_header_b000001.csv, …) instead of a single file.\n          storeSettings = {\n            type             = \"AzureBlobFSReadSettings\"\n            recursive        = true\n            wildcardFileName = \"*.csv\"\n          }\n        }\n        sink = { type = \"SnowflakeV2Sink\", importSettings = { type = \"SnowflakeImportCopyCommand\" } }"
}

If you create a role assignment at the event hub level, the custom topic can forward events only to that specific event hub.\n### Create a role assignment for a Service Bus topic at various scopes\nThe following CLI example shows how to add an Event Grid custom topic's identity to the **Azure Service Bus Data Sender** role at the namespace level or at the Service Bus topic level. If you create the role assignment at the namespace level, the Event Grid topic can forward events to all entities (Service Bus queues or topics) within that namespace. If you create a role assignment at the Service Bus queue or topic level, the Event Grid custom topic can forward events only to that specific Service Bus queue or topic.","contentUrl":"https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/event-grid/add-identity-roles#use-the-azure-cli"},{"title":"Authenticate event delivery to event handlers (Azure Event Grid)","content":"# Authenticate event delivery to event handlers (Azure Event Grid)\nThis article provides information on authenticating event delivery to event handlers.\n## Overview\nAzure Event Grid uses different authentication methods to deliver events to event handlers. `\n| Authentication method | Supported event handlers | Description| \n|  --- | --- | ---  |\n| Access key | - Event Hubs<br>- Service Bus<br>- Storage Queues<br>- Relay Hybrid Connections<br>- Azure Functions<br>- Storage Blobs (Deadletter) | Event Grid service principal credentials fetch access keys. When you register the Event Grid resource provider in your Azure subscription, you grant Event Grid the necessary permissions. |\n| Managed System Identity & Role-based access control | - Event Hubs<br>- Service Bus<br>- Storage Queues<br>- Storage Blobs (Deadletter) | Enable managed system identity for the topic and add it to the appropriate role on the destination. For details, see Use system-assigned identities for event delivery. |\n| Bearer token authentication with Microsoft Entra protected webhook | Webhook | See the Authenticate event delivery to webhook endpoints section for details. |\n| Client secret as a query parameter | Webhook | See the Use client secret as a query parameter section for details. |\n\nNote\nIf you protect your Azure function with a Microsoft Entra app, you need to take the generic webhook approach by using the HTTP trigger. Use the Azure function endpoint as a webhook URL when adding the subscription.","contentUrl":"https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/event-grid/security-authentication"},{"title":"Use managed identities to deliver events in Azure Event Grid","content":"# Use managed identities to deliver events in Azure Event Grid\n## Create event subscriptions that use an identity\n```azurecli\nsubid=\"<AZURE SUBSCRIPTION ID>\"\nrg = \"<RESOURCE GROUP of EVENT GRID CUSTOM TOPIC>\"\ntopicname = \"<EVENT GRID TOPIC NAME>\"\n\n# get the service bus queue resource id\nqueueid=$(az servicebus queue show --namespace-name <SERVICE BUS NAMESPACE NAME> --name <QUEUE NAME> --resource-group <RESOURCE GROUP NAME> --query id --output tsv)\nsb_esname = \"<Specify a name for the event subscription>\"\n```\n#### Create an event subscription by using a managed identity for delivery\nThis command creates an event subscription for an Event Grid custom topic with the endpoint type set to **Service Bus queue**.\n```azurecli\naz eventgrid event-subscription create  \n    --source-resource-id /subscriptions/$subid/resourceGroups/$rg/providers/Microsoft.EventGrid/topics/$topicname\n    --delivery-identity-endpoint-type servicebusqueue  \n    --delivery-identity systemassigned \n    --delivery-identity-endpoint $queueid\n    -n $sb_esname\n```\n#### Create an event subscription by using a managed identity for delivery and dead-lettering\nThis sample command creates an event subscription for an Event Grid custom topic with an endpoint type set to **Service Bus queue**. It also specifies that the system-managed identity is to be used for dead-lettering.\n### Use the Azure CLI - Event Hubs\nIn this section, you learn how to use the Azure CLI to enable the use of a system-assigned identity to deliver events to an event hub. The identity must be a member of the **Azure Event Hubs Data Sender** role. It must also be a member of the **Storage Blob Data Contributor** role on the storage account that's used for dead-lettering.\n#### Define variables\n```azurecli\nsubid=\"<AZURE SUBSCRIPTION ID>\"\nrg = \"<RESOURCE GROUP of EVENT GRID CUSTOM TOPIC>\"\ntopicname = \"<EVENT GRID CUSTOM TOPIC NAME>\"\n\nhubid=$(az eventhubs eventhub show --name <EVENT HUB NAME> --namespace-name <NAMESPACE NAME> --resource-group <RESOURCE GROUP NAME> --query id --output tsv)\neh_esname = \"<SPECIFY EVENT SUBSCRIPTION NAME>\"\n```\n#### Create an event subscription by using a managed identity for delivery\nThis sample command creates an event subscription for an Event Grid custom topic with an endpoint type set to **Event Hubs**.","contentUrl":"https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/event-grid/managed-service-identity#create-event-subscriptions-that-use-an-identity"},{"title":"Managed identity for Azure Data Factory","content":"# Managed identity for Azure Data Factory\n## Required Roles for Managed Identities\nTo effectively use managed identities in Azure Data Factory, specific roles must be assigned to ensure proper access and functionality. Below are the roles required:\n1. **System-Assigned Managed Identity**\n1.1. **Reader Role**: This role is necessary to read the metadata of the resources.\n1.2. **Contributor Role**: This role is required to manage the resources that the managed identity needs to access.\n2. **User-Assigned Managed Identity**\n2.1. **Managed Identity Operator Role**: This role allows the management of the user-assigned managed identity.\n2.2. **Reader Role**: This role is necessary to read the metadata of the resources.\n2.3. **Contributor Role**: This role is required to manage the resources that the managed identity needs to access.\nNote\n1. Users with the Data Factory Contributor role can create and run pipelines that use both the System‑assigned Managed Identity (SAMI) and any User‑assigned Managed Identities (UAMI) attached to the data factory. Those identities inherit all permissions already granted to them on external resources (for example, storage accounts, SQL databases, Key Vault, Fabric Lakehouse).\n2. Please assign the Contributor role only to trusted principals and on the narrowest scope possible. Review and limit the permissions granted to the data factory’s managed identities, use least‑privilege RBAC on downstream resources, and regularly audit role assignments and activity logs.","contentUrl":"https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/data-factory/data-factory-service-identity#required-roles-for-managed-identities"}]}

Good — this corrects what I told you earlier. Per the official docs, the ADF **managed identity needs *no* special permission**, and Event Grid needs none either. The only requirement is that the **identity that creates/starts the trigger** has, on the storage account, one of: Owner, Contributor, or `Microsoft.EventGrid/eventSubscriptions/write`. The Terraform SP is **Contributor on `dataq-rg`** — which covers the storage account — so it already qualifies. So there may be **no UI step needed at all**. Two problems: `rowDelimiter` is empty (conflicts with the set column delimiter), and the location type is `AzureBlobStorageLocation` but the linked service is **ADLS Gen2** (should be `AzureBlobFSLocation`, matching the `AzureBlobFSReadSettings` I added to the source). Let me fix both:

> TOOL

tool_use Edit
id: toolu_01WHKSGaJNALX8ArHHQ5DHau
```json
{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ-harness/terraform/adf_pipeline.tf",
  "old_string": "  azure_blob_storage_location {\n    container = var.adls_filesystems[0]\n    path      = \"snowflake/orders_header\"\n  }\n  column_delimiter    = \",\"\n  first_row_as_header = true\n}",
  "new_string": "  # ADLS Gen2 linked service → must be an AzureBlobFSLocation (not AzureBlobStorage),\n  # to match the AzureBlobFSReadSettings the Copy source uses.\n  azure_blob_fs_location {\n    file_system = var.adls_filesystems[0]\n    path        = \"snowflake/orders_header\"\n  }\n  column_delimiter    = \",\"\n  row_delimiter       = \"\\n\" # mockdata writes \\n line terminators; empty row delimiter + set column delimiter is rejected by ADF\n  first_row_as_header = true\n  quote_character     = \"\\\"\"\n  escape_character    = \"\\\\\"\n  encoding            = \"UTF-8\"\n}"
}
```

Good question — I checked the Snowflake V2 connector docs, and the answer is nuanced:

## Both already use the same ADLS Gen2 account — but the *staging* can't be an ADLS-Gen2-typed linked service

`ls_adls` (source) and `ls_blob_staging` (staging) both point at the **same** storage account (`dataqharness3erlgd`, which is HNS/ADLS Gen2). The difference is the *linked-service type*, and that's a hard connector requirement:

> "To use [staged copy], create an **Azure Blob storage** linked service that refers to the Azure storage account as the interim staging."

The Snowflake V2 staged copy **only** accepts an Azure *Blob*-typed staging linked service — there's no ADLS-Gen2-typed staging option. So no, we can't make that one ADLS Gen2; it must stay Blob-type (against the same account). That part is already correct.

## But two real problems are coming regardless

The next run will hit them, so flagging now:

1. **Staging auth must be SAS, not account key.** The docs: *"When you don't specify `storageIntegration` in the sink, the staging Azure Blob Storage linked service **need to use shared access signature authentication** as required by the Snowflake COPY command."* Our `ls_blob_staging` uses an account-key **connection string** → the COPY will fail. Fix = generate a SAS and switch the staging linked service to it.

2. **The Snowflake role can't write.** The linked service loads with `DATAQ_READER` (least-priv, read-only). The Copy sink needs INSERT/CREATE on `RETAIL.ORDERS_HEADER` (which also has to exist or use auto-create-table). A read-only role can't load.

## My recommendation

The ADF **event trigger itself is proven** (it fires on file landing — that was your actual question, and it's ✅, no UI step). The *Copy-to-Snowflake* mechanics are where ADF's Snowflake connector gets fussy (SAS staging + a write role + target table). Meanwhile the **Airflow schedule path** (`flow_a_snowflake_load`, `write_pandas`) loads to Snowflake directly with none of that friction.

So which do you want?

  "new_string": "# Grant the reader role to the existing user DataQ authenticates as.\nresource \"snowflake_grant_account_role\" \"reader_to_user\" {\n  role_name = snowflake_account_role.reader.name\n  user_name = var.snowflake_reader_user\n}\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Loader (dev) role — the harness ETL (Airflow + ADF) writes with this; it has\n# CREATE TABLE + write DML so loads can create/populate the RETAIL tables.\n# Kept distinct from the read-only DATAQ_READER that DataQ checks run as.\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\nresource \"snowflake_account_role\" \"loader\" {\n  name    = var.snowflake_loader_role\n  comment = \"DataQ harness ETL role: USAGE + CREATE TABLE + write DML for Airflow/ADF loads.\"\n}\n\nresource \"snowflake_grant_privileges_to_account_role\" \"loader_wh_usage\" {\n  account_role_name = snowflake_account_role.loader.name\n  privileges        = [\"USAGE\"]\n  on_account_object {\n    object_type = \"WAREHOUSE\"\n    object_name = snowflake_warehouse.dataq.name\n  }\n}\n\nresource \"snowflake_grant_privileges_to_account_role\" \"loader_db_usage\" {\n  account_role_name = snowflake_account_role.loader.name\n  privileges        = [\"USAGE\"]\n  on_account_object {\n    object_type = \"DATABASE\"\n    object_name = snowflake_database.dataq.name\n  }\n}\n\n# USAGE + CREATE TABLE on each schema (so a load can create the target table).\nresource \"snowflake_grant_privileges_to_account_role\" \"loader_schema\" {\n  for_each          = snowflake_schema.schemas\n  account_role_name = snowflake_account_role.loader.name\n  privileges        = [\"USAGE\", \"CREATE TABLE\"]\n  on_schema {\n    schema_name = \"\\\"${snowflake_database.dataq.name}\\\".\\\"${each.value.name}\\\"\"\n  }\n}\n\n# Full write DML on current + future tables in each schema.\nresource \"snowflake_grant_privileges_to_account_role\" \"loader_tables_future\" {\n  for_each          = snowflake_schema.schemas\n  account_role_name = snowflake_account_role.loader.name\n  privileges        = [\"SELECT\", \"INSERT\", \"UPDATE\", \"DELETE\", \"TRUNCATE\", \"REFERENCES\"]\n  on_schema_object {\n    future {\n      object_type_plural = \"TABLES\"\n      in_schema          = \"\\\"${snowflake_database.dataq.name}\\\".\\\"${each.value.name}\\\"\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n\nresource \"snowflake_grant_privileges_to_account_role\" \"loader_tables_existing\" {\n  for_each          = snowflake_schema.schemas\n  account_role_name = snowflake_account_role.loader.name\n  privileges        = [\"SELECT\", \"INSERT\", \"UPDATE\", \"DELETE\", \"TRUNCATE\", \"REFERENCES\"]\n  on_schema_object {\n    all {\n      object_type_plural = \"TABLES\"\n      in_schema          = \"\\\"${snowflake_database.dataq.name}\\\".\\\"${each.value.name}\\\"\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n\nresource \"snowflake_grant_account_role\" \"loader_to_user\" {\n  role_name = snowflake_account_role.loader.name\n  user_name = var.snowflake_reader_user\n}"
}

  "old_string": "# Snowflake staging for the Copy (the Snowflake connector stages via blob).\nresource \"azurerm_data_factory_linked_service_azure_blob_storage\" \"staging\" {\n  name              = \"ls_blob_staging\"\n  data_factory_id   = azurerm_data_factory.dataq.id\n  connection_string = azurerm_storage_account.landing.primary_connection_string\n}",
  "new_string": "# Snowflake staging for the Copy (the Snowflake connector stages via blob).\n# Snowflake's COPY command requires the staging Blob linked service to use **SAS**\n# auth (account-key connection string is rejected) — so generate an account SAS.\ndata \"azurerm_storage_account_sas\" \"staging\" {\n  connection_string = azurerm_storage_account.landing.primary_connection_string\n  https_only        = true\n\n  resource_types {\n    service   = true\n    container = true\n    object    = true\n  }\n  services {\n    blob  = true\n    queue = false\n    table = false\n    file  = false\n  }\n\n  # Fixed window (disposable harness) to avoid a timestamp()-driven perpetual diff.\n  start  = \"2026-01-01T00:00:00Z\"\n  expiry = \"2027-01-01T00:00:00Z\"\n\n  permissions {\n    read    = true\n    write   = true\n    delete  = true\n    list    = true\n    add     = true\n    create  = true\n    update  = false\n    process = false\n    tag     = false\n    filter  = false\n  }\n}\n\nresource \"azurerm_data_factory_linked_service_azure_blob_storage\" \"staging\" {\n  name            = \"ls_blob_staging\"\n  data_factory_id = azurerm_data_factory.dataq.id\n  sas_uri         = \"https://${azurerm_storage_account.landing.name}.blob.core.windows.net${data.azurerm_storage_account_sas.staging.sas}\"\n}"
}

# Harness Airflow image — apache/airflow + key-based client libs + the DAGs baked in.
# Once built+pushed to the registry, set Terraform's `airflow_image` to this

I'll resolve that trigger detail (it's a minor API body/error-handling quirk; the DAGs are parsed and creds are wired) — but let me answer your two questions now, since they're about the architecture.

## 1. Who loads what, and where data resides

**The source clock (upstream of everything):** the 4 **mockdata Container Apps Jobs** (`mockdata-orders/-tracking/-inventory/-feedback`, on crons) generate batch files into the ADLS **`landing`** zone. Nothing loads until they drop files.

| Dataset | Lands in | Loaded / produced by | Final residence | Read by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **orders_header** | ADLS `landing/snowflake/` | **ADF event pipeline** (storage-event trigger → Copy) ✅ *proven, 240 rows* | Snowflake `DATAQ_DB.RETAIL` | DataQ `DATAQ_READER` |
| order_lines, payments, refunds, returns, customers, products | ADLS `landing/snowflake/` | **Airflow `flow_a_snowflake_load`** (schedule, `write_pandas` auto-create) | Snowflake `RETAIL` | DataQ `DATAQ_READER` |
| location, promotions, channel | ADLS `landing/` | **Airflow `flow_a_uc_reference`** (schedule) | UC `dataq_retail.reference` | DataQ (UC read) |
| sales_events, feedback (bronze→silver→gold) | ADLS `landing/databricks_medallion/bronze/` | **Databricks medallion notebook** (submitted by Airflow `flow_b_medallion`) | UC `dataq_retail.raw/silver/gold` | DataQ (UC read) |
| logistics tracking (CSV), inventory snapshot (Parquet) | ADLS `landing/adls_flatfile/` | mockdata jobs only — **no load step** | stays a flat file in ADLS | DataQ FlatFileCheckRunner (in place) |

So the **two load modalities** you asked for: **event** = ADF (orders), **schedule** = Airflow (everything else). And the **role split you specified**: ETL writes with **`DATAQ_LOADER`** (Snowflake) / the admin PAT (Databricks); **DataQ reads with `DATAQ_READER`** / least-priv UC grants.

## 2. Secrets — why no Key Vault

**Deliberate** — the harness is **key-based by decision** (logged 2026-06-26), *not* Key Vault. Two reasons:

1. **The Terraform SP is Contributor on `dataq-rg` only — it can't create role assignments.** Key Vault done properly = each app's managed identity granted a Key Vault role = a role assignment the SP can't make (needs Owner/User Access Administrator). Same permission wall that forced local ACR builds and the UI-created UC catalog.
2. **It's a disposable test harness, not the product.** DataQ *the product* uses the SecretStore seam → Azure Key Vault (ADR 0010/0013). The harness is the environment DataQ runs *against*.

Where secrets actually live (none in any git-tracked file):

| Layer | Holds | Protection |
|---|---|---|
| `secrets.sh` (harness root) | SP creds, Snowflake pw, Databricks PAT | chmod 600, **gitignored**; sourced into env before TF/CLI |
| `terraform.tfstate` (local) | generated secrets + values TF reads | **gitignored** |
| **Container Apps `secret {}` blocks** | ACR pw, ADLS conn string, Snowflake pw, Postgres conn, Fernet/admin keys | platform-encrypted at rest; referenced by env via `secret_name` — **this is the KV substitute** |
| `random_password`/`random_id`/`azurerm_storage_account_sas` | Postgres pw, Airflow keys, staging SAS | generated, never hardcoded |

**Auth mechanisms** (all key-based per the decision): ADLS = account key/connection string + SAS for Snowflake staging; Snowflake = user+password; Databricks = PAT; ACR = admin creds. **Trade-off** (logged): long-lived account-wide keys in Container App secrets / TF state. The documented upgrade path is managed-identity + RBAC *if the harness outlives the demo* — which needs an Owner to do the role assignments.

| # | New entity (table) | Key columns | Relates to | Residence / load | DQ value it unlocks | Seeded issue |

| 2b | **suppliers** (dim) + **purchase_orders** (fact) | suppliers: supplier_id,name,country,lead_time_days,active · PO: po_number,supplier_id,sku_id,qty_ordered,qty_received,order_date,expected_date,received_date,status | PO→suppliers, PO→products | suppliers: UC `reference` · PO: Snowflake · Airflow schedule | **freshness** on inbound (received vs expected), FK integrity, **volume/anomaly** on daily PO count, `qty_received≤qty_ordered` | stale received_date; orphan supplier_id; qty_received>ordered |
| 2c | **fulfillment_nodes** (dim) + **order_fulfillment** (fact) | nodes: node_id,node_type(DC/store/3PL),region,city,active · of: order_number,node_id,fulfilled_ts,ship_method | of→orders, of→nodes | nodes: UC `reference` · of: Snowflake · Airflow schedule | FK integrity order→node (join target beyond store Location) | orphan node_id; orders missing fulfillment |
| 2d | **categories** (catalog hierarchy) | category_id, category_name, department, brand | products gains `category_id` FK | UC `reference`; products(Snowflake) gains FK | **orphan / FK-integrity** product→category | orphan category_id on some products |
| 2e | **date_dim** (calendar) | date_key, date, fiscal_week, fiscal_quarter, fiscal_year, season, is_holiday | join dim for all dated facts | UC `reference` | completeness (no date gaps); trend-slice dim | a missing date (gap) |
| 2f | **exchange_rates** + **discounts** | rates: currency,rate_date,rate_to_usd · discounts: order_number,discount_type,amount | rates↔orders.currency; discounts→orders | UC `reference` (rates) · Snowflake (discounts) · Airflow schedule | freshness on rates; `order_total` accounts for discount (reconcile) | stale rate_date; discount not reflected in order_total |
| 2g | **cancellations** (entity, optional) | cancellation_id, order_number, reason, cancelled_ts | only orders.status='cancelled' | Snowflake · Airflow schedule | consistency: status='cancelled' ⟺ cancellation row | cancelled order missing its row |

=== config.py ===
"""Generation config: volume tiers + the §2 route map (dataset -> run path / format).

No secrets, no cloud calls — this module only describes *what* to generate and
*where each dataset lands*. The emit layer (emit.py) writes to a local out/ dir
mirroring the route map; uploading to ADLS / loading to Snowflake/UC is a later
step (§3, once Terraform §1 is applied).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Volume tiers — scale knobs for perf testing (§6 rides these via --tier).
# Counts are "base entities"; transactional tables fan out from them.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

VOLUME_TIERS: dict[str, dict[str, int]] = {
    "S": {"customers": 200, "products": 150, "stores": 8, "promos": 15, "orders": 800},
    "M": {
        "customers": 1_000,
        "products": 600,
        "stores": 25,
        "promos": 40,
        "orders": 4_000,
    },
    "L": {
        "customers": 5_000,
        "products": 2_500,
        "stores": 80,
        "promos": 120,
        "orders": 20_000,
    },
    "XL": {
        "customers": 20_000,
        "products": 8_000,
        "stores": 250,
        "promos": 300,
        "orders": 100_000,
    },
}

DEFAULT_TIER = "S"

TAX_RATE = 0.08  # flat sales-tax rate: order_total = subtotal + subtotal * TAX_RATE


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Route map (§2) — which dataset lands on which DataQ run path + file format.
# emit.py uses `subdir` + `fmt` to lay out the output tree.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Route:
    """Where a generated dataset belongs in the DataQ run-path topology."""

    flow: str  # "A-snowflake" | "A-uc" | "B-medallion" | "C-flatfile"
    subdir: str  # path under out/ root
    fmt: str  # "csv" | "parquet" | "json"


ROUTES: dict[str, Route] = {
    # Flow A — load to warehouse (Snowflake): transactional + financial core.
    "products": Route("A-snowflake", "snowflake/products", "csv"),
    "customers": Route("A-snowflake", "snowflake/customers", "csv"),
    "orders_header": Route("A-snowflake", "snowflake/orders_header", "csv"),
    "order_lines": Route("A-snowflake", "snowflake/order_lines", "csv"),
    "payments": Route("A-snowflake", "snowflake/payments", "csv"),
    "refunds": Route("A-snowflake", "snowflake/refunds", "csv"),
    "returns": Route("A-snowflake", "snowflake/returns", "csv"),
    # Flow A — Unity Catalog plain load: governed reference data (no medallion).
    "locations": Route("A-uc", "unity_catalog/locations", "parquet"),
    "channels": Route("A-uc", "unity_catalog/channels", "parquet"),
    "promotions": Route("A-uc", "unity_catalog/promotions", "parquet"),
    # Flow B — medallion bronze source (Databricks notebook refines bronze->silver->gold).
    "sales_events": Route(
        "B-medallion", "databricks_medallion/bronze/sales_events", "json"
    ),
    "feedback": Route("B-medallion", "databricks_medallion/bronze/feedback", "json"),
    # Flow C — flat-file in place (ADLS). Batch-resolved.
    "tracking_events": Route("C-flatfile", "adls_flatfile/logistics_tracking", "csv"),
    "inventory_snapshot": Route(
        "C-flatfile", "adls_flatfile/inventory_snapshot", "parquet"
    ),
}


@dataclass
class GenConfig:
    """Resolved generation parameters for one run."""

    tier: str = DEFAULT_TIER
    seed: int = 42
    out_dir: str = "out"
    state_dir: str = "state"  # incremental-tick state (§2a)
    inject_issues: bool = True
    issue_rate: float = 0.03  # fraction of rows touched by deliberate DQ issues
    snapshots: int = (
        5  # inventory daily snapshots (exercises batch resolution + freshness)
    )
    tracking_batches: tuple[str, ...] = ("ready", "in_transit", "delivered")
    counts: dict[str, int] = field(default_factory=dict)

    def resolve(self) -> GenConfig:
        if self.tier not in VOLUME_TIERS:
            raise ValueError(
                f"unknown tier {self.tier!r}; choose from {list(VOLUME_TIERS)}"
            )
        self.counts = dict(VOLUME_TIERS[self.tier])
        return self

1	"""Retail dataset generator with referential consistency (§2).
2	
3	One system-of-record per entity. Shared key pools (sku_id, customer_id, store_id,
4	order_number, tracking_number) mean the same id denotes the same entity everywhere —
5	so the cross-dataset reconciliation / FK-orphan / join checks measure *real* DQ, not
6	generation noise. The only inconsistencies are the deliberate ones injected by
7	dq_issues.py.
8	
9	Timestamps are anchored to generation wall-clock `now` (offsets are seeded): the
10	*latest* inventory snapshot / tracking-delivered batch are genuinely fresh, so the
11	reserved freshness monitors (ADR 0012) bite. Everything else is reproducible per seed.
12	
13	Returns a uniform dict[str, DataFrame]. Multi-file datasets carry a split column:
14	  - tracking_events: `batch`          (emit.py -> one CSV per batch)
15	  - inventory_snapshot: `snapshot_date` (emit.py -> one Parquet per date)
16	"""
17	
18	from __future__ import annotations
19	
20	import datetime as dt
21	
22	import pandas as pd
23	
24	from .config import TAX_RATE, GenConfig
25	from .pools import (
26	    CARRIERS,
27	    CHANNEL_WEIGHTS,
28	    CHANNELS,
29	    CITIES,
30	    COLORS,
31	    FIRST_NAMES,
32	    LAST_NAMES,
33	    MATERIALS,
34	    PAYMENT_METHODS,
35	    PRODUCT_CATEGORIES,
36	    PROMO_TYPES,
37	    RETURN_REASONS,
38	    SIZES,
39	    STREETS,
40	    SURVEY_COMMENTS,
41	)
42	from .rng import Rng
43	
44	
45	def generate(config: GenConfig) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
46	    rng = Rng(config.seed)
47	    now = dt.datetime.now().replace(microsecond=0)
48	    c = config.counts
49	
50	    products = _products(rng, c["products"], now)
51	    customers = _customers(rng, c["customers"], now)
52	    locations = _locations(rng, c["stores"])
53	    channels = _channels()
54	    promotions = _promotions(rng, c["promos"], now)
55	
56	    sku_ids = products["sku_id"].tolist()
57	    customer_ids = customers["customer_id"].tolist()
58	    store_ids = locations["store_id"].tolist()
59	    promo_ids = promotions["promo_id"].tolist()
60	
61	    orders_header, order_lines = _orders(
62	        rng, c["orders"], now, sku_ids, customer_ids, store_ids, promo_ids, products
63	    )
64	    order_totals = dict(
65	        zip(orders_header["order_number"], orders_header["order_total"])
66	    )
67	
68	    payments = _payments(rng, orders_header)
69	    refunds = _refunds(rng, orders_header, order_totals)
70	    returns = _returns(rng, order_lines, now)
71	
72	    sales_events = _sales_events(orders_header)
73	    feedback = _feedback(rng, customers, now)
74	
75	    tracking_events = _tracking_events(rng, orders_header, now, config.tracking_batches)
76	    inventory_snapshot = _inventory_snapshot(
77	        rng, sku_ids, store_ids, now, config.snapshots
78	    )
79	
80	    return {
81	        "products": products,
82	        "customers": customers,
83	        "locations": locations,
84	        "channels": channels,
85	        "promotions": promotions,
86	        "orders_header": orders_header,
87	        "order_lines": order_lines,
88	        "payments": payments,
89	        "refunds": refunds,
90	        "returns": returns,
91	        "sales_events": sales_events,
92	        "feedback": feedback,
93	        "tracking_events": tracking_events,
94	        "inventory_snapshot": inventory_snapshot,
95	    }
96	
97	
98	# --- master data -----------------------------------------------------------
99	
100	
101	def _products(rng: Rng, n: int, now: dt.datetime) -> pd.DataFrame:
102	    skus = rng.id_pool("SKU", n)
103	    rows = []
104	    for sku in skus:
105	        rows.append(
106	            {
107	                "sku_id": sku,
108	                "style_id": f"STY-{rng.randint(1000, 9999)}",
109	                "category": rng.choice(PRODUCT_CATEGORIES),
110	                "color": rng.choice(COLORS),
111	                "material": rng.choice(MATERIALS),
112	                "size": rng.choice(SIZES),
113	                "unit_price": rng.money(8.0, 240.0),
114	                "active": rng.chance(0.92),
115	                "created_at": rng.datetime_between(now - dt.timedelta(days=720), now),
116	            }
117	        )
118	    return pd.DataFrame(rows)
119	
120	
121	def _customers(rng: Rng, n: int, now: dt.datetime) -> pd.DataFrame:
122	    ids = rng.id_pool("CUST", n)
123	    rows = []
124	    for cid in ids:
125	        first = rng.choice(FIRST_NAMES)
126	        last = rng.choice(LAST_NAMES)
127	        city, state = rng.choice(CITIES)
128	        rows.append(
129	            {
130	                "customer_id": cid,
131	                "first_name": first,
132	                "last_name": last,
133	                "email": f"{first}.{last}{rng.randint(1, 999)}@example.com".lower(),  # PII (#226)
134	                "phone": f"+1-555-{rng.randint(100, 999)}-{rng.randint(1000, 9999)}",  # PII
135	                "street": f"{rng.randint(100, 9999)} {rng.choice(STREETS)}",
136	                "city": city,
137	                "state": state,
138	                "signup_date": rng.datetime_between(
139	                    now - dt.timedelta(days=1000), now
140	                ).date(),
141	                "marketing_opt_in": rng.chance(0.6),
142	            }
143	        )
144	    return pd.DataFrame(rows)
145	
146	
147	def _locations(rng: Rng, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
148	    ids = rng.id_pool("STORE", n, width=4)
149	    rows = []
150	    for sid in ids:
151	        city, state = rng.choice(CITIES)
152	        open_h = rng.randint(7, 10)
153	        rows.append(
154	            {
155	                "store_id": sid,
156	                "store_name": f"{city} {rng.choice(['Center', 'Plaza', 'Market', 'Square'])}",
157	                "street": f"{rng.randint(100, 9999)} {rng.choice(STREETS)}",
158	                "city": city,
159	                "state": state,
160	                "open_hour": open_h,
161	                "close_hour": open_h + rng.randint(8, 12),
162	            }
163	        )
164	    return pd.DataFrame(rows)
165	
166	
167	def _channels() -> pd.DataFrame:
168	    return pd.DataFrame(
169	        {
170	            "channel": CHANNELS,
171	            "description": [
172	                "Web storefront",
173	                "Physical retail",
174	                "Third-party marketplace",
175	            ],
176	            "is_online": [True, False, True],
177	        }
178	    )
179	
180	
181	def _promotions(rng: Rng, n: int, now: dt.datetime) -> pd.DataFrame:
182	    ids = rng.id_pool("PROMO", n, width=4)
183	    rows = []
184	    for pid in ids:
185	        start = rng.datetime_between(now - dt.timedelta(days=180), now).date()
186	        ptype = rng.choice(PROMO_TYPES)
187	        rows.append(
188	            {
189	                "promo_id": pid,
190	                "promo_type": ptype,
191	                "value": (
192	                    rng.randint(5, 40)
193	                    if ptype == "percent_off"
194	                    else rng.money(5.0, 50.0) if ptype == "amount_off" else 0
195	                ),
196	                "channel": rng.weighted(CHANNELS + [None], CHANNEL_WEIGHTS + [0.3]),
197	                "start_date": start,
198	                "end_date": start + dt.timedelta(days=rng.randint(7, 60)),
199	            }
200	        )
201	    return pd.DataFrame(rows)
202	
203	
204	# --- transactional core ----------------------------------------------------
205	
206	
207	def _orders(
208	    rng: Rng,
209	    n: int,
210	    now: dt.datetime,
211	    sku_ids: list[str],
212	    customer_ids: list[str],
213	    store_ids: list[str],
214	    promo_ids: list[str],
215	    products: pd.DataFrame,
216	) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
217	    """Header + line items. subtotal = sum(line_total); order_total = subtotal + tax.
218	
219	    This intra-dataset tie-out (sum(line_total) == order_total) is reconciliation
220	    target #1 (ADR 0014) — shaped clean here; dq_issues.py breaks a few on purpose.
221	    """
222	    price_by_sku = dict(zip(products["sku_id"], products["unit_price"]))
223	    order_numbers = rng.id_pool("ORD", n, width=8)
224	
225	    h: dict[str, list] = {
226	        k: []
227	        for k in (
228	            "order_number",
229	            "customer_id",
230	            "channel",
231	            "store_id",
232	            "promo_id",
233	            "order_ts",
234	            "status",
235	            "subtotal",
236	            "tax",
237	            "order_total",
238	            "currency",
239	        )
240	    }
241	    line_rows: dict[str, list] = {
242	        k: []
243	        for k in (
244	            "line_id",
245	            "order_number",
246	            "sku_id",
247	            "qty",
248	            "unit_price",
249	            "line_total",
250	        )
251	    }
252	    line_seq = 0
253	
254	    for order_number in order_numbers:
255	        channel = rng.weighted(CHANNELS, CHANNEL_WEIGHTS)
256	        store_id = None if channel == "online" else rng.choice(store_ids)
257	        n_lines = rng.randint(1, 5)
258	        subtotal = 0.0
259	        for _ in range(n_lines):
260	            line_seq += 1
261	            sku = rng.choice(sku_ids)
262	            qty = rng.randint(1, 4)
263	            unit_price = round(price_by_sku[sku], 2)
264	            line_total = round(qty * unit_price, 2)
265	            subtotal += line_total
266	            line_rows["line_id"].append(f"OL-{line_seq:09d}")
267	            line_rows["order_number"].append(order_number)
268	            line_rows["sku_id"].append(sku)
269	            line_rows["qty"].append(qty)
270	            line_rows["unit_price"].append(unit_price)
271	            line_rows["line_total"].append(line_total)
272	
273	        subtotal = round(subtotal, 2)
274	        tax = round(subtotal * TAX_RATE, 2)
275	        order_total = round(subtotal + tax, 2)
276	        h["order_number"].append(order_number)
277	        h["customer_id"].append(rng.choice(customer_ids))
278	        h["channel"].append(channel)
279	        h["store_id"].append(store_id)
280	        h["promo_id"].append(rng.choice(promo_ids) if rng.chance(0.3) else None)
281	        h["order_ts"].append(rng.datetime_between(now - dt.timedelta(days=120), now))
282	        h["status"].append(
283	            rng.weighted(
284	                ["placed", "shipped", "delivered", "returned", "cancelled"],
285	                [0.15, 0.2, 0.5, 0.1, 0.05],
286	            )
287	        )
288	        h["subtotal"].append(subtotal)
289	        h["tax"].append(tax)
290	        h["order_total"].append(order_total)
291	        h["currency"].append("USD")
292	
293	    return pd.DataFrame(h), pd.DataFrame(line_rows)
294	
295	
296	def _payments(rng: Rng, orders: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
297	    """captured_amount == order_total when captured — reconciliation target #2."""
298	    rows = []
299	    for _, o in orders.iterrows():
300	        status = rng.weighted(["captured", "authorized", "failed"], [0.9, 0.06, 0.04])
301	        captured = float(o["order_total"]) if status == "captured" else 0.0
302	        rows.append(
303	            {
304	                "payment_id": f"PAY-{o['order_number'][4:]}",
305	                "order_number": o["order_number"],
306	                "method": rng.choice(PAYMENT_METHODS),
307	                "status": status,
308	                "captured_amount": round(captured, 2),
309	                "paid_ts": o["order_ts"] + dt.timedelta(minutes=rng.randint(1, 90)),
310	            }
311	        )
312	    return pd.DataFrame(rows)
313	
314	
315	def _refunds(
316	    rng: Rng, orders: pd.DataFrame, order_totals: dict[str, float]
317	) -> pd.DataFrame:
318	    rows = []
319	    refundable = orders[orders["status"].isin(["returned", "cancelled"])]
320	    for _, o in refundable.iterrows():
321	        total = order_totals[o["order_number"]]
322	        rows.append(
323	            {
324	                "refund_id": f"REF-{o['order_number'][4:]}",
325	                "order_number": o["order_number"],
326	                "refund_amount": round(total * rng.uniform(0.3, 1.0), 2),
327	                "reason": rng.choice(RETURN_REASONS),
328	                "refund_ts": o["order_ts"] + dt.timedelta(days=rng.randint(1, 21)),
329	            }
330	        )
331	    return pd.DataFrame(rows)
332	
333	
334	def _returns(rng: Rng, lines: pd.DataFrame, now: dt.datetime) -> pd.DataFrame:
335	    sample = lines.sample(frac=0.08, random_state=7) if len(lines) else lines
336	    rows = []
337	    for i, ln in enumerate(sample.itertuples(index=False), start=1):
338	        rows.append(
339	            {
340	                "return_id": f"RET-{i:08d}",
341	                "order_number": ln.order_number,
342	                "sku_id": ln.sku_id,
343	                "qty": min(ln.qty, rng.randint(1, 2)),
344	                "reason": rng.choice(RETURN_REASONS),
345	                "channel": rng.weighted(CHANNELS, CHANNEL_WEIGHTS),
346	                "return_ts": now - dt.timedelta(days=rng.randint(0, 60)),
347	            }
348	        )
349	    return pd.DataFrame(rows)
350	
351	
352	# --- Flow B medallion bronze sources ---------------------------------------
353	
354	
355	def _sales_events(orders: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
356	    """One row per (order, lifecycle event). gold.daily_revenue rolls these up and
357	    must reconcile back to Snowflake order_total (cross-platform comparison, ADR 0014).
358	    """
359	    rows = []
360	    for _, o in orders.iterrows():
361	        base_ts = o["order_ts"]
362	        for k, (etype, offset_h) in enumerate(
363	            [("placed", 0), ("shipped", 24), ("audited", 72)]
364	        ):
365	            rows.append(
366	                {
367	                    "event_id": f"EVT-{o['order_number'][4:]}-{k}",
368	                    "order_number": o["order_number"],
369	                    "event_type": etype,
370	                    "event_ts": base_ts + dt.timedelta(hours=offset_h),
371	                    "channel": o["channel"],
372	                    "store_id": o["store_id"],
373	                    "amount": float(o["order_total"]) if etype == "placed" else None,
374	                }
375	            )
376	    return pd.DataFrame(rows)
377	
378	
379	def _feedback(rng: Rng, customers: pd.DataFrame, now: dt.datetime) -> pd.DataFrame:
380	    sample = (
381	        customers.sample(frac=0.4, random_state=11) if len(customers) else customers
382	    )
383	    rows = []
384	    for i, cust in enumerate(sample.itertuples(index=False), start=1):
385	        rows.append(
386	            {
387	                "feedback_id": f"FB-{i:08d}",
388	                "customer_id": cust.customer_id,
389	                "channel": rng.weighted(CHANNELS, CHANNEL_WEIGHTS),
390	                "rating": rng.randint(1, 5),
391	                "comment": rng.choice(SURVEY_COMMENTS),
392	                "email": cust.email,  # PII — silver layer redacts (#226)
393	                "created_ts": now - dt.timedelta(days=rng.randint(0, 90)),
394	            }
395	        )
396	    return pd.DataFrame(rows)
397	
398	
399	# --- Flow C flat files -----------------------------------------------------
400	
401	
402	def _tracking_events(
403	    rng: Rng, orders: pd.DataFrame, now: dt.datetime, batches: tuple[str, ...]
404	) -> pd.DataFrame:
405	    """A shipment keeps ONE tracking_number across ready->in_transit->delivered events
406	    that arrive in separate batches (§2). emit.py splits by `batch` into CSV files."""
407	    shipped = orders[orders["status"].isin(["shipped", "delivered", "returned"])]
408	    status_for_batch = {
409	        "ready": "ready_for_shipment",
410	        "in_transit": "in_transit",
411	        "delivered": "delivered",
412	    }
413	    # batch recency: ready oldest, delivered newest (so freshness on delivered passes).
414	    batch_age_days = {"ready": 5, "in_transit": 2, "delivered": 0}
415	    rows = []
416	    for _, o in shipped.iterrows():
417	        tracking_number = f"TRK{o['order_number'][4:]}"
418	        carrier = rng.choice(CARRIERS)
419	        city, _ = rng.choice(CITIES)
420	        for batch in batches:
421	            rows.append(
422	                {
423	                    "tracking_number": tracking_number,
424	                    "order_number": o["order_number"],
425	                    "carrier": carrier,
426	                    "status": status_for_batch[batch],
427	                    "event_ts": now
428	                    - dt.timedelta(
429	                        days=batch_age_days[batch], hours=rng.randint(0, 12)
430	                    ),
431	                    "location_city": city,
432	                    "batch": batch,
433	                }
434	            )
435	    return pd.DataFrame(rows)
436	
437	
438	def _inventory_snapshot(
439	    rng: Rng, sku_ids: list[str], store_ids: list[str], now: dt.datetime, snapshots: int
440	) -> pd.DataFrame:
441	    """Daily snapshot over a stable sku x store grid. emit.py splits by `snapshot_date`
442	    into Parquet (zero-copy Arrow read, PR #140). The latest snapshot is fresh (load_ts
443	    ~now) so freshness passes; volume band / anomaly ride the per-day row counts."""
444	    # Keep the grid bounded for large tiers — sample sku/store pairs once, reuse daily.
445	    grid_skus = sku_ids if len(sku_ids) <= 400 else rng.sample(sku_ids, 400)
446	    grid_stores = store_ids if len(store_ids) <= 20 else rng.sample(store_ids, 20)
447	    pairs = [(s, st) for s in grid_skus for st in grid_stores]
448	
449	    rows = []
450	    for d in range(snapshots):
451	        snap_date = (now - dt.timedelta(days=snapshots - 1 - d)).date()
452	        load_ts = now - dt.timedelta(days=snapshots - 1 - d, hours=rng.randint(0, 3))
453	        for sku, store in pairs:
454	            rows.append(
455	                {
456	                    "sku_id": sku,
457	                    "store_id": store,
458	                    "on_hand": rng.randint(0, 500),
459	                    "planned": rng.randint(0, 200),
460	                    "snapshot_date": snap_date,
461	                    "load_ts": load_ts,
462	                }
463	            )
464	    return pd.DataFrame(rows)
465

1	"""Seeded randomness — every value derives from one `random.Random(seed)` so a
2	given (--tier, --seed) reproduces byte-for-byte. No third-party deps (no Faker):
3	stdlib random + curated pools (pools.py) give tighter control over the referential
4	consistency §2 demands than Faker would.
5	"""
6	
7	from __future__ import annotations
8	
9	import datetime as dt
10	import random
11	from collections.abc import Sequence
12	from typing import TypeVar
13	
14	T = TypeVar("T")
15	
16	
17	class Rng:
18	    """Thin convenience wrapper over random.Random with id/date helpers."""
19	
20	    def __init__(self, seed: int) -> None:
21	        self._r = random.Random(seed)
22	
23	    # --- primitives -------------------------------------------------------
24	    def choice(self, seq: Sequence[T]) -> T:
25	        return self._r.choice(seq)
26	
27	    def choices(
28	        self, seq: Sequence[T], weights: Sequence[float], k: int = 1
29	    ) -> list[T]:
30	        return self._r.choices(seq, weights=weights, k=k)
31	
32	    def weighted(self, seq: Sequence[T], weights: Sequence[float]) -> T:
33	        return self._r.choices(seq, weights=weights, k=1)[0]
34	
35	    def randint(self, lo: int, hi: int) -> int:
36	        return self._r.randint(lo, hi)
37	
38	    def uniform(self, lo: float, hi: float) -> float:
39	        return self._r.uniform(lo, hi)
40	
41	    def money(self, lo: float, hi: float) -> float:
42	        return round(self._r.uniform(lo, hi), 2)
43	
44	    def chance(self, p: float) -> bool:
45	        return self._r.random() < p
46	
47	    def sample(self, seq: Sequence[T], k: int) -> list[T]:
48	        return self._r.sample(list(seq), k)
49	
50	    def shuffle(self, seq: list[T]) -> None:
51	        self._r.shuffle(seq)
52	
53	    # --- ids --------------------------------------------------------------
54	    def id_pool(self, prefix: str, n: int, width: int = 6) -> list[str]:
55	        """A stable, ordered pool of human-readable ids (e.g. SKU-000001)."""
56	        return [f"{prefix}-{i:0{width}d}" for i in range(1, n + 1)]
57	
58	    # --- dates ------------------------------------------------------------
59	    def datetime_between(self, start: dt.datetime, end: dt.datetime) -> dt.datetime:
60	        span = int((end - start).total_seconds())
61	        return start + dt.timedelta(seconds=self._r.randint(0, max(span, 1)))
62

1	"""Deliberate DQ-issue injection (§2: "seed some deliberate DQ issues … so checks
2	actually fail — proves severity tiers + alerting, not just green dashboards").
3	
4	Every injected issue is recorded in a manifest (written by emit.py as
5	`_dq_issues_manifest.json`) so the QA/QE agent (§4) can assert the checks fail
6	*exactly* where we broke the data — and nowhere else (that's why referential
7	consistency in generate.py matters: no accidental failures to confuse the signal).
8	
9	Row-level issues are applied here (mutating the in-memory frames). The cross-file
10	schema-drift issue is applied in emit.py (it perturbs one snapshot file's columns)
11	and appended to the same manifest.
12	"""
13	
14	from __future__ import annotations
15	
16	import datetime as dt
17	
18	import pandas as pd
19	
20	from .config import GenConfig
21	
22	
23	def inject(datasets: dict[str, pd.DataFrame], config: GenConfig) -> list[dict]:
24	    """Mutate `datasets` in place; return the list of injected-issue records."""
25	    issues: list[dict] = []
26	    rate = config.issue_rate
27	
28	    def record(kind: str, dataset: str, detail: str, keys: list) -> None:
29	        issues.append(
30	            {
31	                "kind": kind,
32	                "dataset": dataset,
33	                "detail": detail,
34	                "n": len(keys),
35	                "keys": keys[:50],
36	            }
37	        )
38	
39	    # 1. Nulls — required dimension / PII columns.
40	    orders = datasets["orders_header"]
41	    idx = _sample_idx(orders, rate, seed=101)
42	    orders.loc[idx, "channel"] = None
43	    record(
44	        "null",
45	        "orders_header",
46	        "channel set NULL (required slice dimension)",
47	        orders.loc[idx, "order_number"].tolist(),
48	    )
49	
50	    customers = datasets["customers"]
51	    idx = _sample_idx(customers, rate, seed=102)
52	    customers.loc[idx, "email"] = None
53	    record(
54	        "null",
55	        "customers",
56	        "email set NULL (PII / contactability)",
57	        customers.loc[idx, "customer_id"].tolist(),
58	    )
59	
60	    # 2. Duplicates — exact-row dupes break uniqueness checks.
61	    lines = datasets["order_lines"]
62	    dup = lines.sample(frac=rate, random_state=103)
63	    datasets["order_lines"] = pd.concat([lines, dup], ignore_index=True)
64	    record(
65	        "duplicate",
66	        "order_lines",
67	        "exact-row duplicates appended",
68	        dup["line_id"].tolist(),
69	    )
70	
71	    products = datasets["products"]
72	    dup_sku = products.sample(
73	        n=max(1, int(len(products) * rate * 0.5)), random_state=104
74	    )
75	    datasets["products"] = pd.concat([products, dup_sku], ignore_index=True)
76	    record(
77	        "duplicate",
78	        "products",
79	        "duplicate sku_id rows (PK violation)",
80	        dup_sku["sku_id"].tolist(),
81	    )
82	
83	    # 3. FK orphans — point a few children at non-existent parents.
84	    lines = datasets["order_lines"]
85	    idx = _sample_idx(lines, rate * 0.5, seed=105)
86	    lines.loc[idx, "sku_id"] = "SKU-000000"  # never generated
87	    record(
88	        "fk_orphan",
89	        "order_lines",
90	        "sku_id -> non-existent product SKU-000000",
91	        lines.loc[idx, "line_id"].tolist(),
92	    )
93	
94	    idx = _sample_idx(orders, rate * 0.5, seed=106)
95	    orders.loc[idx, "customer_id"] = "CUST-000000"  # never generated
96	    record(
97	        "fk_orphan",
98	        "orders_header",
99	        "customer_id -> non-existent CUST-000000",
100	        orders.loc[idx, "order_number"].tolist(),
101	    )
102	
103	    # 4. Reconciliation mismatch #1 — sum(line_total)+tax != order_total (ADR 0014).
104	    idx = _sample_idx(orders, rate * 0.5, seed=107)
105	    orders.loc[idx, "order_total"] = (orders.loc[idx, "order_total"] * 1.15).round(2)
106	    record(
107	        "reconciliation",
108	        "orders_header",
109	        "order_total inflated vs sum(line_total)+tax",
110	        orders.loc[idx, "order_number"].tolist(),
111	    )
112	
113	    # 5. Reconciliation mismatch #2 — captured_amount != order_total.
114	    payments = datasets["payments"]
115	    captured = payments[payments["status"] == "captured"]
116	    if len(captured):
117	        idx = _sample_idx(captured, rate * 0.5, seed=108)
118	        payments.loc[idx, "captured_amount"] = (
119	            payments.loc[idx, "captured_amount"] - 7.77
120	        ).round(2)
121	        record(
122	            "reconciliation",
123	            "payments",
124	            "captured_amount != order_total (underpayment)",
125	            payments.loc[idx, "payment_id"].tolist(),
126	        )
127	
128	    # 6. Stale freshness — push the LATEST inventory snapshot's load_ts ~26h back so a
129	    #    "last load < 1h/24h" freshness monitor FAILS on the newest batch.
130	    inv = datasets["inventory_snapshot"]
131	    latest_date = inv["snapshot_date"].max()
132	    latest_mask = inv["snapshot_date"] == latest_date
133	    inv.loc[latest_mask, "load_ts"] = inv.loc[latest_mask, "load_ts"] - dt.timedelta(
134	        hours=26
135	    )
136	    record(
137	        "stale",
138	        "inventory_snapshot",
139	        f"latest snapshot {latest_date} load_ts pushed 26h back",
140	        [str(latest_date)],
141	    )
142	
143	    # 7. Volume drop — gut a mid snapshot's row count for a volume-band / anomaly hit.
144	    dates = sorted(inv["snapshot_date"].unique())
145	    if len(dates) >= 3:
146	        drop_date = dates[len(dates) // 2]
147	        drop_mask = inv["snapshot_date"] == drop_date
148	        keep = inv[~drop_mask]
149	        thinned = inv[drop_mask].sample(frac=0.3, random_state=109)
150	        datasets["inventory_snapshot"] = pd.concat([keep, thinned], ignore_index=True)
151	        record(
152	            "volume_drop",
153	            "inventory_snapshot",
154	            f"snapshot {drop_date} thinned to ~30% rows",
155	            [str(drop_date)],
156	        )
157	
158	    return issues
159	
160	
161	def _sample_idx(df: pd.DataFrame, frac: float, seed: int) -> pd.Index:
162	    n = max(1, int(len(df) * frac))
163	    return df.sample(n=min(n, len(df)), random_state=seed).index
164

1	"""Write generated datasets to the §2 route-map tree, on any `Store` (storage.py) —
2	local FS for dev / a mounted volume, or ADLS Gen2 blob for the Container Apps Job
3	(`--out adls://<acct>/<filesystem>[/<prefix>]`). Paths are relative; the store roots them.
4	
5	Layout under the out root:
6	  snowflake/<table>/<table>.csv                 Flow A -> Snowflake (COPY INTO source)
7	  unity_catalog/<table>/<table>.parquet         Flow A -> UC plain load
8	  databricks_medallion/bronze/<src>/<src>.json  Flow B -> medallion bronze (NDJSON)
9	  adls_flatfile/logistics_tracking/tracking_events_<batch>.csv   Flow C (event-append)
10	  adls_flatfile/inventory_snapshot/inventory_<date>.parquet      Flow C (daily snapshot)
11	
12	`write` = one-shot backfill (§2). `write_batch` = one incremental tick (§2a),
13	batch-suffixed (`<name>_<batch_id>.<fmt>`) since landing zones are append-style.
14	
15	Sidecar manifests at the out root:
16	  _manifest.json / _ticks.jsonl            what was written
17	  _dq_issues_manifest.json[l]              the deliberate failures
18	"""
19	
20	from __future__ import annotations
21	
22	import json
23	from io import BytesIO, StringIO
24	
25	import pandas as pd
26	
27	from .config import ROUTES, GenConfig
28	from .storage import Store, make_store
29	
30	
31	def _df_bytes(df: pd.DataFrame, fmt: str) -> bytes:
32	    if fmt == "csv":
33	        sbuf = StringIO()
34	        df.to_csv(sbuf, index=False)
35	        return sbuf.getvalue().encode()
36	    if fmt == "parquet":
37	        buf = BytesIO()
38	        df.to_parquet(buf, index=False)
39	        return buf.getvalue()
40	    if fmt == "json":  # NDJSON bronze raw
41	        sbuf = StringIO()
42	        df.to_json(sbuf, orient="records", lines=True, date_format="iso")
43	        return sbuf.getvalue().encode()
44	    raise ValueError(f"unknown format {fmt!r}")
45	
46	
47	def _put(store: Store, rel: str, df: pd.DataFrame, fmt: str) -> str:
48	    store.write_bytes(rel, _df_bytes(df, fmt))
49	    return rel
50	
51	
52	def write(
53	    datasets: dict[str, pd.DataFrame], config: GenConfig, dq_issues: list[dict]
54	) -> dict:
55	    store = make_store(config.out_dir)
56	    file_manifest: dict[str, dict] = {}
57	
58	    for name, df in datasets.items():
59	        route = ROUTES[name]
60	        if name == "tracking_events":
61	            files = _write_tracking(store, df)
62	        elif name == "inventory_snapshot":
63	            files, drift = _write_inventory(store, df, config.inject_issues)
64	            if drift:
65	                dq_issues.append(drift)
66	        else:
67	            files = [_put(store, f"{route.subdir}/{name}.{route.fmt}", df, route.fmt)]
68	
69	        file_manifest[name] = {
70	            "flow": route.flow,
71	            "format": route.fmt,
72	            "rows": len(df),
73	            "files": files,
74	        }
75	
76	    store.write_bytes(
77	        "_manifest.json", json.dumps(file_manifest, indent=2, default=str).encode()
78	    )
79	    store.write_bytes(
80	        "_dq_issues_manifest.json",
81	        json.dumps(dq_issues, indent=2, default=str).encode(),
82	    )
83	    return file_manifest
84	
85	
86	def write_batch(
87	    datasets: dict[str, pd.DataFrame],
88	    config: GenConfig,
89	    batch_id: str,
90	    feed: str,
91	    issues: list[dict],
92	) -> dict:
93	    """One incremental tick (§2a): batch-suffixed files into the route subdirs."""
94	    store = make_store(config.out_dir)
95	    entry: dict = {"batch_id": batch_id, "feed": feed, "datasets": {}}
96	    for name, df in datasets.items():
97	        route = ROUTES[name]
98	        rel = f"{route.subdir}/{name}_{batch_id}.{route.fmt}"
99	        _put(store, rel, df, route.fmt)
100	        entry["datasets"][name] = {"rows": len(df), "file": rel}
101	
102	    store.append_text("_ticks.jsonl", json.dumps(entry, default=str) + "\n")
103	    for it in issues:
104	        store.append_text(
105	            "_dq_issues_manifest.jsonl",
106	            json.dumps({**it, "batch_id": batch_id}, default=str) + "\n",
107	        )
108	    return entry
109	
110	
111	def _write_tracking(store: Store, df: pd.DataFrame) -> list[str]:
112	    subdir = ROUTES["tracking_events"].subdir
113	    files = []
114	    for batch, group in df.groupby("batch"):
115	        rel = f"{subdir}/tracking_events_{batch}.csv"
116	        files.append(_put(store, rel, group.drop(columns=["batch"]), "csv"))
117	    return files
118	
119	
120	def _write_inventory(
121	    store: Store, df: pd.DataFrame, inject_drift: bool
122	) -> tuple[list[str], dict | None]:
123	    subdir = ROUTES["inventory_snapshot"].subdir
124	    files: list[str] = []
125	    drift: dict | None = None
126	    latest_date = df["snapshot_date"].max()
127	    for snap_date, group in df.groupby("snapshot_date"):
128	        out = group.drop(columns=["snapshot_date"])
129	        if inject_drift and snap_date == latest_date:
130	            out = out.rename(
131	                columns={"on_hand": "qty_on_hand"}
132	            )  # schema drift on newest load
133	            drift = {
134	                "kind": "schema_drift",
135	                "dataset": "inventory_snapshot",
136	                "detail": f"newest snapshot {snap_date} renames on_hand -> qty_on_hand",
137	                "n": 1,
138	                "keys": [str(snap_date)],
139	            }
140	        files.append(
141	            _put(store, f"{subdir}/inventory_{snap_date}.parquet", out, "parquet")
142	        )
143	    return files, drift
144

1	"""Incremental `tick` generators (§2a) — one batch per call, continuing state.
2	
3	Each feed ticks at its own cadence (driven externally by Airflow/ADF schedules):
4	masters rarely change · orders 4x/day · tracking 2x/day · inventory daily ·
5	feedback every 2 days. Referential consistency holds *across* ticks because every
6	tick draws from the persisted master pools and the climbing id counters in
7	`HarnessState` — the only inconsistencies are deliberate (the --issues / anomaly flags).
8	"""
9	
10	from __future__ import annotations
11	
12	import datetime as dt
13	
14	import pandas as pd
15	
16	from .config import TAX_RATE, GenConfig
17	from .generate import (
18	    _channels,
19	    _customers,
20	    _locations,
21	    _products,
22	    _promotions,
23	)
24	from .pools import (
25	    CARRIERS,
26	    CHANNEL_WEIGHTS,
27	    CHANNELS,
28	    CITIES,
29	    PAYMENT_METHODS,
30	    RETURN_REASONS,
31	    SURVEY_COMMENTS,
32	    TRACKING_STATUSES,
33	)
34	from .rng import Rng
35	from .state import HarnessState, save_masters, save_state
36	from .storage import make_store
37	
38	FEEDS = ("orders", "tracking", "inventory", "feedback")
39	
40	# Per-tick default batch sizes (override with --count). Scales mildly with tier.
41	_TICK_ORDERS = {"S": 40, "M": 120, "L": 400, "XL": 1500}
42	_TICK_FEEDBACK = {"S": 15, "M": 50, "L": 150, "XL": 500}
43	
44	
45	# --- init ------------------------------------------------------------------
46	
47	
48	def init_state(config: GenConfig) -> tuple[dict[str, pd.DataFrame], HarnessState]:
49	    """Generate + persist the master pools; return them for an initial emit."""
50	    rng = Rng(config.seed)
51	    now = dt.datetime.now().replace(microsecond=0)
52	    c = config.counts
53	    masters = {
54	        "products": _products(rng, c["products"], now),
55	        "customers": _customers(rng, c["customers"], now),
56	        "locations": _locations(rng, c["stores"]),
57	        "channels": _channels(),
58	        "promotions": _promotions(rng, c["promos"], now),
59	    }
60	    state = HarnessState(seed=config.seed, tier=config.tier, created_at=now.isoformat())
61	    store = make_store(config.state_dir)
62	    save_masters(store, masters)
63	    save_state(store, state)
64	    return masters, state
65	
66	
67	# --- tick dispatch ---------------------------------------------------------
68	
69	
70	def tick(
71	    config: GenConfig,
72	    state: HarnessState,
73	    masters: dict[str, pd.DataFrame],
74	    feed: str,
75	    count: int | None,
76	    *,
77	    inject_issues: bool = False,
78	    volume_drop: bool = False,
79	    stale: bool = False,
80	    schema_drift: bool = False,
81	) -> tuple[dict[str, pd.DataFrame], list[dict]]:
82	    """Produce one batch for `feed`, mutating `state` in place. Caller persists state."""
83	    state.batch_counter += 1
84	    rng = Rng(config.seed + state.batch_counter)  # deterministic per (seed, tick)
85	    now = dt.datetime.now().replace(microsecond=0)
86	
87	    if feed == "orders":
88	        n = count or _TICK_ORDERS[config.tier]
89	        return _tick_orders(rng, now, state, masters, n, inject_issues)
90	    if feed == "tracking":
91	        return _tick_tracking(rng, now, state)
92	    if feed == "inventory":
93	        return _tick_inventory(
94	            rng, now, state, masters, volume_drop, stale, schema_drift
95	        )
96	    if feed == "feedback":
97	        n = count or _TICK_FEEDBACK[config.tier]
98	        return _tick_feedback(rng, now, state, masters, n)
99	    raise ValueError(f"unknown feed {feed!r}; choose from {FEEDS}")
100	
101	
102	# --- orders ----------------------------------------------------------------
103	
104	
105	def _tick_orders(
106	    rng: Rng,
107	    now: dt.datetime,
108	    state: HarnessState,
109	    masters: dict[str, pd.DataFrame],
110	    n: int,
111	    inject_issues: bool,
112	) -> tuple[dict[str, pd.DataFrame], list[dict]]:
113	    products = masters["products"]
114	    price_by_sku = dict(zip(products["sku_id"], products["unit_price"]))
115	    sku_ids = products["sku_id"].tolist()
116	    customer_ids = masters["customers"]["customer_id"].tolist()
117	    store_ids = masters["locations"]["store_id"].tolist()
118	    promo_ids = masters["promotions"]["promo_id"].tolist()
119	
120	    base_order = state.counters["order"]
121	    base_line = state.counters["line"]
122	    order_numbers = [f"ORD-{base_order + i:08d}" for i in range(1, n + 1)]
123	
124	    h: dict[str, list] = {
125	        k: []
126	        for k in (
127	            "order_number",
128	            "customer_id",
129	            "channel",
130	            "store_id",
131	            "promo_id",
132	            "order_ts",
133	            "status",
134	            "subtotal",
135	            "tax",
136	            "order_total",
137	            "currency",
138	        )
139	    }
140	    lines: dict[str, list] = {
141	        k: []
142	        for k in (
143	            "line_id",
144	            "order_number",
145	            "sku_id",
146	            "qty",
147	            "unit_price",
148	            "line_total",
149	        )
150	    }
151	    payments_rows, refunds_rows, returns_rows, sales_rows = [], [], [], []
152	    line_seq = base_line
153	    return_seq = state.counters["return"]
154	
155	    for order_number in order_numbers:
156	        channel = rng.weighted(CHANNELS, CHANNEL_WEIGHTS)
157	        store_id = None if channel == "online" else rng.choice(store_ids)
158	        subtotal = 0.0
159	        n_lines = rng.randint(1, 5)
160	        for _ in range(n_lines):
161	            line_seq += 1
162	            sku = rng.choice(sku_ids)
163	            qty = rng.randint(1, 4)
164	            unit_price = round(price_by_sku[sku], 2)
165	            line_total = round(qty * unit_price, 2)
166	            subtotal += line_total
167	            lines["line_id"].append(f"OL-{line_seq:09d}")
168	            lines["order_number"].append(order_number)
169	            lines["sku_id"].append(sku)
170	            lines["qty"].append(qty)
171	            lines["unit_price"].append(unit_price)
172	            lines["line_total"].append(line_total)
173	
174	        subtotal = round(subtotal, 2)
175	        tax = round(subtotal * TAX_RATE, 2)
176	        order_total = round(subtotal + tax, 2)
177	        order_ts = now - dt.timedelta(minutes=rng.randint(0, 360))
178	        status = rng.weighted(
179	            ["placed", "shipped", "delivered", "returned", "cancelled"],
180	            [0.2, 0.25, 0.4, 0.1, 0.05],
181	        )
182	        h["order_number"].append(order_number)
183	        h["customer_id"].append(rng.choice(customer_ids))
184	        h["channel"].append(channel)
185	        h["store_id"].append(store_id)
186	        h["promo_id"].append(rng.choice(promo_ids) if rng.chance(0.3) else None)
187	        h["order_ts"].append(order_ts)
188	        h["status"].append(status)
189	        h["subtotal"].append(subtotal)
190	        h["tax"].append(tax)
191	        h["order_total"].append(order_total)
192	        h["currency"].append("USD")
193	
194	        suffix = order_number[4:]
195	        pay_status = rng.weighted(
196	            ["captured", "authorized", "failed"], [0.9, 0.06, 0.04]
197	        )
198	        payments_rows.append(
199	            {
200	                "payment_id": f"PAY-{suffix}",
201	                "order_number": order_number,
202	                "method": rng.choice(PAYMENT_METHODS),
203	                "status": pay_status,
204	                "captured_amount": round(
205	                    order_total if pay_status == "captured" else 0.0, 2
206	                ),
207	                "paid_ts": order_ts + dt.timedelta(minutes=rng.randint(1, 90)),
208	            }
209	        )
210	        if status in ("returned", "cancelled"):
211	            refunds_rows.append(
212	                {
213	                    "refund_id": f"REF-{suffix}",
214	                    "order_number": order_number,
215	                    "refund_amount": round(order_total * rng.uniform(0.3, 1.0), 2),
216	                    "reason": rng.choice(RETURN_REASONS),
217	                    "refund_ts": order_ts + dt.timedelta(days=rng.randint(1, 21)),
218	                }
219	            )
220	            return_seq += 1
221	            returns_rows.append(
222	                {
223	                    "return_id": f"RET-{return_seq:08d}",
224	                    "order_number": order_number,
225	                    "sku_id": lines["sku_id"][-1],
226	                    "qty": 1,
227	                    "reason": rng.choice(RETURN_REASONS),
228	                    "channel": channel if channel else rng.choice(CHANNELS),
229	                    "return_ts": now - dt.timedelta(days=rng.randint(0, 5)),
230	                }
231	            )
232	        for k, (etype, off_h) in enumerate(
233	            [("placed", 0), ("shipped", 24), ("audited", 72)]
234	        ):
235	            sales_rows.append(
236	                {
237	                    "event_id": f"EVT-{suffix}-{k}",
238	                    "order_number": order_number,
239	                    "event_type": etype,
240	                    "event_ts": order_ts + dt.timedelta(hours=off_h),
241	                    "channel": channel,
242	                    "store_id": store_id,
243	                    "amount": order_total if etype == "placed" else None,
244	                }
245	            )
246	        # Register an open shipment for orders that ship (lifecycle plays out over ticks).
247	        if status in ("shipped", "delivered", "returned"):
248	            city, _ = rng.choice(CITIES)
249	            state.open_shipments.append(
250	                {
251	                    "tracking_number": f"TRK{suffix}",
252	                    "order_number": order_number,
253	                    "carrier": rng.choice(CARRIERS),
254	                    "city": city,
255	                    "stage": 0,
256	                }
257	            )
258	
259	    state.counters["order"] = base_order + n
260	    state.counters["line"] = line_seq
261	    state.counters["return"] = return_seq
262	
263	    datasets = {
264	        "orders_header": pd.DataFrame(h),
265	        "order_lines": pd.DataFrame(lines),
266	        "payments": pd.DataFrame(payments_rows),
267	        "refunds": pd.DataFrame(refunds_rows),
268	        "returns": pd.DataFrame(returns_rows),
269	        "sales_events": pd.DataFrame(sales_rows),
270	    }
271	    issues = _inject_order_issues(datasets, rng) if inject_issues else []
272	    return datasets, issues
273	
274	
275	def _inject_order_issues(datasets: dict[str, pd.DataFrame], rng: Rng) -> list[dict]:
276	    issues: list[dict] = []
277	    oh, ol = datasets["orders_header"], datasets["order_lines"]
278	    if len(oh) >= 3:
279	        idx = oh.sample(n=max(1, len(oh) // 20), random_state=1).index
280	        oh.loc[idx, "channel"] = None
281	        issues.append(
282	            {
283	                "kind": "null",
284	                "dataset": "orders_header",
285	                "detail": "channel NULL",
286	                "n": len(idx),
287	                "keys": oh.loc[idx, "order_number"].tolist(),
288	            }
289	        )
290	        idx2 = oh.sample(n=max(1, len(oh) // 30), random_state=2).index
291	        oh.loc[idx2, "order_total"] = (oh.loc[idx2, "order_total"] * 1.15).round(2)
292	        issues.append(
293	            {
294	                "kind": "reconciliation",
295	                "dataset": "orders_header",
296	                "detail": "order_total inflated",
297	                "n": len(idx2),
298	                "keys": oh.loc[idx2, "order_number"].tolist(),
299	            }
300	        )
301	    if len(ol) >= 3:
302	        idx3 = ol.sample(n=max(1, len(ol) // 30), random_state=3).index
303	        ol.loc[idx3, "sku_id"] = "SKU-000000"
304	        issues.append(
305	            {
306	                "kind": "fk_orphan",
307	                "dataset": "order_lines",
308	                "detail": "sku_id -> SKU-000000",
309	                "n": len(idx3),
310	                "keys": ol.loc[idx3, "line_id"].tolist(),
311	            }
312	        )
313	    return issues
314	
315	
316	# --- tracking (advance open shipments one lifecycle stage) ------------------
317	
318	
319	def _tick_tracking(
320	    rng: Rng, now: dt.datetime, state: HarnessState
321	) -> tuple[dict[str, pd.DataFrame], list[dict]]:
322	    rows, still_open = [], []
323	    for ship in state.open_shipments:
324	        stage = ship["stage"]
325	        rows.append(
326	            {
327	                "tracking_number": ship["tracking_number"],
328	                "order_number": ship["order_number"],
329	                "carrier": ship["carrier"],
330	                "status": TRACKING_STATUSES[stage],
331	                "event_ts": now - dt.timedelta(minutes=rng.randint(0, 120)),
332	                "location_city": ship["city"],
333	            }
334	        )
335	        ship["stage"] = stage + 1
336	        if ship["stage"] < len(TRACKING_STATUSES):
337	            still_open.append(ship)  # more events to come on later ticks
338	    state.open_shipments = still_open
339	    return {"tracking_events": pd.DataFrame(rows)}, []
340	
341	
342	# --- inventory (one daily snapshot over the stable grid) --------------------
343	
344	
345	def _tick_inventory(
346	    rng: Rng,
347	    now: dt.datetime,
348	    state: HarnessState,
349	    masters: dict[str, pd.DataFrame],
350	    volume_drop: bool,
351	    stale: bool,
352	    schema_drift: bool,
353	) -> tuple[dict[str, pd.DataFrame], list[dict]]:
354	    sku_ids = masters["products"]["sku_id"].tolist()
355	    store_ids = masters["locations"]["store_id"].tolist()
356	    grid_skus = sku_ids[:400]
357	    grid_stores = store_ids[:20]
358	    load_ts = now - (dt.timedelta(hours=26) if stale else dt.timedelta(0))
359	    snap_date = now.date()
360	
361	    rows = [
362	        {
363	            "sku_id": sku,
364	            "store_id": store,
365	            "on_hand": rng.randint(0, 500),
366	            "planned": rng.randint(0, 200),
367	            "snapshot_date": snap_date,
368	            "load_ts": load_ts,
369	        }
370	        for sku in grid_skus
371	        for store in grid_stores
372	    ]
373	    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
374	
375	    issues: list[dict] = []
376	    if volume_drop:
377	        df = df.sample(frac=0.3, random_state=9).reset_index(drop=True)
378	        issues.append(
379	            {
380	                "kind": "volume_drop",
381	                "dataset": "inventory_snapshot",
382	                "detail": f"{snap_date} thinned to ~30%",
383	                "n": 1,
384	                "keys": [str(snap_date)],
385	            }
386	        )
387	    if stale:
388	        issues.append(
389	            {
390	                "kind": "stale",
391	                "dataset": "inventory_snapshot",
392	                "detail": f"{snap_date} load_ts +26h back",
393	                "n": 1,
394	                "keys": [str(snap_date)],
395	            }
396	        )
397	    if schema_drift:
398	        df = df.rename(columns={"on_hand": "qty_on_hand"})
399	        issues.append(
400	            {
401	                "kind": "schema_drift",
402	                "dataset": "inventory_snapshot",
403	                "detail": f"{snap_date} on_hand -> qty_on_hand",
404	                "n": 1,
405	                "keys": [str(snap_date)],
406	            }
407	        )
408	
409	    state.last_inventory_date = str(snap_date)
410	    return {"inventory_snapshot": df}, issues
411	
412	
413	# --- feedback --------------------------------------------------------------
414	
415	
416	def _tick_feedback(
417	    rng: Rng,
418	    now: dt.datetime,
419	    state: HarnessState,
420	    masters: dict[str, pd.DataFrame],
421	    n: int,
422	) -> tuple[dict[str, pd.DataFrame], list[dict]]:
423	    customers = masters["customers"]
424	    sample = customers.sample(
425	        n=min(n, len(customers)), random_state=state.batch_counter
426	    )
427	    base_fb = state.counters["feedback"]
428	    rows = []
429	    for i, cust in enumerate(sample.itertuples(index=False), start=1):
430	        rows.append(
431	            {
432	                "feedback_id": f"FB-{base_fb + i:08d}",
433	                "customer_id": cust.customer_id,
434	                "channel": rng.weighted(CHANNELS, CHANNEL_WEIGHTS),
435	                "rating": rng.randint(1, 5),
436	                "comment": rng.choice(SURVEY_COMMENTS),
437	                "email": cust.email,
438	                "created_ts": now,
439	            }
440	        )
441	    state.counters["feedback"] = base_fb + len(rows)
442	    return {"feedback": pd.DataFrame(rows)}, []
443

1	"""Persisted harness state for incremental `tick` generation (§2a).
2	
3	The §2 backfill is stateless one-shot. Recurring ticks need continuity *across*
4	runs: the same master pools, climbing id sequences (no `order_number` collisions),
5	and open shipments (a tracking_number created on an earlier tick gets its next
6	lifecycle event on a later tick). That continuity lives here.
7	
8	Storage is behind the shared **`Store` seam** (storage.py) so the same state works
9	whether ticks run locally (filesystem) or as the ephemeral **Container Apps Job**
10	(ADLS blob — local disk doesn't survive between Job runs). Build a store from a URI
11	with `make_store` (`adls://…` -> ADLS, else local path).
12	
13	Logical contents (relative names the store holds):
14	  state.json              counters, open_shipments, last_inventory_date, batch_counter
15	  masters/<name>.parquet  products, customers, locations, channels, promotions
16	"""
17	
18	from __future__ import annotations
19	
20	import json
21	from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
22	from io import BytesIO
23	
24	import pandas as pd
25	
26	from .storage import Store
27	
28	MASTER_NAMES = ("products", "customers", "locations", "channels", "promotions")
29	STATE_FILE = "state.json"
30	
31	
32	@dataclass
33	class HarnessState:
34	    seed: int
35	    tier: str
36	    created_at: str
37	    batch_counter: int = 0
38	    counters: dict[str, int] = field(
39	        default_factory=lambda: {"order": 0, "line": 0, "return": 0, "feedback": 0}
40	    )
41	    last_inventory_date: str | None = None
42	    open_shipments: list[dict] = field(default_factory=list)
43	
44	    @classmethod
45	    def from_dict(cls, d: dict) -> HarnessState:
46	        return cls(**d)
47	
48	
49	# --- state + masters IO (store-agnostic) -----------------------------------
50	
51	
52	def state_exists(store: Store) -> bool:
53	    return store.exists(STATE_FILE)
54	
55	
56	def save_state(store: Store, state: HarnessState) -> None:
57	    store.write_bytes(
58	        STATE_FILE, json.dumps(asdict(state), indent=2, default=str).encode()
59	    )
60	
61	
62	def load_state(store: Store) -> HarnessState:
63	    if not state_exists(store):
64	        raise FileNotFoundError("no state found — run `python -m mockdata init` first")
65	    return HarnessState.from_dict(json.loads(store.read_bytes(STATE_FILE)))
66	
67	
68	def save_masters(store: Store, masters: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> None:
69	    for name in MASTER_NAMES:
70	        buf = BytesIO()
71	        masters[name].to_parquet(buf, index=False)
72	        store.write_bytes(f"masters/{name}.parquet", buf.getvalue())
73	
74	
75	def load_masters(store: Store) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
76	    return {
77	        name: pd.read_parquet(BytesIO(store.read_bytes(f"masters/{name}.parquet")))
78	        for name in MASTER_NAMES
79	    }
80	
```
