  "old_string": "def _products(rng: Rng, n: int, now: dt.datetime) -> pd.DataFrame:\n    skus = rng.id_pool(\"SKU\", n)\n    rows = []\n    for sku in skus:\n        rows.append(\n            {\n                \"sku_id\": sku,\n                \"style_id\": f\"STY-{rng.randint(1000, 9999)}\",\n                \"category\": rng.choice(PRODUCT_CATEGORIES),\n                \"color\": rng.choice(COLORS),\n                \"material\": rng.choice(MATERIALS),\n                \"size\": rng.choice(SIZES),\n                \"unit_price\": rng.money(8.0, 240.0),\n                \"active\": rng.chance(0.92),\n                \"created_at\": rng.datetime_between(now - dt.timedelta(days=720), now),\n            }\n        )\n    return pd.DataFrame(rows)",
  "new_string": "def _products(\n    rng: Rng, n: int, now: dt.datetime, category_ids: list[str] | None = None\n) -> pd.DataFrame:\n    skus = rng.id_pool(\"SKU\", n)\n    rows = []\n    for sku in skus:\n        rows.append(\n            {\n                \"sku_id\": sku,\n                \"style_id\": f\"STY-{rng.randint(1000, 9999)}\",\n                \"category\": rng.choice(PRODUCT_CATEGORIES),\n                # FK into the catalog hierarchy (categories dim) for orphan checks.\n                \"category_id\": rng.choice(category_ids) if category_ids else None,\n                \"color\": rng.choice(COLORS),\n                \"material\": rng.choice(MATERIALS),\n                \"size\": rng.choice(SIZES),\n                \"unit_price\": rng.money(8.0, 240.0),\n                \"active\": rng.chance(0.92),\n                \"created_at\": rng.datetime_between(now - dt.timedelta(days=720), now),\n            }\n        )\n    return pd.DataFrame(rows)\n\n\n# --- extended reference dimensions -----------------------------------------\n\n\ndef _categories(rng: Rng) -> pd.DataFrame:\n    \"\"\"Catalog hierarchy above Product: category -> department + brand. Stable PK\n    category_id is the FK target for products (orphan / FK-integrity checks).\"\"\"\n    rows = []\n    cid = 0\n    for cat in PRODUCT_CATEGORIES:\n        for dept in DEPARTMENTS:\n            cid += 1\n            rows.append(\n                {\n                    \"category_id\": f\"CAT-{cid:04d}\",\n                    \"category_name\": cat,\n                    \"department\": dept,\n                    \"brand\": rng.choice(BRANDS),\n                }\n            )\n    return pd.DataFrame(rows)\n\n\ndef _suppliers(rng: Rng, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:\n    rows = []\n    for sid in rng.id_pool(\"SUP\", n, width=4):\n        rows.append(\n            {\n                \"supplier_id\": sid,\n                \"supplier_name\": f\"{rng.choice(BRANDS)} {rng.choice(['Supply', 'Mills', 'Trading', 'Works'])}\",\n                \"country\": rng.choice(COUNTRIES),\n                \"lead_time_days\": rng.randint(3, 45),\n                \"active\": rng.chance(0.9),\n            }\n        )\n    return pd.DataFrame(rows)\n\n\ndef _fulfillment_nodes(rng: Rng, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:\n    \"\"\"The node (DC / store / 3PL) that fulfils an order — a join target beyond the\n    store Location dimension.\"\"\"\n    rows = []\n    for nid in rng.id_pool(\"NODE\", n, width=4):\n        city, _ = rng.choice(CITIES)\n        rows.append(\n            {\n                \"node_id\": nid,\n                \"node_type\": rng.choice(NODE_TYPES),\n                \"region\": rng.choice(REGIONS),\n                \"city\": city,\n                \"active\": rng.chance(0.95),\n            }\n        )\n    return pd.DataFrame(rows)\n\n\ndef _date_dim(now: dt.datetime, days: int = 540) -> pd.DataFrame:\n    \"\"\"Calendar dimension for trend slicing (fiscal week/quarter, season). Contiguous\n    daily rows — a completeness check verifies there are no gaps.\"\"\"\n    rows = []\n    start = (now - dt.timedelta(days=days - 1)).date()\n    for i in range(days):\n        d = start + dt.timedelta(days=i)\n        iso_year, iso_week, _ = d.isocalendar()\n        rows.append(\n            {\n                \"date_key\": int(d.strftime(\"%Y%m%d\")),\n                \"date\": d,\n                \"day_of_week\": d.strftime(\"%A\"),\n                \"fiscal_week\": iso_week,\n                \"fiscal_quarter\": (d.month - 1) // 3 + 1,\n                \"fiscal_year\": iso_year,\n                \"season\": SEASONS[(d.month % 12) // 3],\n                \"is_holiday\": d.month == 12 and d.day in (24, 25, 31),\n            }\n        )\n    return pd.DataFrame(rows)\n\n\ndef _exchange_rates(rng: Rng, now: dt.datetime, days: int = 90) -> pd.DataFrame:\n    \"\"\"Daily FX rate to USD per currency. Latest rate_date is fresh (freshness monitor);\n    enables multi-currency conversion checks even though orders are USD today.\"\"\"\n    rows = []\n    start = (now - dt.timedelta(days=days - 1)).date()\n    for i in range(days):\n        d = start + dt.timedelta(days=i)\n        for cur in CURRENCIES:\n            base = FX_TO_USD[cur]\n            rows.append(\n                {\n                    \"currency\": cur,\n                    \"rate_date\": d,\n                    # small daily jitter around the static reference\n                    \"rate_to_usd\": round(base * rng.uniform(0.98, 1.02), 6),\n                }\n            )\n    return pd.DataFrame(rows)"
}

  "new_string": "# --- extended domain facts -------------------------------------------------\n\nSETTLEMENT_FEE_RATE = 0.025  # processor fee: net = gross - gross*fee\n\n\ndef _settlements(rng: Rng, payments: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:\n    \"\"\"Finance ledger: one settlement per captured payment. net = gross - fee, and\n    gross must reconcile back to payment.captured_amount (finance reconciliation).\"\"\"\n    rows = []\n    captured = payments[payments[\"status\"] == \"captured\"]\n    for i, p in enumerate(captured.itertuples(index=False), start=1):\n        gross = round(float(p.captured_amount), 2)\n        fee = round(gross * SETTLEMENT_FEE_RATE, 2)\n        rows.append(\n            {\n                \"settlement_id\": f\"STL-{i:08d}\",\n                \"payment_id\": p.payment_id,\n                \"batch_id\": f\"SB-{(i - 1) // 100:05d}\",\n                \"gross_amount\": gross,\n                \"fee_amount\": fee,\n                \"net_amount\": round(gross - fee, 2),\n                \"status\": rng.weighted(SETTLEMENT_STATUSES, [0.1, 0.85, 0.05]),\n                \"settled_ts\": p.paid_ts + dt.timedelta(days=rng.randint(1, 3)),\n            }\n        )\n    return pd.DataFrame(rows)\n\n\ndef _purchase_orders(\n    rng: Rng, n: int, now: dt.datetime, supplier_ids: list[str], sku_ids: list[str]\n) -> pd.DataFrame:\n    \"\"\"Inbound supply feed: PO -> supplier + sku. received_date vs expected_date drives\n    an inbound-freshness monitor; qty_received <= qty_ordered is a reconciliation rule.\"\"\"\n    rows = []\n    for i in range(1, n + 1):\n        order_date = rng.datetime_between(now - dt.timedelta(days=90), now).date()\n        expected = order_date + dt.timedelta(days=rng.randint(5, 40))\n        status = rng.weighted(PO_STATUSES, [0.2, 0.2, 0.55, 0.05])\n        qty_ordered = rng.randint(20, 500)\n        if status == \"received\":\n            qty_received = qty_ordered\n            received = expected + dt.timedelta(days=rng.randint(-3, 5))\n        elif status == \"partial\":\n            qty_received = rng.randint(1, qty_ordered - 1)\n            received = expected + dt.timedelta(days=rng.randint(-2, 7))\n        else:\n            qty_received = 0\n            received = None\n        rows.append(\n            {\n                \"po_number\": f\"PO-{i:08d}\",\n                \"supplier_id\": rng.choice(supplier_ids),\n                \"sku_id\": rng.choice(sku_ids),\n                \"qty_ordered\": qty_ordered,\n                \"qty_received\": qty_received,\n                \"order_date\": order_date,\n                \"expected_date\": expected,\n                \"received_date\": received,\n                \"status\": status,\n            }\n        )\n    return pd.DataFrame(rows)\n\n\ndef _order_fulfillment(\n    rng: Rng, orders: pd.DataFrame, node_ids: list[str]\n) -> pd.DataFrame:\n    \"\"\"Which node fulfilled each shipped/delivered order (join target beyond store).\"\"\"\n    rows = []\n    shipped = orders[orders[\"status\"].isin([\"shipped\", \"delivered\", \"returned\"])]\n    for o in shipped.itertuples(index=False):\n        rows.append(\n            {\n                \"order_number\": o.order_number,\n                \"node_id\": rng.choice(node_ids),\n                \"fulfilled_ts\": o.order_ts + dt.timedelta(hours=rng.randint(2, 48)),\n                \"ship_method\": rng.choice([\"ground\", \"express\", \"freight\"]),\n            }\n        )\n    return pd.DataFrame(rows)\n\n\ndef _discounts(rng: Rng, orders: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:\n    \"\"\"Per-order standalone discount (distinct from promotions): order_total should\n    already net the discount — a reconciliation testbed.\"\"\"\n    rows = []\n    discounted = orders[orders[\"promo_id\"].notna()]\n    for i, o in enumerate(discounted.itertuples(index=False), start=1):\n        rows.append(\n            {\n                \"discount_id\": f\"DSC-{i:08d}\",\n                \"order_number\": o.order_number,\n                \"discount_type\": rng.choice(DISCOUNT_TYPES),\n                \"amount\": round(float(o.subtotal) * rng.uniform(0.05, 0.25), 2),\n            }\n        )\n    return pd.DataFrame(rows)\n\n\ndef _cancellations(rng: Rng, orders: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:\n    \"\"\"One row per cancelled order — status='cancelled' must have a cancellation row\n    (a consistency check between the status flag and the cancellation entity).\"\"\"\n    rows = []\n    cancelled = orders[orders[\"status\"] == \"cancelled\"]\n    for i, o in enumerate(cancelled.itertuples(index=False), start=1):\n        rows.append(\n            {\n                \"cancellation_id\": f\"CNL-{i:08d}\",\n                \"order_number\": o.order_number,\n                \"reason\": rng.choice(CANCELLATION_REASONS),\n                \"cancelled_ts\": o.order_ts + dt.timedelta(hours=rng.randint(1, 72)),\n            }\n        )\n    return pd.DataFrame(rows)\n\n\n# --- Flow B medallion bronze sources ---------------------------------------"
}

  "new_string": "    state.counters[\"feedback\"] = base_fb + len(rows)\n    return {\"feedback\": pd.DataFrame(rows)}, []\n\n\n# --- supply (inbound purchase orders — the inbound-freshness cadence) -------\n\n\ndef _tick_supply(\n    rng: Rng,\n    now: dt.datetime,\n    state: HarnessState,\n    masters: dict[str, pd.DataFrame],\n    n: int,\n) -> tuple[dict[str, pd.DataFrame], list[dict]]:\n    \"\"\"One inbound batch of purchase orders. po_number climbs across ticks; FK to the\n    persisted supplier + product pools. received_date freshness trends over ticks.\"\"\"\n    supplier_ids = masters[\"suppliers\"][\"supplier_id\"].tolist()\n    sku_ids = masters[\"products\"][\"sku_id\"].tolist()\n    base_po = state.counters[\"po\"]\n    rows = []\n    for i in range(1, n + 1):\n        order_date = (now - dt.timedelta(days=rng.randint(0, 5))).date()\n        expected = order_date + dt.timedelta(days=rng.randint(5, 40))\n        status = rng.weighted(PO_STATUSES, [0.4, 0.25, 0.3, 0.05])\n        qty_ordered = rng.randint(20, 500)\n        if status == \"received\":\n            qty_received = qty_ordered\n            received = (now - dt.timedelta(days=rng.randint(0, 2))).date()\n        elif status == \"partial\":\n            qty_received = rng.randint(1, qty_ordered - 1)\n            received = (now - dt.timedelta(days=rng.randint(0, 2))).date()\n        else:\n            qty_received = 0\n            received = None\n        rows.append(\n            {\n                \"po_number\": f\"PO-{base_po + i:08d}\",\n                \"supplier_id\": rng.choice(supplier_ids),\n                \"sku_id\": rng.choice(sku_ids),\n                \"qty_ordered\": qty_ordered,\n                \"qty_received\": qty_received,\n                \"order_date\": order_date,\n                \"expected_date\": expected,\n                \"received_date\": received,\n                \"status\": status,\n            }\n        )\n    state.counters[\"po\"] = base_po + n\n    return {\"purchase_orders\": pd.DataFrame(rows)}, []"
}

1	"""Flow A — plain load to Unity Catalog (reference data). §3a.
2	
3	Proves the UnityCatalogCheckRunner *without* the medallion machinery: governed
4	reference tables (location / promotions / channel) loaded straight into the UC
5	`reference` schema, then the DataQ trigger fires. Schedule-trigger modality (the UC
6	half of the event+schedule mix). Loads are reference-sized (tens–hundreds of rows).
7	
8	Required env (key-based): AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING, DATABRICKS_HOST/TOKEN/HTTP_PATH,
9	UC_CATALOG, plus the DATAQ_WEBHOOK_* trigger vars.
10	"""
11	
12	from __future__ import annotations
13	
14	import os
15	
16	import pendulum
17	from _harness import load_to_uc, read_feed
18	from airflow import DAG
19	from airflow.operators.python import PythonOperator
20	from dataq_airflow_callback import on_dataq_failure, on_dataq_success
21	
22	UC_CATALOG = os.environ.get("UC_CATALOG", "dataq_retail")
23	UC_REFERENCE_SCHEMA = os.environ.get("UC_REFERENCE_SCHEMA", "reference")
24	
25	# Reference feeds (route map §2) land as Parquet under unity_catalog/<feed>/.
26	UC_FEEDS = ["locations", "channels", "promotions"]
27	
28	
29	def _load(feed: str, **_: object) -> None:
30	    df = read_feed(f"unity_catalog/{feed}", "parquet")
31	    if not df.empty:
32	        load_to_uc(df, UC_CATALOG, UC_REFERENCE_SCHEMA, feed)
33	
34	
35	with DAG(
36	    dag_id="flow_a_uc_reference",
37	    description="DataQ harness Flow A — load reference data from ADLS into Unity Catalog",
38	    schedule="45 1 * * *",  # after the Snowflake load + the §2a Jobs
39	    start_date=pendulum.datetime(2026, 6, 1, tz="UTC"),
40	    catchup=False,
41	    on_success_callback=on_dataq_success,
42	    on_failure_callback=on_dataq_failure,
43	    tags=["dataq-harness", "flow-a", "unity-catalog"],
44	):
45	    for _feed in UC_FEEDS:
46	        PythonOperator(
47	            task_id=f"load_{_feed}",
48	            python_callable=_load,
49	            op_kwargs={"feed": _feed},
50	        )
51

1	"""Shared load helpers for the DataQ-harness Airflow DAGs (§3).
2	
3	All auth is key-based (the disposable-harness decision): ADLS via the storage
4	**connection string**, Snowflake via user/password, Databricks via PAT. Heavy
5	client libs are imported lazily inside the functions so DAG *parsing* stays cheap
6	(the scheduler imports this module on every parse).
7	
8	Reads are "load the whole landing-zone subdir": each scheduled run concatenates all
9	batch files for a feed and overwrites the target table — idempotent and simple for a
10	demo. (Production would track a per-file watermark; noted as a follow-up.)
11	"""
12	
13	from __future__ import annotations
14	
15	import io
16	import os
17	
18	import pandas as pd
19	
20	ADLS_FILESYSTEM = os.environ.get("ADLS_FILESYSTEM", "landing")
21	
22	
23	def _adls_filesystem():
24	    from azure.storage.filedatalake import DataLakeServiceClient
25	
26	    conn = os.environ["AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING"]
27	    return DataLakeServiceClient.from_connection_string(conn).get_file_system_client(
28	        ADLS_FILESYSTEM
29	    )
30	
31	
32	def read_feed(subdir: str, fmt: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
33	    """Concatenate every batch file under <filesystem>/<subdir> into one DataFrame."""
34	    fs = _adls_filesystem()
35	    paths = sorted(p.name for p in fs.get_paths(path=subdir) if not p.is_directory)
36	    frames = []
37	    for path in paths:
38	        data = fs.get_file_client(path).download_file().readall()
39	        buf = io.BytesIO(data)
40	        frames.append(pd.read_csv(buf) if fmt == "csv" else pd.read_parquet(buf))
41	    return pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True) if frames else pd.DataFrame()
42	
43	
44	def load_to_snowflake(df: pd.DataFrame, table: str) -> int:
45	    """Overwrite a Snowflake table from a DataFrame (write_pandas, auto-create)."""
46	    import snowflake.connector
47	    from snowflake.connector.pandas_tools import write_pandas
48	
49	    conn = snowflake.connector.connect(
50	        account=os.environ["SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT"],
51	        user=os.environ["SNOWFLAKE_USER"],
52	        password=os.environ["SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD"],
53	        warehouse=os.environ["SNOWFLAKE_WAREHOUSE"],
54	        database=os.environ["SNOWFLAKE_DATABASE"],
55	        schema=os.environ.get("SNOWFLAKE_SCHEMA", "RETAIL"),
56	        role=os.environ.get("SNOWFLAKE_ROLE") or None,
57	    )
58	    try:
59	        df.columns = [c.upper() for c in df.columns]
60	        _ok, _chunks, rows, _ = write_pandas(
61	            conn, df, table.upper(), auto_create_table=True, overwrite=True
62	        )
63	        return int(rows)
64	    finally:
65	        conn.close()
66	
67	
68	_PANDAS_TO_SQL = {
69	    "int64": "BIGINT",
70	    "float64": "DOUBLE",
71	    "bool": "BOOLEAN",
72	    "datetime64[ns]": "TIMESTAMP",
73	}
74	
75	
76	def load_to_uc(df: pd.DataFrame, catalog: str, schema: str, table: str) -> int:
77	    """Create-or-replace + insert a (small, reference-sized) DataFrame into a UC table."""
78	    from databricks import sql
79	
80	    full = f"`{catalog}`.`{schema}`.`{table}`"
81	    cols = ", ".join(
82	        f"`{c}` {_PANDAS_TO_SQL.get(str(t), 'STRING')}" for c, t in df.dtypes.items()
83	    )
84	    rows = [
85	        tuple(None if pd.isna(v) else v for v in record)
86	        for record in df.itertuples(index=False, name=None)
87	    ]
88	    conn = sql.connect(
89	        server_hostname=os.environ["DATABRICKS_HOST"]
90	        .replace("https://", "")
91	        .rstrip("/"),
92	        http_path=os.environ["DATABRICKS_HTTP_PATH"],  # SQL warehouse path
93	        access_token=os.environ["DATABRICKS_TOKEN"],
94	    )
95	    try:
96	        cur = conn.cursor()
97	        cur.execute(f"CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE {full} ({cols})")
98	        if rows:
99	            placeholders = ", ".join(["?"] * len(df.columns))
100	            cur.executemany(f"INSERT INTO {full} VALUES ({placeholders})", rows)
101	        return len(rows)
102	    finally:
103	        conn.close()
104	
```

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ-harness/airflow/dags/flow_a_payments_event.py",
  "content": "\"\"\"Flow A — event-driven load to Snowflake (payments). §3a.\n\nThe *event* half of the Airflow trigger mix (the schedule half is\n``flow_a_snowflake_load``). Payments land with every orders tick, so this DAG\nwatches the ``snowflake/payments/`` landing dir and loads on **arrival** rather\nthan on a daily clock.\n\nCloud Airflow can't natively complete Event Grid's webhook validation handshake,\nso this uses the documented **file-sensor** pattern: a reschedule-mode\n``PythonSensor`` pokes ADLS for a rising batch-file count (vs an Airflow Variable\nwatermark); when a new file lands it fires a whole-subdir overwrite load\n(idempotent, like the schedule DAG). The poke interval bounds arrival latency.\n\nRequired env (key-based): AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING,\nSNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT/USER/PASSWORD/WAREHOUSE/DATABASE[/SCHEMA/ROLE], plus the\nDATAQ_WEBHOOK_* trigger vars.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport pendulum\nfrom _harness import count_feed_files, load_to_snowflake, read_feed\nfrom airflow import DAG\nfrom airflow.models import Variable\nfrom airflow.operators.python import PythonOperator\nfrom airflow.sensors.python import PythonSensor\nfrom dataq_airflow_callback import on_dataq_failure, on_dataq_success\n\nPAYMENTS_SUBDIR = \"snowflake/payments\"\nWATERMARK_KEY = \"payments_event_filecount\"\n\n\ndef _new_files_arrived(**_: object) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"True when more payment batch files exist than we last processed.\"\"\"\n    current = count_feed_files(PAYMENTS_SUBDIR)\n    seen = int(Variable.get(WATERMARK_KEY, default_var=0))\n    return current > seen\n\n\ndef _load_payments(**_: object) -> None:\n    df = read_feed(PAYMENTS_SUBDIR, \"csv\")\n    if not df.empty:\n        load_to_snowflake(df, \"payments\")  # overwrite — idempotent\n    Variable.set(WATERMARK_KEY, count_feed_files(PAYMENTS_SUBDIR))\n\n\nwith DAG(\n    dag_id=\"flow_a_payments_event\",\n    description=\"DataQ harness Flow A — event/arrival-driven payments load (file-sensor)\",\n    schedule=\"*/10 * * * *\",  # poke cadence — bounds file-arrival latency\n    start_date=pendulum.datetime(2026, 6, 1, tz=\"UTC\"),\n    catchup=False,\n    max_active_runs=1,\n    on_success_callback=on_dataq_success,\n    on_failure_callback=on_dataq_failure,\n    tags=[\"dataq-harness\", \"flow-a\", \"snowflake\", \"event\"],\n):\n    wait = PythonSensor(\n        task_id=\"wait_for_new_payments\",\n        python_callable=_new_files_arrived,\n        mode=\"reschedule\",  # free the worker slot between pokes\n        poke_interval=120,\n        timeout=540,  # give up within the 10-min window; next run re-pokes\n        soft_fail=True,  # no new file in the window -> skip, not fail\n    )\n    load = PythonOperator(task_id=\"load_payments\", python_callable=_load_payments)\n    wait >> load\n"
}

I'll pause the verification — the user raises a correct architectural point that I should fix first.

You're right, and it's a real design flaw in the harness. The ADF pipeline is **failing** purely because its `NotifyDataQ` web activity can't reach DataQ (empty webhook URL, DataQ not deployed). That hard-wires the orchestrator's success to DataQ being up — backwards. DataQ is one of potentially many quality tools; it should **discover** orchestration runs by polling the provider's API (which is exactly DataQ's `OrchestrationProvider` 10-min polling design, ADR 0006), not be a hard dependency the pipeline pushes to.

Let me decouple it — remove the `NotifyDataQ` push from both ADF pipelines so they're pure ETL. First the orders pipeline:

def _notify(context: dict[str, Any], state: str) -> None:
    """Build, sign, and POST one DAG-run event. Never raises."""
    url = os.environ.get("DATAQ_WEBHOOK_URL")
    secret = os.environ.get("DATAQ_WEBHOOK_SECRET")
    if not url or not secret:
        _LOG.warning("DataQ callback skipped: DATAQ_WEBHOOK_URL / DATAQ_WEBHOOK_SECRET not set")
        return

    try:
        dag_run = context.get("dag_run")
        dag_id = getattr(dag_run, "dag_id", None) or getattr(context.get("dag"), "dag_id", None)
        run_id = getattr(dag_run, "run_id", None)
        base_url = os.environ.get("DATAQ_AIRFLOW_BASE_URL") or _airflow_base_url()
        if not dag_id or not run_id or not base_url:
            _LOG.warning(
                "DataQ callback skipped: could not resolve dag_id/run_id/base_url from context"

> AGENT

Confirmed — **correct, Airflow does not have that dependency.** The difference is structural:

## ADF (what I just fixed) vs Airflow

| | ADF (before fix) | Airflow |
|---|---|---|
| How DataQ was notified | `NotifyDataQ` **WebActivity** — a first-class step *inside* the pipeline | `on_success_callback` / `on_failure_callback` — DAG-level **callbacks** |
| Effect of DataQ being unreachable | Activity fails → **whole pipeline marked Failed** ❌ | Callback runs *after* the run state is already decided → **cannot** change it |
| Failure handling | — | `_notify` is documented "**Never raises**" — catches `HTTPError` + bare `Exception`, logs, returns (comment: *"the DAG run is unaffected"*) |
| Currently | (removed) | Also **no-ops** — `DATAQ_WEBHOOK_URL`/`SECRET` aren't set in the Airflow env, so it logs "skipped" and returns |

So Airflow is safe three times over: the notification is a post-hoc callback (not a task in the critical path), it never raises, and it's currently unconfigured so it no-ops. A DAG can't fail because of DataQ.

The ADF case was the only genuine hard-wiring (a WebActivity is a real pipeline step), which is why removing it was the right call — and I did the same-spirit thing there: pure ETL, DataQ discovers runs by polling the provider's REST API (ADR 0006/0007), the resilient pull model.

**One nuance for full symmetry:** the Airflow DAGs still *reference* DataQ (they `import dataq_airflow_callback`). It's harmless (best-effort, non-fatal), but if you want **zero** DataQ references in the orchestrator — true symmetry with the now-pure ADF pipelines — I can drop the callbacks entirely and rely solely on DataQ's polling. Want me to?

Also, status on the in-flight work: the Airflow **Snowflake load with the new entities** is still rolling out — Container Apps had cached the old `:latest` image, so I switched to an immutable tag (`v202606271401`) and re-applied; the new revision (with the new feed DAGs: settlements/PO/order_fulfillment/discounts/cancellations) is still propagating. The ADF side is fully verified: **CUSTOMERS (200, timer) + ORDERS_HEADER (720, event)** loaded, both pipelines now Succeed.

Submits the medallion notebook (databricks/medallion_notebook.py, imported into the
workspace) as a one-off Databricks job run on a job cluster, waits for completion, then
the DAG success callback triggers DataQ → suites run on the UC silver/gold tables.

Key-based: the ADLS account name + key are parsed from the storage connection string and
passed to the notebook (which sets them in spark conf — no external location needed).

Required env: AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING, DATABRICKS_HOST/TOKEN, MEDALLION_NOTEBOOK_PATH,
optional UC_CATALOG / ADLS_FILESYSTEM / DATABRICKS_SPARK_VERSION / DATABRICKS_NODE_TYPE,

this DAG (`flow_a_snowflake_load`). Offset to run AFTER the file-creation Jobs (§2a).

=== flow_a_payments_event.py (lines 1-18) ===
"""Flow A — event-driven load to Snowflake (payments). §3a.

The *event* half of the Airflow trigger mix (the schedule half is
``flow_a_snowflake_load``). Payments land with every orders tick, so this DAG
watches the ``snowflake/payments/`` landing dir and loads on **arrival** rather
than on a daily clock.

Cloud Airflow can't natively complete Event Grid's webhook validation handshake,
so this uses the documented **file-sensor** pattern: a reschedule-mode
``PythonSensor`` pokes ADLS for a rising batch-file count (vs an Airflow Variable
watermark); when a new file lands it fires a whole-subdir overwrite load
(idempotent, like the schedule DAG). The poke interval bounds arrival latency.

Required env (key-based): AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING,
SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT/USER/PASSWORD/WAREHOUSE/DATABASE[/SCHEMA/ROLE], plus the
DATAQ_WEBHOOK_* trigger vars.
"""

=== flow_a_uc_reference.py (lines 1-18) ===
"""Flow A — plain load to Unity Catalog (reference data). §3a.

Proves the UnityCatalogCheckRunner *without* the medallion machinery: governed
reference tables (location / promotions / channel) loaded straight into the UC

Decisive find: there's only **one** revision (`0000005`) and it's `running=Failed` with traffic=100 — yet it answers 200 with **old** DAGs. That means the failed scheduler never re-serialized the new DAGs into Postgres, so the API serves the **stale serialized DAGs** from the metadata DB. The container is wedged.

The cleaner, infra-level way that matches "tear down and re-create" is to recreate the **metadata database itself** via Terraform — that gives Airflow a clean slate (fresh `serialized_dag`), and the container's init re-migrates it. > DEVELOPER

What is the issue - Postgres is offer-restricted in westus2

> AGENT

It's an **Azure subscription-level capacity restriction** — not a permissions, quota-you-set, or code problem. Here's the precise picture.

## What happened
When Terraform tried to create the Postgres Flexible Server in westus2, Azure rejected it:
```
Status: "LocationIsOfferRestricted"
Message: "Subscriptions are restricted from provisioning in location 'westus2'.
          Try again in a different location. For exceptions ... request a quota increase."
```

## What "offer-restricted" means
Azure gates **which subscriptions can provision a specific *offer* (service + SKU family) in a specific *region*.** Here the offer is **Azure Database for PostgreSQL – Flexible Server**, and the region is **westus2**.

- It's keyed on **(subscription type × region × service)** — not your account, not the Terraform SP, not a quota number you control. Azure itself is saying "this subscription isn't allowed to spin up *this service* in *this region* right now."
- **westus2 is one of Azure's most capacity-constrained regions.** To protect capacity there, Azure restricts new provisioning of in-demand services for non-enterprise subscriptions (pay-as-you-go / MSDN / new subs). Postgres Flexible Server is one such gated offer.
- Crucially, it's **service-specific**: everything *else* in the harness (Storage, ACR, Container Apps, ADF, Log Analytics) provisions fine in westus2 — **only** Postgres Flexible Server is blocked there for this subscription.

## How I detected it
`az postgres flexible-server list-skus -l <region>` is the tell:
- **westus2 → ~1.6 KB** (essentially empty = restricted)
- **centralus / westus3 / westus → ~80 KB** (full SKU list = open)

## The two ways out
1. **Deploy Postgres in an open region** — what I did. First centralus (open, but ~30–40ms from the westus2 Container Apps → too slow for Airflow's chatty scheduler), now **westus3** (open *and* adjacent to westus2 → sub-millisecond latency).
2. **Request an exception** — file an Azure support/quota request (`aka.ms/postgres-request-quota-increase`) to lift the restriction for westus2. Slower (human approval), and unnecessary since westus3 solves it cleanly.

So it's an Azure-side policy, not a bug — and option 1 (westus3) is the right fix, which is what's deploying now.

> AGENT

Now I can see the real cause. The LocalExecutor **is** spawning task workers (`QueuedLocalWorker running ['airflow','tasks','run',...]`), but every one hits `DeprecationWarning: ... use of fork() may lead to deadlocks in the child` — the workers **fork-deadlock**. The scheduler process is multi-threaded (Azure SDK / gRPC background threads), and forking it to run a task deadlocks the child → tasks never progress past `scheduled`.

The fix is to make Airflow run each task in a **fresh interpreter (spawn, not fork)**:

> TOOL

tool_use Edit
id: toolu_01NWUSetx5SVSG73Ed29hYW6
```json
{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ-harness/terraform/airflow.tf",
  "old_string": "    { name = \"AIRFLOW__CORE__LOAD_EXAMPLES\", value = \"False\" },\n    # Enable basic-auth on the REST API so DAG runs can be triggered programmatically.\n    { name = \"AIRFLOW__API__AUTH_BACKENDS\", value = \"airflow.api.auth.backend.basic_auth,airflow.api.auth.backend.session\" },",
  "new_string": "    { name = \"AIRFLOW__CORE__LOAD_EXAMPLES\", value = \"False\" },\n    # Enable basic-auth on the REST API so DAG runs can be triggered programmatically.\n    { name = \"AIRFLOW__API__AUTH_BACKENDS\", value = \"airflow.api.auth.backend.basic_auth,airflow.api.auth.backend.session\" },\n    # Run each task in a FRESH interpreter (spawn) instead of forking the scheduler.\n    # The scheduler is multi-threaded (Azure SDK / gRPC bg threads); LocalExecutor's\n    # fork() of it deadlocks the child → tasks stick in 'scheduled' and never run.\n    { name = \"AIRFLOW__CORE__EXECUTE_TASKS_NEW_PYTHON_INTERPRETER\", value = \"True\" },"
}
```

Yes — it needs more CPU, and here's exactly why it's slow.

## Why Airflow execution is slow

It's the combination of two things:

1. **Tiny scheduler container (0.5 vCPU / 1 GiB).** With **LocalExecutor**, every task runs as a subprocess *inside the scheduler container*. There's no separate worker pool — that one 0.5-vCPU container does DAG parsing **and** runs all task processes. 0.5 vCPU realistically runs only ~1–2 tasks at once, so the rest sit `queued` and drain slowly (exactly what you see: `queued: 7 → …`).

2. **The fork-deadlock fix made each task heavy.** To stop the fork-deadlock, I set `EXECUTE_TASKS_NEW_PYTHON_INTERPRETER=True` — so instead of a cheap `fork()`, each task launches a **brand-new Python interpreter** that re-imports all of Airflow + the heavy client libs (snowflake-connector, azure-storage, databricks) *before doing any work*. That's several seconds of CPU + a few hundred MB RAM per task, just for startup. On 0.5 vCPU those cold-starts serialize.

So: heavy per-task cost × tiny CPU × single executor = slow drain. It's *working* (tasks complete, just slowly).

**The fix is more CPU/memory on the scheduler** (it's the task runner). Let me bump it 0.5→2.0 vCPU / 1→4 GiB:

## Honest status: Airflow execution is the one stubborn piece

**Everything you asked for architecturally is done and verified:**
- ✅ **Generator** — all deferred entities added (24 datasets, 18 seeded issues, FK-clean), verified locally.
- ✅ **ADF decoupled from DataQ** — pure ETL, both pipelines Succeed; **event (orders) + timer (customers) load Snowflake** (ORDERS_HEADER 720, CUSTOMERS 200).
- ✅ **Airflow decoupled from DataQ** — zero references.
- ✅ **Infra fixes** — westus3 Postgres (latency), immutable image tags, spawn-interpreter (fork-deadlock), scheduler 1.5/3 GiB.

**The blocker — and why more resources alone won't fix it:** the Airflow **LocalExecutor on Container Apps Consumption** is the wrong shape for this load. Three compounding limits:
1. **The Consumption profile hard-caps a replica at 2 vCPU / 4 GiB total** — I'm already at the max. There's no "just add more."
2. **Every task cold-starts a full Python interpreter** (the fork-deadlock fix) re-importing Airflow + snowflake/azure/databricks — hundreds of MB + seconds each.
3. **The DAGs fan out all 9 feeds in parallel** → they swamp the tiny single executor; they queue but don't drain, and `load_date_dim` is failing outright (a real bug — `load_to_uc`'s type mapping for `date`/`bool` columns, made worse by no remote logging to debug).

So this needs an **approach decision**, not another tweak. Here are the real options:

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ-harness/terraform/redis.tf",
  "content": "# Redis broker for Airflow CeleryExecutor (§3 / execution scaling).\n# Self-hosted Redis container (not Azure Cache for Redis) — cheapest + fastest for a\n# disposable harness; the broker is transient (no persistence needed). Internal-only\n# TCP ingress so only the Airflow scheduler + workers in this environment reach it.\nresource \"azurerm_container_app\" \"redis\" {\n  name                         = \"dataq-harness-redis\"\n  container_app_environment_id = azurerm_container_app_environment.harness.id\n  resource_group_name          = data.azurerm_resource_group.dataq.name\n  revision_mode                = \"Single\"\n\n  ingress {\n    external_enabled = false # only reachable within the Container Apps environment\n    transport        = \"tcp\"\n    target_port      = 6379\n    exposed_port     = 6379\n    traffic_weight {\n      latest_revision = true\n      percentage      = 100\n    }\n  }\n\n  template {\n    min_replicas = 1\n    max_replicas = 1\n    container {\n      name   = \"redis\"\n      image  = \"redis:7-alpine\" # public image — no registry auth needed\n      cpu    = 0.5\n      memory = \"1Gi\"\n      args   = [\"redis-server\", \"--save\", \"\", \"--appendonly\", \"no\"] # in-memory only\n    }\n  }\n\n  tags = local.common_tags\n}\n"
}

Now the scalable worker app (its own replicas, each up to 2vCPU/4GiB):

> TOOL

tool_use Write
id: toolu_01BRczPPyNgUaSHRrs95Aphw
```json
{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ-harness/terraform/airflow_worker.tf",
  "content": "# Airflow Celery workers — a SEPARATE, horizontally scalable container app. This is the\n# point of CeleryExecutor: each worker replica gets its own 2 vCPU / 4 GiB (the per-replica\n# Consumption cap), and we run several — lifting the single-LocalExecutor ceiling that\n# throttled task throughput. Workers pull tasks from the Redis broker, execute, and write\n# results to the Postgres result backend. No ingress (workers don't serve traffic).\nresource \"azurerm_container_app\" \"airflow_worker\" {\n  name                         = \"dataq-harness-airflow-worker\"\n  container_app_environment_id = azurerm_container_app_environment.harness.id\n  resource_group_name          = data.azurerm_resource_group.dataq.name\n  revision_mode                = \"Single\"\n\n  # The metadata DB must be migrated (by the main app's init container) before workers\n  # can run tasks; ordering the worker after the scheduler app makes that the common case.\n  depends_on = [azurerm_container_app.airflow]\n\n  identity {\n    type = \"SystemAssigned\"\n  }\n\n  registry {\n    server               = azurerm_container_registry.harness.login_server\n    username             = azurerm_container_registry.harness.admin_username\n    password_secret_name = \"acr-password\"\n  }\n\n  # Workers need the same secrets the tasks touch (no webserver/admin secrets).\n  secret {\n    name  = \"acr-password\"\n    value = azurerm_container_registry.harness.admin_password\n  }\n  secret {\n    name  = \"adls-conn\"\n    value = azurerm_storage_account.landing.primary_connection_string\n  }\n  secret {\n    name  = \"snowflake-password\"\n    value = var.snowflake_password\n  }\n  secret {\n    name  = \"databricks-token\"\n    value = var.databricks_token\n  }\n  secret {\n    name  = \"celery-result-backend\"\n    value = local.celery_result_backend\n  }\n  secret {\n    name  = \"pg-conn\"\n    value = local.airflow_pg_conn\n  }\n  secret {\n    name  = \"fernet-key\"\n    value = local.airflow_fernet_key\n  }\n\n  template {\n    min_replicas = 2 # two always-on workers; raise max for burst\n    max_replicas = 4\n\n    container {\n      name   = \"worker\"\n      image  = local.airflow_image\n      cpu    = 2.0 # worker-only app → can take the full per-replica cap\n      memory = \"4Gi\"\n      args   = [\"celery\", \"worker\"]\n      dynamic \"env\" {\n        for_each = local.airflow_env\n        content {\n          name        = env.value.name\n          value       = lookup(env.value, \"value\", null)\n          secret_name = lookup(env.value, \"secret_name\", null)\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n  tags = local.common_tags\n}\n"
}
```

**No — we have zero retry logic.** Confirmed: the DAGs have no `retries`/`default_args`, `load_to_uc` makes a single connection attempt with no wait/backoff, and `AIRFLOW__CORE__DEFAULT_TASK_RETRIES` isn't set (so Airflow's default is 0). That's almost certainly why the UC loads fail — the **serverless warehouse cold-starts** (and 8 tasks hit it at once), the first connection errors, and with **no retry the task dies immediately**. My single laptop connection worked precisely because one connection warms it fine.

Let me add proper retry logic with exponential backoff (so a cold/starting warehouse recovers) to all DAGs:

> TOOL

tool_use Bash
id: toolu_01SPnSfPNPyR7sPPuSSb7ScT

> AGENT

**Root cause found:** `OSError: Repetition level histogram size mismatch` in `pd.read_parquet`. This is a **pyarrow version skew** — the mockdata generator image writes Parquet with a newer pyarrow (size-statistics/rep-level histograms) that the airflow worker's older pyarrow can't read. (The Snowflake feeds are CSV, which is why they worked.) Let me check both images' pyarrow pins:

This was a long fight, but the **entire harness load layer now works end-to-end across every orchestration path.** Here's where it stands:

## ✅ Working & verified (all loads landing)

| Path | Modality | Lands |
|---|---|---|
| **ADF** | event (blob trigger) | `ORDERS_HEADER` (720) |
| **ADF** | timer (schedule) | `CUSTOMERS` (200) |
| **Airflow** | event (file-sensor) | `PAYMENTS` (240) |
| **Airflow + Celery** | schedule | 9 Snowflake feeds incl. new domain: `SETTLEMENTS, PURCHASE_ORDERS, ORDER_FULFILLMENT, DISCOUNTS, CANCELLATIONS` (+ order_lines, products, refunds, returns) |
| **Airflow + Celery** | schedule | 8 UC reference tables: `categories, suppliers, fulfillment_nodes, date_dim, exchange_rates, locations, channels, promotions` |

**Snowflake `RETAIL`: 12 tables. UC `dataq_retail.reference`: 8 tables.** The full 2×2 orchestration matrix + all the deferred domain entities.

## The chain of root-causes I had to clear to get here
1. **Postgres offer-restricted** in westus2 → centralus → (latency) → **westus3**
2. **Image caching** (`:latest` reused) → **immutable tags**
3. **Scheduler can't execute** (LocalExecutor fork-deadlock + 2-vCPU cap) → **CeleryExecutor + scalable workers + Redis broker**
4. **Broker unreachable** (`.internal.` FQDN) → **short app-name**
5. **No retry logic** (your catch!) → **4× exponential backoff**
6. **pyarrow skew** (mockdata writes 24, airflow reads 19 → "repetition level histogram size mismatch") → **pinned both to 19 + regenerated parquet**

## Remaining
- **Flow B medallion** (Databricks notebook bronze→silver→gold) + the **Databricks read/write split** you asked for — *in progress*.
- **Cleanup**: re-add ADF `ignore_changes`, remove the ADLS `_debug` diagnostic files, final `terraform plan` clean.

1	"""Flow B — medallion (bronze -> silver -> gold) in Unity Catalog. §3b.
2	
3	Submits the medallion notebook (databricks/medallion_notebook.py, imported into the
4	workspace) as a one-off Databricks job run on a job cluster, and waits for completion.
5	Pure ETL — DataQ (one of several possible monitors) discovers this run by polling the
6	Airflow REST API, not via any push from the DAG.
7	
8	Key-based: the ADLS account name + key are parsed from the storage connection string and
9	passed to the notebook (which sets them in spark conf — no external location needed).
10	
11	Required env: AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING, DATABRICKS_HOST/TOKEN, MEDALLION_NOTEBOOK_PATH,
12	optional UC_CATALOG / ADLS_FILESYSTEM / DATABRICKS_SPARK_VERSION / DATABRICKS_NODE_TYPE.
13	"""
14	
15	from __future__ import annotations
16	
17	import os
18	
19	import pendulum
20	from airflow import DAG
21	from airflow.operators.python import PythonOperator
22	
23	
24	def _parse_conn(cs: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
25	    parts = dict(kv.split("=", 1) for kv in cs.split(";") if "=" in kv)
26	    return parts["AccountName"], parts["AccountKey"]
27	
28	
29	def _run_medallion(**_: object) -> str:
30	    from databricks.sdk import WorkspaceClient
31	    from databricks.sdk.service import compute, jobs
32	
33	    account, key = _parse_conn(os.environ["AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING"])
34	    client = WorkspaceClient(
35	        host=os.environ["DATABRICKS_HOST"], token=os.environ["DATABRICKS_TOKEN"]
36	    )
37	    run = client.jobs.submit(
38	        run_name="dataq-harness-medallion",
39	        tasks=[
40	            jobs.SubmitTask(
41	                task_key="medallion",
42	                notebook_task=jobs.NotebookTask(
43	                    notebook_path=os.environ["MEDALLION_NOTEBOOK_PATH"],
44	                    base_parameters={
45	                        "storage_account": account,
46	                        "storage_key": key,
47	                        "catalog": os.environ.get("UC_CATALOG", "dataq_retail"),
48	                        "landing_fs": os.environ.get("ADLS_FILESYSTEM", "landing"),
49	                    },
50	                ),
51	                new_cluster=compute.ClusterSpec(
52	                    spark_version=os.environ.get(
53	                        "DATABRICKS_SPARK_VERSION", "15.4.x-scala2.12"
54	                    ),
55	                    node_type_id=os.environ.get("DATABRICKS_NODE_TYPE", "m5d.large"),
56	                    num_workers=1,
57	                ),
58	            )
59	        ],
60	    ).result()  # blocks until the run finishes; raises if it fails
61	    return str(run.run_id)
62	
63	
64	with DAG(
65	    default_args={
66	        # Retry transient failures (e.g. serverless SQL warehouse / job-cluster
67	        # cold starts) with exponential backoff so a starting warehouse recovers.
68	        "retries": 4,
69	        "retry_delay": pendulum.duration(seconds=30),
70	        "retry_exponential_backoff": True,
71	        "max_retry_delay": pendulum.duration(minutes=5),
72	    },
73	    dag_id="flow_b_medallion",
74	    description="DataQ harness Flow B — Databricks bronze->silver->gold medallion",
75	    schedule="0 2 * * *",  # after the Flow A loads
76	    start_date=pendulum.datetime(2026, 6, 1, tz="UTC"),
77	    catchup=False,
78	    tags=["dataq-harness", "flow-b", "medallion"],
79	):
80	    PythonOperator(task_id="run_medallion_notebook", python_callable=_run_medallion)
81

1	# Databricks notebook source
2	# DataQ harness — Flow B medallion (bronze -> silver -> gold) in Unity Catalog. §3b.
3	#
4	# Reads the bronze JSON the §2a mockdata Jobs drop in the ADLS landing zone and writes
5	# UC raw/silver/gold tables. Key-based ADLS access: the storage account name + key are
6	# passed in as notebook parameters by the Airflow DAG (flow_b_medallion).
7	#
8	# Import once into the workspace (path = MEDALLION_NOTEBOOK_PATH the DAG references):
9	#   databricks workspace import databricks/medallion_notebook.py /Shared/dataq/medallion -l PYTHON
10	
11	# COMMAND ----------
12	dbutils.widgets.text("storage_account", "")
13	dbutils.widgets.text("storage_key", "")
14	dbutils.widgets.text("catalog", "dataq_retail")
15	dbutils.widgets.text("landing_fs", "landing")
16	
17	account = dbutils.widgets.get("storage_account")
18	key = dbutils.widgets.get("storage_key")
19	catalog = dbutils.widgets.get("catalog")
20	landing_fs = dbutils.widgets.get("landing_fs")
21	
22	# Key-based ADLS access (no external location / credential needed).
23	spark.conf.set(f"fs.azure.account.key.{account}.dfs.core.windows.net", key)
24	base = (
25	    f"abfss://{landing_fs}@{account}.dfs.core.windows.net/databricks_medallion/bronze"
26	)
27	
28	# COMMAND ----------
29	# BRONZE — raw load of the NDJSON the generator drops (schema-on-read).
30	spark.read.json(f"{base}/sales_events/*.json").write.mode("overwrite").saveAsTable(
31	    f"{catalog}.raw.sales_events"
32	)
33	spark.read.json(f"{base}/feedback/*.json").write.mode("overwrite").saveAsTable(
34	    f"{catalog}.raw.feedback"
35	)
36	
37	# COMMAND ----------
38	# SILVER — clean + PII-redact (the lakehouse hygiene story).
39	from pyspark.sql import functions as F  # noqa: E402
40	
41	(
42	    spark.table(f"{catalog}.raw.feedback")
43	    .withColumn("email", F.sha2(F.col("email"), 256))  # PII redaction (#226)
44	    .dropDuplicates(["feedback_id"])
45	    .write.mode("overwrite")
46	    .saveAsTable(f"{catalog}.silver.feedback")
47	)
48	
49	(
50	    spark.table(f"{catalog}.raw.sales_events")
51	    .filter(F.col("event_type") == "placed")
52	    .select(
53	        "order_number",
54	        "channel",
55	        "store_id",
56	        F.col("amount").cast("double").alias("amount"),
57	        F.to_date("event_ts").alias("sale_date"),
58	    )
59	    .write.mode("overwrite")
60	    .saveAsTable(f"{catalog}.silver.sales")
61	)
62	
63	# COMMAND ----------
64	# GOLD — daily revenue rollup. Reconciles back to Snowflake order_total (ADR 0014):
65	# sum(gold.daily_revenue) should tie out to the Snowflake orders total — the
66	# cross-platform `comparison` target (built post-v1, shaped now).
67	(
68	    spark.table(f"{catalog}.silver.sales")
69	    .groupBy("sale_date", "channel")
70	    .agg(
71	        F.sum("amount").alias("daily_revenue"),
72	        F.countDistinct("order_number").alias("orders"),
73	    )
74	    .write.mode("overwrite")
75	    .saveAsTable(f"{catalog}.gold.daily_revenue")
76	)
77

  "old_string": "def read_feed(subdir: str, fmt: str) -> pd.DataFrame:\n    \"\"\"Concatenate every batch file under <filesystem>/<subdir> into one DataFrame.\"\"\"\n    fs = _adls_filesystem()\n    paths = sorted(p.name for p in fs.get_paths(path=subdir) if not p.is_directory)\n    frames = []\n    for path in paths:\n        data = fs.get_file_client(path).download_file().readall()\n        buf = io.BytesIO(data)\n        frames.append(pd.read_csv(buf) if fmt == \"csv\" else pd.read_parquet(buf))\n    return pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True) if frames else pd.DataFrame()",
  "new_string": "def _read_buf(buf: \"io.BytesIO\", fmt: str) -> pd.DataFrame:\n    if fmt == \"csv\":\n        return pd.read_csv(buf)\n    if fmt == \"parquet\":\n        return pd.read_parquet(buf)\n    if fmt == \"json\":  # NDJSON (bronze)\n        return pd.read_json(buf, lines=True)\n    raise ValueError(f\"unknown format {fmt!r}\")\n\n\ndef read_feed(subdir: str, fmt: str) -> pd.DataFrame:\n    \"\"\"Concatenate every batch file under <filesystem>/<subdir> into one DataFrame.\"\"\"\n    fs = _adls_filesystem()\n    paths = sorted(p.name for p in fs.get_paths(path=subdir) if not p.is_directory)\n    frames = []\n    for path in paths:\n        data = fs.get_file_client(path).download_file().readall()\n        frames.append(_read_buf(io.BytesIO(data), fmt))\n    return pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True) if frames else pd.DataFrame()\n\n\ndef run_uc_sql(statements: list[str]) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Execute SQL statements on the Databricks SQL warehouse (silver/gold transforms).\"\"\"\n    from databricks import sql\n\n    conn = sql.connect(\n        server_hostname=os.environ[\"DATABRICKS_HOST\"]\n        .replace(\"https://\", \"\")\n        .rstrip(\"/\"),\n        http_path=os.environ[\"DATABRICKS_HTTP_PATH\"],\n        access_token=os.environ[\"DATABRICKS_TOKEN\"],\n    )\n    try:\n        cur = conn.cursor()\n        for stmt in statements:\n            cur.execute(stmt)\n    finally:\n        conn.close()"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ-harness/airflow/dags/flow_b_medallion.py",
  "content": "\"\"\"Flow B — medallion (bronze -> silver -> gold) in Unity Catalog. §3b.\n\nBronze NDJSON the §2a mockdata Jobs drop in ADLS is loaded into UC `raw` (worker reads\nwith pandas, writes via the Databricks SQL warehouse — same path as the reference loads);\nsilver/gold are SQL transforms on the warehouse. Implemented on the **serverless SQL\nwarehouse** rather than a PySpark job cluster: the trial workspace's reliable compute is\nserverless, and reading ADLS from the warehouse is avoided by loading raw in the worker\n(no UC storage credential for ADLS — that needs a role assignment the harness SP can't make).\n\nPure ETL — DataQ discovers this run by polling the Airflow REST API, not via any push.\n\nRequired env (key-based): AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING,\nDATABRICKS_HOST/TOKEN/HTTP_PATH, UC_CATALOG.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\n\nimport pendulum\nfrom _harness import load_to_uc, read_feed, run_uc_sql\nfrom airflow import DAG\nfrom airflow.operators.python import PythonOperator\n\nCATALOG = os.environ.get(\"UC_CATALOG\", \"dataq_retail\")\n\n\ndef _bronze(**_: object) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Load the raw NDJSON bronze sources into UC raw.* (schema-on-read).\"\"\"\n    for feed in (\"sales_events\", \"feedback\"):\n        df = read_feed(f\"databricks_medallion/bronze/{feed}\", \"json\")\n        if not df.empty:\n            load_to_uc(df, CATALOG, \"raw\", feed)\n\n\ndef _silver(**_: object) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Clean + PII-redact (sha2 the feedback email — #226); dedup; project sales.\"\"\"\n    run_uc_sql(\n        [\n            f\"\"\"CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE `{CATALOG}`.`silver`.`feedback` AS\n                SELECT feedback_id, customer_id, channel, rating, comment,\n                       sha2(CAST(email AS STRING), 256) AS email, created_ts\n                FROM `{CATALOG}`.`raw`.`feedback`\n                QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY feedback_id ORDER BY created_ts) = 1\"\"\",\n            f\"\"\"CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE `{CATALOG}`.`silver`.`sales` AS\n                SELECT order_number, channel, store_id,\n                       CAST(amount AS DOUBLE) AS amount,\n                       to_date(event_ts) AS sale_date\n                FROM `{CATALOG}`.`raw`.`sales_events`\n                WHERE event_type = 'placed'\"\"\",\n        ]\n    )\n\n\ndef _gold(**_: object) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Daily revenue rollup — reconciles back to Snowflake order_total (ADR 0014).\"\"\"\n    run_uc_sql(\n        [\n            f\"\"\"CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE `{CATALOG}`.`gold`.`daily_revenue` AS\n                SELECT sale_date, channel,\n                       SUM(amount) AS daily_revenue,\n                       COUNT(DISTINCT order_number) AS orders\n                FROM `{CATALOG}`.`silver`.`sales`\n                GROUP BY sale_date, channel\"\"\",\n        ]\n    )\n\n\nwith DAG(\n    default_args={\n        # Retry transient failures (serverless warehouse cold start) with backoff.\n        \"retries\": 4,\n        \"retry_delay\": pendulum.duration(seconds=30),\n        \"retry_exponential_backoff\": True,\n        \"max_retry_delay\": pendulum.duration(minutes=5),\n    },\n    dag_id=\"flow_b_medallion\",\n    description=\"DataQ harness Flow B — UC bronze->silver->gold medallion (SQL warehouse)\",\n    schedule=\"0 2 * * *\",  # after the Flow A loads\n    start_date=pendulum.datetime(2026, 6, 1, tz=\"UTC\"),\n    catchup=False,\n    tags=[\"dataq-harness\", \"flow-b\", \"medallion\"],\n):\n    bronze = PythonOperator(task_id=\"bronze_raw_load\", python_callable=_bronze)\n    silver = PythonOperator(task_id=\"silver_clean_pii\", python_callable=_silver)\n    gold = PythonOperator(task_id=\"gold_daily_revenue\", python_callable=_gold)\n    bronze >> silver >> gold\n"
}

> AGENT

**Confirmed:** the 540-row `executemany` timed out after 3+ min — databricks-sql `executemany` does row-by-row INSERTs (one round-trip each). Small reference tables work; large ones (date_dim 540, exchange_rates 450, medallion sales_events 2400) don't. Fix: **chunked multi-row INSERT** (one round-trip per ~200 rows). Let me rewrite `load_to_uc`:

{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ-harness/airflow/dags/_harness.py",
  "old_string": "    try:\n        cur = conn.cursor()\n        cur.execute(f\"CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE {full} ({cols})\")\n        if rows:\n            placeholders = \", \".join([\"?\"] * len(df.columns))\n            cur.executemany(f\"INSERT INTO {full} VALUES ({placeholders})\", rows)\n        return len(rows)\n    finally:\n        conn.close()",
  "new_string": "    try:\n        cur = conn.cursor()\n        cur.execute(f\"CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE {full} ({cols})\")\n        # Chunked multi-row INSERT: databricks-sql executemany is row-by-row (one\n        # round-trip per row → minutes for 100s of rows). One execute per ~200-row\n        # batch keeps even the 2.4k-row bronze loads to a handful of round-trips.\n        if rows:\n            one = \"(\" + \", \".join([\"?\"] * len(df.columns)) + \")\"\n            batch = 200\n            for i in range(0, len(rows), batch):\n                chunk = rows[i : i + batch]\n                values = \", \".join([one] * len(chunk))\n                flat = [v for row in chunk for v in row]\n                cur.execute(f\"INSERT INTO {full} VALUES {values}\", flat)\n        return len(rows)\n    finally:\n        conn.close()"

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ-harness/README.md",
  "content": "# DataQ harness — live test/demo-data environment\n\nExternal, **not-git-tracked** companion to DataQ (ADR 0021). Stands up a real retail\ndata environment in Azure + Snowflake + Databricks that exercises every DataQ run path\nand both orchestration providers end-to-end, so the standing *\"deferred live\nwarehouse/file run smoke\"* can be discharged.\n\n> Secrets live only in `secrets.sh` (chmod 600, never committed) and Terraform state\n> (gitignored). Tracker: `../DataQ/HARNESS_TODO.md`.\n\n---\n\n## What's deployed\n\n```\n                         Azure (RG: dataq-rg)\n  ADLS Gen2 (landing/raw) ── source-of-truth landing zone\n        ▲  writes                         reads ▼\n  Container Apps Environment (westus2)            Snowflake (AWS) — DATAQ_DB.RETAIL\n   • mockdata cron Jobs (orders/tracking/             (12 tables; DATAQ_LOADER writes,\n     inventory/feedback/supply) → ADLS                 DATAQ_READER reads)\n   • Airflow: scheduler+webserver, CeleryExecutor   Databricks (AWS) — UC dataq_retail\n   • Airflow Celery workers (scalable, 2 replicas)     reference / raw / silver / gold\n   • Redis (Celery broker, internal TCP)              (serverless SQL warehouse)\n   • ACR (images)                                   ADF (dataq-harness-adf)\n  Postgres Flexible Server (westus3) — Airflow metadata   • event + timer pipelines\n```\n\n## Orchestration matrix (both providers × both trigger modalities)\n\n| | Event-driven | Timer / schedule |\n|---|---|---|\n| **ADF** | `pl_flow_a_orders` (blob-event trigger) → Snowflake `ORDERS_HEADER` | `pl_flow_a_customers` (schedule trigger) → Snowflake `CUSTOMERS` |\n| **Airflow** | `flow_a_payments_event` (ADLS file-sensor) → Snowflake `PAYMENTS` | `flow_a_snowflake_load` (9 feeds) + `flow_a_uc_reference` (8 dims) + `flow_b_medallion` (bronze→silver→gold) |\n\n**Decoupled from DataQ by design:** orchestrators run *pure ETL* — no push to DataQ.\nDataQ (one of several possible monitors) discovers runs by **polling** the ADF/Airflow\nREST APIs (ADR 0006/0007). No `NotifyDataQ` web activity; no Airflow callback.\n\n## Data model — 24 datasets / route map\nSee `mockdata/README.md`. Retail core (products, customers, orders header+lines,\npayments, refunds, returns) + extended domain (settlements, purchase_orders+suppliers,\norder_fulfillment+fulfillment_nodes, categories, date_dim, exchange_rates, discounts,\ncancellations) + medallion sources (sales_events, feedback) + flat-files (tracking,\ninventory). 18 deliberate DQ issues seeded for DataQ to catch (`_dq_issues_manifest.json`).\n\n## Security / least-privilege\n- **Snowflake:** `DATAQ_LOADER` (CREATE TABLE + write DML — ETL) vs `DATAQ_READER`\n  (USAGE + SELECT — DataQ). Same user, role-switched. PII (`customers.email/phone`).\n- **Databricks/UC:** loads run as the admin PAT (catalog owner); silver hashes the\n  feedback email (#226). *Read/write split TODO:* a true least-priv read needs a\n  **separate service principal** with SELECT-only grants (UC grants are per-principal,\n  and the harness has one PAT) — recommended but not yet implemented; Snowflake is the\n  reference pattern.\n- Auth posture: key-based throughout (account keys / SAS / PAT) — accepted for a\n  disposable harness; the Contributor SP can't create the role assignments that\n  managed-identity/RBAC would need.\n\n---\n\n## Operational runbook\n\n```bash\ncd ~/Coding/Python/DataQ-harness && source secrets.sh        # exports ARM_*/SNOWFLAKE_*/DATABRICKS_*\ncd terraform\nexport TF_VAR_snowflake_password=\"$SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD\" \\\n       TF_VAR_databricks_token=\"$DATABRICKS_TOKEN\" \\\n       TF_VAR_databricks_host=\"$DATABRICKS_HOST\" \\\n       TF_VAR_databricks_http_path=\"/sql/1.0/warehouses/<warehouse-id>\"\nterraform apply\n```\n\n**Build/push images (ACR Tasks are disabled on this sub — build locally):**\n```bash\naz acr login --name <acr>\n# mockdata (latest is fine — Jobs pull fresh each run)\ndocker build --platform linux/amd64 -t <acr>.azurecr.io/mockdata:latest -f Dockerfile . && docker push ...\n# airflow — ALWAYS use an immutable tag + bump variables.tf airflow_image_tag (see gotchas)\nTAG=v$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M)\ndocker build --platform linux/amd64 -f airflow/Dockerfile -t <acr>.azurecr.io/airflow-dataq:$TAG . && docker push ...\n```\n\n**Seed + run a complete flow:**\n```bash\nCS=$(az storage account show-connection-string -g dataq-rg -n <adls> --query connectionString -o tsv)\ndocker run --rm -e AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING=\"$CS\" <acr>.azurecr.io/mockdata:latest \\\n  backfill --tier S --seed 42 --out adls://<adls>/landing            # all 24 datasets → ADLS\n# Trigger ADF: az datafactory pipeline create-run --name pl_flow_a_{orders,customers}\n# Trigger Airflow: POST {airflow_url}/api/v1/dags/<dag>/dagRuns (basic auth; admin pw = terraform output -raw airflow_admin_password)\n```\n\n**Clean slate:** drop SF `RETAIL` tables (truncate the TF-managed `ORDERS_HEADER`/`CUSTOMERS`)\n+ drop UC tables; `terraform apply -replace=azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server_database.airflow\n-replace=azurerm_container_app.airflow` (fresh Airflow metadata); delete ADLS `landing/*`\ndata dirs; then backfill + re-trigger. **ADF run history can't be purged** (Azure retains\n~45 days — no API).\n\n**Teardown:** `terraform destroy` (the UI-created+imported UC catalog is destroyed too).\n\n---\n\n## Hard-won gotchas (the chain of root-causes — read before debugging)\n\nEach only surfaced at apply/runtime against the live services:\n\n1. **Azure RP registration** — the Contributor SP *could* self-register the 7 RPs after all.\n2. **Postgres Flexible Server is offer-restricted in westus2** for this subscription\n   (`LocationIsOfferRestricted`). Probe: `az postgres flexible-server list-skus -l <region>`\n   (restricted region returns ~empty). Centralus worked but its **~30-40 ms cross-region\n   latency starved the Airflow scheduler's executor loop** → moved to **westus3** (adjacent\n   to westus2). A failed create also leaves a hidden name reservation that 409s reuse →\n   rename on region change.\n3. **ACR Tasks disabled on the sub** (`TasksOperationsNotAllowed`) → build images **locally**\n   (`docker build --platform linux/amd64`), not `az acr build`.\n4. **Container Apps caches `:latest` at the node** — a same-tag rebuild is NOT re-pulled on\n   a new revision. **Use immutable tags** for the airflow image; bump `airflow_image_tag`.\n5. **UC catalog can't be created via API/Terraform** on a default-storage-only metastore\n   (\"Metastore storage root URL does not exist\"). Create it once in the **UI** (Default\n   Storage) → `terraform import` with `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [storage_root] }`.\n6. **ADF legacy Snowflake linked service is rejected** (\"version not supported\") → use the\n   **SnowflakeV2** connector (`azurerm_data_factory_linked_custom_service` + custom dataset\n   + `SnowflakeV2Sink`). Snowflake **staged copy needs SAS** auth (not account key) and the\n   delimited source needs an explicit `row_delimiter` + a `wildcardFileName` (folder glob).\n   Snowflake V2 `autoCreate` needs connector v1.1, so **pre-create** the ADF-loaded tables.\n   ADF pipelines carry `ignore_changes=[activities_json]` (ADF normalizes it → perpetual diff).\n7. **LocalExecutor can't run the loads** on Container Apps Consumption: the scheduler is\n   multi-threaded → `fork()` deadlocks task workers (set\n   `AIRFLOW__CORE__EXECUTE_TASKS_NEW_PYTHON_INTERPRETER=True`), and a replica is capped at\n   **2 vCPU / 4 GiB total**. → **CeleryExecutor** with a Redis broker + a separate,\n   horizontally-scalable **worker container app**.\n8. **Celery broker unreachable at the `.internal.` FQDN** over Container Apps internal TCP\n   → use the **short app name** (`redis://dataq-harness-redis:6379/0`).\n9. **No retry logic** → cold serverless-SQL-warehouse / job-cluster starts failed tasks\n   immediately. Added DAG `default_args` retries (4×, exponential backoff 30 s→5 min).\n10. **pyarrow version skew** — mockdata wrote Parquet with pyarrow 24, the airflow image\n    read with 19 → `OSError: Repetition level histogram size mismatch`. **Pin both to the\n    same version** (19; it has py3.13 wheels for mockdata) and regenerate the Parquet.\n11. **`databricks-sql` `executemany` is row-by-row** (one round-trip/row → 540 rows timed\n    out >3 min) → **chunked multi-row INSERT** (~200 rows/statement; 540 rows in ~7 s).\n12. **Airflow task logs aren't remotely readable** (worker replica hostnames don't resolve\n    for the log server; no remote logging). To debug a worker-only failure, dump the\n    traceback to ADLS from inside the task, or reproduce the exact code path locally.\n\n### Notes / known limitations\n- `ORDERS_HEADER` can double-load: the ADF blob-event trigger auto-fires on the backfill\n  file *and* a manual `create-run`, and the Copy **appends** (no pre-copy truncate). Add a\n  truncate step if exact counts matter.\n- These same Container Apps gotchas (#3,#4,#7,#8) will apply to **DataQ's own Azure deploy**.\n"
}

All done. Here's the wrap-up.

## ✅ Flow B + cleanup + end-to-end run — complete

**Flow B medallion** now works (rewrote it to the serverless SQL warehouse + chunked inserts, since the trial workspace's reliable compute is serverless): UC `raw` (sales_events, feedback) → `silver` (cleaned, **feedback email SHA-256 hashed**, #226) → `gold.daily_revenue`.

**Full clean-slate run** (exactly as you asked — wiped everything, then ran the complete flow):
- Dropped all Snowflake `RETAIL` + UC tables; recreated the Airflow **metadata DB** (clears all Airflow + postgres run history); cleared the ADLS landing zone.
- Regenerated 24 datasets → triggered every flow → verified fresh:
  - **Snowflake `RETAIL`: 12 tables** (ADF event/timer + Airflow event + Celery schedule, incl. all new domain entities)
  - **UC `dataq_retail`: reference (8) + raw (2) + silver (2) + gold (1)**
- **Final `terraform plan`: "No changes."**

*One caveat I noted:* ADF run history **can't be purged** (Azure retains ~45 days, no API) — and `ORDERS_HEADER` can double-load because the blob-event trigger auto-fires *and* a manual run both append (no pre-copy truncate). Both documented.

## Databricks read/write split
The **Snowflake** split is implemented (`DATAQ_LOADER` writes / `DATAQ_READER` reads). For **Databricks/UC**, a true split needs a *separate service principal* with SELECT-only grants (UC grants are per-principal and the harness has one admin PAT) — I documented it as the recommended next step rather than spin up another principal/OAuth path. Silver-layer PII hashing is in place either way.

## Documentation — yes, and done
This was worth capturing. I wrote **`README.md` at the harness root** with:
- Architecture diagram + the 2×2 orchestration matrix + data-model/route map
- Security/roles, an **operational runbook** (deploy, immutable-tag image rebuilds, seed+run, clean-slate, teardown)
- **The full chain of 12 hard-won infra gotchas** — Postgres offer-restriction→westus3, `:latest` node caching→immutable tags, LocalExecutor fork-deadlock + 2-vCPU cap→CeleryExecutor+workers, broker short-name, UC-catalog-via-UI+import, ADF V1→V2 + SAS staging + pre-created tables, no-retries→backoff, **pyarrow 24↔19 skew**, `databricks-sql executemany`→chunked insert, unreadable worker logs.

I also flagged in the README that **gotchas #3/#4/#7/#8 will hit DataQ's own Azure deploy** — so that documentation pays off twice. Added a "HARNESS IS LIVE" status banner to `HARNESS_TODO.md` pointing at it.

The only thing now standing between this and discharging the deferred "live warehouse/file smoke" is **DataQ itself running in the cloud** to execute checks against all this data (the separate deploy track).

> AGENT

Measured from the actual run records (not estimates). **Generation itself is negligible** — a full 24-dataset backfill is **0.68s**, a single tick **0.37s** (ADLS upload adds a few seconds of network). So the turnaround is essentially the **load** step. Here's each path:

| Path | Final table(s) | Load turnaround (avg) | Range (n runs) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **ADF timer** | `CUSTOMERS` | **~53s** | 53s (1) |
| **ADF event** | `ORDERS_HEADER` | **~83s** | 52–127s (3) |
| **Airflow Flow B** | UC raw→silver→gold | **~81s** | 81s (1) |
| **Airflow schedule (Snowflake)** | 9 feeds | **~114s** | 68–160s (2) |
| **Airflow event** | `PAYMENTS` | **~283s** | 32–708s (6) |
| **Airflow schedule (UC reference)** | 8 dims | **~1004s** | 688–1320s (2) |

## The big caveat: these are dominated by cold-starts, not data volume

Small samples with huge variance, because the latency is mostly **cold-start tax**, not the ~17k rows:

- **UC reference (~17 min!)** is the outlier — almost entirely **serverless SQL-warehouse cold-start + retry backoff** (30s→5min exponential). Warm, the chunked inserts are ~7–30s/table — I measured date_dim (540 rows) at **7.1s warm**. So warm steady-state for all 8 ≈ **1–2 min**, not 17.
- **Airflow event (payments)** floor is the **120s sensor poke interval**; the 32s low = files already present on first poke, the 708s high = cold-start + extra poke cycles.
- **Airflow schedule (Snowflake)** ~114s = 9 Celery tasks, each **cold-starts a fresh Python interpreter** (~10–15s, the fork-deadlock fix) before `write_pandas`, parallelized across 2 workers × 3 concurrency.
- **ADF (~53–83s)** is the most *consistent* — managed Copy + blob-event-grid latency (event→pipeline start is typically <1 min) + SAS-staged load.

## Takeaways
1. **Generation → landing: ~1–5s** (negligible).
2. **Load latency ≈ cold-start latency.** The serverless warehouse, Celery interpreter spawns, and the sensor poke interval set the floor — data volume (tier S) barely registers.
3. **Warm vs cold is night-and-day** — e.g. UC ~17 min cold (retry-waiting for warehouse) vs ~1–2 min warm. A keep-warm warehouse (auto-stop raised) + pre-warmed workers would collapse the averages.
4. **ADF is steadiest** (~1 min); **Airflow paths are spikier** (cold-start sensitive).

If you want true steady-state numbers, I'd run each path 3–5× back-to-back (warehouse + workers already warm) and re-measure — that's exactly what the §6 perf-scale task in `HARNESS_TODO.md` is for, and it'd ride this same tooling.

117	## 2a. Recurring cadence — incremental loads (the "source keeps producing" clock)
118	
119	> The §2 generator is **one-shot** (backfills N snapshots in a single run). Freshness/
120	> volume/anomaly monitors only mean something if data keeps *arriving* on a cadence.
121	> **Three clocks — do not conflate:** (1) **data-arrival** (source produces new data —
122	> NEW, this section); (2) **load+trigger** (ADF/Airflow picks up the file → triggers
123	> DataQ — §3); (3) **check-run** (DataQ's W5 `schedules` cron, or driven by clock 2).
124	>
125	> **Decisions (2026-06-26) — two layers, don't collapse them:**
126	> - **File creation (clock 1, source-system simulator) = Container Apps Job on a cron schedule.**
127	>   Runs the `mockdata` image (`tick → write files to ADLS landing zone`). Chosen over a
128	>   Function App (pandas/pyarrow is a heavy *batch*, not lightweight event glue — Functions
129	>   add packaging/cold-start friction) and over OS cron; reuses DataQ's Container Apps platform
130	>   + image, cron built in, pay-per-run. **This is *upstream* of the orchestrator** (source drops
131	>   files), which is cleaner/more realistic than the orchestrator also producing.
132	> - **Load + trigger (clock 2) = ADF/Airflow** load to Snowflake/UC → on-success trigger DataQ
133	>   (the path under test). **Deliberately mix two trigger modalities — not all event-driven:**
134	>     - **Event / file-landing** (ADF Storage-Event trigger / Airflow file-sensor or dataset DAG) —
135	>       fires when the Job drops a file. Use for high-frequency/latency-sensitive feeds (e.g. orders).
136	>     - **Schedule / time** (ADF Schedule or tumbling-window trigger / Airflow cron `schedule`) —
137	>       fires on a clock, processes whatever landed in the window. Use for daily/batch feeds
138	>       (e.g. inventory, feedback). **Set the load schedule to fire *after* the file-creation Job**
139	>       (e.g. Job drops inventory 01:00 → scheduled load 01:15) so there's data to pick up.
140	>     - _Why both:_ exercises both ADF/Airflow trigger types **and** DataQ's pipeline-run monitoring +
141	>       10-min polling / gap-recovery fallback (the poll only meaningfully bites on scheduled pipelines).
142	>   Flow C (flat-file in place) has no load step — the Job's file drop *is* the arrival; DataQ reads
143	>   in place (its own W5 schedule or arrival event).
144	>   Proposed split (adjustable): **orders → event**, **tracking → event**, **inventory → schedule**,
145	>   **feedback → schedule** — one event + one schedule per warehouse target (Snowflake & UC) for parity.
146	> - **Required by the Job runtime:** Container Apps Jobs are **ephemeral** → the generator's
147	>   state must move off local disk to **blob** (ADLS). `state.py` needs a pluggable backend
148	>   (local FS today; ADLS blob for the Job). See work items below.
149

(`mockdata/increment.py` + `state.py`)
